data.description: A 57-year-old female without any medical history was admitted for evaluation of a left ventricular tumor that was discovered incidentally. The patient was asymptomatic and had no relevant past medical history. Physical examination findings were not specifically described in the case report.

A rare benign primary cardiac tumor composed predominantly of fibroblasts and dense collagen. It usually arises within the ventricular myocardium, particularly the left ventricle, and may be discovered incidentally.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging appearance of a well-defined intramyocardial ventricular tumor with fibrous characteristics
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpitations or ventricular arrhythmias
No chest pain
No dyspnea or heart-failure symptoms
No syncope

data.description: A benign vascular cardiac tumor composed of proliferating blood vessels. It can occur in any cardiac chamber or myocardial wall and is sometimes detected incidentally.
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpitations or arrhythmia
No chest pain
No dyspnea
Imaging and histologic appearance dominated by dense fibrous tissue rather than a predominantly vascular mass

data.description: A benign tumor of mature adipose tissue that may arise in the myocardium, subendocardium, or pericardium. Many cardiac lipomas are asymptomatic and found incidentally.
symptoms_not_in_common: Left ventricular intramyocardial lesion with fibrous rather than fatty imaging characteristics
No evidence of fat-rich tissue on the described imaging
No compressive symptoms, arrhythmia, or heart-failure symptoms

data.description: The most common benign primary cardiac tumor, usually arising from the interatrial septum in the left atrium. It may cause obstructive, embolic, or constitutional symptoms, although occasional cases are incidental.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac tumor may occasionally be asymptomatic
symptoms_not_in_common: Left ventricular rather than typical left atrial location
No dyspnea, syncope, or positional symptoms
No embolic manifestations
No fever, weight loss, or other constitutional symptoms

data.description: A rare malignant primary cardiac tumor, such as undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, or angiosarcoma. These tumors often invade adjacent myocardium and commonly produce progressive cardiac symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Left ventricular involvement is possible, though uncommon
Early disease can occasionally be incidentally identified
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as weight loss or fatigue
No chest pain
No dyspnea or heart-failure symptoms
No evidence provided of invasive growth, metastases, or malignant clinical behavior

data.description: A previously healthy 10-year-old boy presented with left upper quadrant abdominal pain that worsened with deep breathing or lying down, accompanied by fever. He also complained of mild cough and whitish sputum. On physical examination, the child was irritable but there were no other remarkable findings. Laboratory data showed elevated C-reactive protein (8.65 mg/dL) without leukocytosis and other findings were unremarkable.
Ischemic injury of splenic tissue caused by impaired blood supply, often appearing as peripheral wedge-shaped, poorly perfused splenic lesions on ultrasound or MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Acute left upper quadrant abdominal pain
Imaging appearance of focal peripheral splenic lesions with reduced perfusion
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild cough
Whitish sputum

data.description: A localized bacterial or fungal infection within the spleen that can cause fever, left upper quadrant pain, and focal splenic lesions on imaging.
symptoms_not_in_common: No leukocytosis
Mild cough with whitish sputum
No remarkable abdominal examination findings

data.diagnosis: Splenic vein thrombosis with secondary splenic infarction
data.description: Thrombosis of the splenic venous circulation can impair splenic blood flow and may produce splenic congestion or infarction; MRI may demonstrate abnormal vascular signal near the splenic hilum.
symptoms_in_common: Focal splenic perfusion abnormalities on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild cough
Whitish sputum
No known pancreatitis, abdominal trauma, hypercoagulable disorder, or portal hypertension

data.diagnosis: Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection with extrapulmonary splenic infarction
data.description: Mycoplasma pneumoniae commonly causes an atypical respiratory infection and can rarely trigger thrombosis or splenic infarction through inflammation or transient antiphospholipid antibodies.
symptoms_in_common: Possible thrombotic splenic complication causing left upper quadrant pain
symptoms_not_in_common: No prominent respiratory distress
No reported chest imaging evidence of pneumonia
No leukocytosis

data.description: Usually caused by Epstein-Barr virus, infectious mononucleosis can cause fever and splenic enlargement or, rarely, splenic infarction due to transient hypercoagulability.
symptoms_in_common: Left upper quadrant pain suggesting splenic involvement
Possible splenic vascular or infarct-like lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No sore throat
No cervical lymphadenopathy
No reported splenomegaly on examination
No leukocytosis or atypical lymphocytosis
Mild cough with sputum is not typical

data.description: A 38-year-old woman presented with a three-day history of fever, generalized myalgia and arthralgia, and the sensation of difficulty when breathing in. She had poorly localized discomfort in the left diaphragmatic region on deep inspiration and loose stools over the preceding three days. Three days before presentation she had returned from a three-week trip to Western Australia, and 18 months earlier she had traveled to Vietnam. On examination she appeared well but was febrile at 38.0°C and tachypnoeic at 22 breaths/min, with all other observations normal. Examination of all other systems was unremarkable. Blood tests showed severe neutrophilia (18.9 × 10⁹/L; reference range 2.0-8.1), raised C reactive protein (354 mg/L; reference value <10), and normal renal and liver biochemistry. Chest radiography and urinalysis were normal. Blood cultures taken at presentation were negative.
An extraintestinal complication of amoebiasis in which Entamoeba histolytica forms a hepatic abscess, often months to years after travel to an endemic region.
symptoms_in_common: Marked neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein
Left upper abdominal/diaphragmatic discomfort worsened by deep inspiration
Hepatic lesion on CT compatible with an abscess
Previous travel to Vietnam, where amoebiasis is endemic
symptoms_not_in_common: No focal right-upper-quadrant abdominal pain
Normal liver biochemistry
Recent travel to Western Australia is not a typical exposure for amoebiasis

data.description: A localized bacterial infection of the liver, commonly caused by enteric organisms and associated with fever, inflammatory-marker elevation, and a low-attenuation liver lesion on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Loose stools suggesting a possible gastrointestinal source
CT evidence of a focal hepatic lesion compatible with abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: No jaundice
Normal liver biochemistry
Blood cultures were negative
No significant focal abdominal tenderness or systemic toxicity on examination

data.diagnosis: Melioidosis with hepatic abscess (Burkholderia pseudomallei infection)
data.description: Melioidosis is an infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, endemic in northern Australia and parts of Southeast Asia; it can cause pneumonia, sepsis, and abscesses in the liver and spleen.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel to Australia and previous travel to Southeast Asia
High neutrophil count and C-reactive protein
symptoms_not_in_common: Travel was to Western Australia rather than the more strongly endemic tropical northern regions
Chest radiograph was normal
No diabetes, chronic kidney disease, hazardous alcohol use, or other stated predisposing condition
Blood cultures were negative

data.diagnosis: Hepatic fascioliasis (Fasciola hepatica or Fasciola gigantica infection)
data.description: A liver fluke infection acquired from contaminated water or aquatic vegetation; the acute migratory phase may cause fever, abdominal discomfort, and focal hepatic lesions.
symptoms_in_common: History of travel to regions where food- and water-borne parasitic infections can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No eosinophilia was reported; severe neutrophilia is more prominent
Very high C-reactive protein is more suggestive of bacterial abscess
No reported ingestion of raw aquatic plants or untreated water
Loose stools are nonspecific and not a prominent typical feature

data.diagnosis: Septic portal vein thrombophlebitis (pylephlebitis) associated with intra-abdominal infection
data.description: Pylephlebitis is infected thrombosis of the portal venous system, usually arising from gastrointestinal infection such as diverticulitis, appendicitis, or colitis; it may coexist with hepatic abscesses.
symptoms_in_common: Marked neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein
Loose stools suggesting a gastrointestinal infectious source
Possible hepatic inflammatory lesion on CT
Imaging appearance may include portal venous branch abnormality adjacent to hepatic inflammatory change
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear abdominal source such as appendicitis or diverticulitis was described
No focal lower abdominal pain
Blood cultures were negative
Normal liver biochemistry

data.description: A 60-year-old white Caucasian woman presented with a 4-year history of worsening gait and sensory disturbance accompanied by urinary urgency and nocturia. She reported slow deterioration in vision from age 50, though she could still drive. Her mother was registered blind and had Parkinson's disease with dementia. On examination, she had a spastic gait with normal power in lower limbs but increased tone and sustained ankle clonus. Reflexes were brisk with flexor plantar responses. She had mild reduction in visual acuity and dyschromatopsia, but no detectable visual field defect and preserved pupillary light reflexes. CSF analysis showed presence of oligoclonal bands. Routine hematological, biochemical and immunological blood tests were normal, including folate and vitamin B12. Anti-aquaporin 4 antibodies were negative in serum.

data.diagnosis: OPA1-related autosomal dominant optic atrophy plus syndrome
data.description: A mitochondrial disorder caused by pathogenic OPA1 variants, typically producing slowly progressive bilateral optic atrophy and sometimes additional neurologic features such as spastic paraplegia, ataxia, neuropathy, deafness, or cognitive symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive visual decline beginning in adulthood
Bilateral optic disc pallor/optic atrophy and retinal nerve fiber layer thinning on OCT
Family history of severe visual impairment in the mother
Urinary urgency and nocturia consistent with corticospinal tract involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF oligoclonal bands are not a typical defining feature
Maternal Parkinsonism with dementia is not a classic OPA1 presentation

data.diagnosis: Hereditary spastic paraplegia with optic atrophy, such as SPG7-related disease
data.description: Hereditary spastic paraplegias are genetic disorders characterized by progressive degeneration of corticospinal tracts, causing lower-limb spasticity and bladder dysfunction. Some complicated forms, including SPG7, can include optic atrophy and other neurologic features.
symptoms_in_common: Normal lower-limb strength despite increased tone
Brisk reflexes and sustained ankle clonus
Optic atrophy/retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
Family history suggestive of inherited neurologic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF oligoclonal bands are not typical of hereditary spastic paraplegia
Dyschromatopsia is less prominent in many hereditary spastic paraplegia subtypes
No reported ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, or cerebellar signs, which can accompany SPG7 disease

data.description: A chronic inflammatory and neurodegenerative central nervous system disease that can cause gradually progressive spastic paraparesis, sensory disturbance, bladder dysfunction, and optic pathway injury. Oligoclonal bands support intrathecal immune activity.
symptoms_in_common: Spastic gait with increased tone, brisk reflexes, and ankle clonus
Visual impairment and dyschromatopsia that may reflect optic nerve involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Very slowly progressive bilateral visual loss over approximately 10 years is less typical than a discrete episode of optic neuritis
Preserved pupillary light reflexes and absence of a visual field defect are less typical of clinically significant optic neuritis
The provided brain and spinal imaging does not show typical multifocal demyelinating lesions
Family history of blindness suggests a possible inherited optic neuropathy rather than multiple sclerosis

data.diagnosis: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy with an MS-like neurologic syndrome (Harding disease)
data.description: A mitochondrial DNA disorder in which hereditary optic neuropathy coexists with central nervous system demyelinating or MS-like manifestations. It is more often associated with maternally inherited visual loss and can include spasticity and bladder symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of blindness through the maternal line
Optic atrophy and retinal nerve fiber layer loss
Spastic gait and upper motor neuron signs
CSF oligoclonal bands can occur in an MS-like overlap syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy usually causes subacute, often severe central visual loss rather than mild gradual visual decline over many years
Typical onset is younger than age 50
The patient is female, whereas classic Leber hereditary optic neuropathy is more common in men
No central scotoma or marked visual field defect was detected

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory disorder affecting the optic nerves and spinal cord, often causing optic neuritis and myelitis with motor, sensory, and bladder dysfunction. It is commonly associated with aquaporin-4 antibodies, although seronegative cases occur.
symptoms_in_common: Visual impairment with color vision disturbance
Spastic gait and corticospinal tract signs
Potential optic nerve and spinal cord involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Anti-aquaporin 4 antibodies are negative
The visual loss is chronic and gradual rather than an acute or subacute optic neuritis attack
There is no reported longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesion
The imaging shown does not demonstrate typical inflammatory brain or spinal cord lesions
CSF oligoclonal bands are less typical than in multiple sclerosis

data.description: 14-year-old female with >2 months of generalized pruritus, scleral icterus, and petechiae/ecchymoses on the extremities. She denied fever, abdominal pain, and abdominal distension. Past history included amenorrhea, menstrual irregularities, and acne; she had taken Chinese herbal medicines for about 9 months. Exam showed clear consciousness, facial acne and pigmentation, mild scleral and mucocutaneous jaundice, soft non-tender abdomen, and no lower extremity edema.

An autosomal-recessive disorder of impaired copper excretion caused by ATP7B mutations, leading to copper accumulation in the liver, brain, cornea, and other tissues. The reported homozygous ATP7B c.2333G>T (p.Arg778Leu) pathogenic variant, Kayser-Fleischer-type corneal findings, and basal-ganglia MRI abnormalities strongly support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Petechiae and ecchymoses suggesting impaired hepatic synthetic function or thrombocytopenia
Basal ganglia abnormalities on brain MRI
Corneal copper deposition compatible with Kayser-Fleischer rings
symptoms_not_in_common: No described neurologic symptoms such as tremor, dystonia, dysarthria, or behavioral change
No abdominal pain or abdominal distension
No lower-extremity edema

data.description: Liver injury caused by medications, supplements, or herbal preparations. Chinese herbal medicines can cause hepatocellular, cholestatic, or mixed-pattern hepatitis and may produce jaundice and severe itching.
symptoms_in_common: History of Chinese herbal medicine use for approximately 9 months
Petechiae and ecchymoses that may occur with severe liver dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Basal ganglia MRI changes suggesting metal deposition
Corneal findings compatible with Kayser-Fleischer rings
Pathogenic homozygous ATP7B mutation
Menstrual irregularities and amenorrhea are not typical direct manifestations

data.description: A chronic immune-mediated inflammatory liver disease that commonly affects girls and young women and can present with jaundice, impaired liver function, and progression to cirrhosis if untreated.
symptoms_in_common: Petechiae and ecchymoses potentially related to hepatic dysfunction
Menstrual irregularities or amenorrhea can occur in chronic liver disease
Absence of fever and abdominal pain does not exclude the condition
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent generalized pruritus is less typical than in cholestatic disorders
Basal ganglia MRI abnormalities suggesting copper or metal deposition
Corneal copper-deposition findings
Pathogenic homozygous ATP7B mutation
History of prolonged herbal medicine exposure is not characteristic

data.description: A chronic cholestatic disease characterized by inflammatory fibrosis and stricturing of the bile ducts, causing impaired bile flow, itching, and jaundice. It is less common in young females and is often associated with inflammatory bowel disease.
symptoms_in_common: Possible bruising due to chronic cholestasis and impaired vitamin K absorption
No fever or abdominal pain can occur in chronic uncomplicated disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported inflammatory bowel disease symptoms
Basal ganglia MRI evidence of metal deposition is not typical
Corneal findings compatible with Kayser-Fleischer rings are not typical
Pathogenic homozygous ATP7B mutation is not associated with this disease
Amenorrhea and acne are not characteristic features

data.description: A group of inherited childhood and adolescent cholestatic liver diseases caused by defects in bile formation or transport. It typically presents with persistent pruritus, jaundice, and progressive liver injury.
symptoms_in_common: Petechiae and ecchymoses may occur in advanced cholestatic liver disease because of vitamin deficiencies or liver dysfunction
No fever, abdominal pain, or abdominal distension
symptoms_not_in_common: Basal ganglia MRI abnormalities suggesting copper deposition
Corneal findings compatible with Kayser-Fleischer rings
Pathogenic ATP7B mutation points to Wilson disease rather than PFIC
Facial acne and menstrual irregularities are not typical PFIC features
History of herbal medicine use is not a typical cause of PFIC

data.description: 66-year-old man with a 2-day history of fever, lethargy, polyarticular arthralgias, and a painful rash. Past history included hypertension, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, hypercholesterolemia, and biopsy-proven autoimmune hepatitis; azathioprine 75 mg had been started 10 days earlier. On examination, he was febrile (38°C) with bilateral tender knees and a patellar tap. Laboratory tests showed neutrophilic leukocytosis, elevated CRP and ESR, mildly elevated rheumatoid factor, and negative anti-CCP, dsDNA, ENA, and ASO tests; renal function and urinalysis were normal, chest radiograph was normal, and synovial fluid was noninflammatory with no bacteria or crystals.

data.diagnosis: Azathioprine-induced Sweet syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis)
data.description: A neutrophilic inflammatory skin disorder that may be triggered by medications, including azathioprine, and classically causes abrupt fever, neutrophilia, painful erythematous plaques or nodules, and arthralgia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Noninflammatory synovial fluid
Mildly positive rheumatoid factor

data.description: A potentially severe idiosyncratic systemic reaction to azathioprine, usually occurring within days to weeks of initiation, characterized by fever, malaise, rash, arthralgia, and inflammatory-marker elevation; it is not necessarily dose-related.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea
No renal impairment
No pulmonary findings or abnormal chest radiograph

data.description: A medication-associated immune reaction causing fever, rash, and symmetric joint pain or swelling, generally developing one to two weeks after exposure to a new drug.
symptoms_in_common: Timing shortly after a newly introduced medication
symptoms_not_in_common: Neutrophilic leukocytosis is less characteristic than in acute neutrophilic dermatosis
The rash appears as painful localized plaques rather than a typical diffuse urticarial eruption
No reported pruritus
No reported lymphadenopathy

data.description: Inflammation of small cutaneous blood vessels, often triggered by medications, which can produce palpable purpura or painful erythematous lesions and may be accompanied by fever and arthralgia.
symptoms_in_common: Recent exposure to a new medication
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal urinalysis and renal function, with no evidence of renal vasculitis
No reported palpable purpura predominantly on the lower legs
Neutrophilic leukocytosis is not a defining feature
No reported abdominal pain or neuropathy

data.description: A systemic autoinflammatory disorder that can cause high fever, inflammatory polyarthritis, neutrophilic leukocytosis, elevated inflammatory markers, and a transient salmon-colored rash.
symptoms_in_common: Negative anti-CCP, dsDNA, and ENA testing
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 66 years is atypical for disease onset
Rash is painful and plaque-like rather than typically evanescent salmon-pink
Fever is only 38°C rather than the usual high quotidian spiking fever
No reported sore throat
Synovial fluid is noninflammatory
Very close temporal association with starting azathioprine favors a drug reaction

data.description: A 60-year-old woman presented after sustaining direct trauma to the anterior neck from a fall. She developed progressively worsening hoarse voice, difficulty swallowing, and pain with neck movement. Physical examination revealed visible neck swelling with bruising tracking onto the anterior chest wall. There was no tenderness on palpation of the cervical spine. On flexible nasal endoscopy, swelling of the posterior pharyngeal wall was observed, indicating potential airway compromise.
Bleeding into the retropharyngeal/prevertebral soft tissues after neck trauma, causing expansion of the posterior pharyngeal wall and possible airway obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising extending onto the anterior chest wall
Posterior pharyngeal wall swelling on flexible endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: No cervical spine tenderness

data.diagnosis: Laryngeal trauma with laryngeal edema or hematoma
data.description: Blunt injury to the larynx can cause mucosal swelling, soft-tissue hematoma, vocal-cord dysfunction, and progressive upper-airway obstruction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Posterior pharyngeal wall swelling is more suggestive of a retropharyngeal process
Bruising tracking to the anterior chest wall is less specific for isolated laryngeal injury

data.description: A localized hematoma within or adjacent to the pharyngeal wall after blunt trauma can narrow the pharyngeal airway and produce dysphagia and voice change.
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive bruising over the neck and anterior chest wall may indicate deeper or more diffuse soft-tissue bleeding
Pain with neck movement is not a defining feature

data.diagnosis: Cervical spine injury with prevertebral soft-tissue swelling
data.description: Cervical vertebral fracture, ligamentous injury, or associated prevertebral hemorrhage after trauma may produce marked prevertebral swelling and dysphagia; absence of tenderness does not fully exclude injury.
symptoms_in_common: Potential airway compromise from soft-tissue swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: No cervical spine tenderness
Hoarse voice is less typical of an isolated cervical spine injury
Prominent external neck and chest bruising is less typical of isolated spine injury

data.description: A deep neck space infection causing a collection behind the pharynx, with posterior pharyngeal swelling, painful swallowing, neck stiffness, and risk of airway compromise.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute direct anterior neck trauma preceding symptoms
Visible bruising of the neck
Bruising tracking onto the anterior chest wall
Hoarse voice is less characteristic
No reported fever or infectious symptoms

data.description: 37-year-old man with 3 months of recurrent episodes of weakness, irritability, poor concentration, confusion/foggy sensorium, cold clammy feeling, fatigue, and unusual behavior/memory loss, often after several hours without eating and worse at night or early morning. He craved sweets, drank large amounts of cola for relief, and gained 13 kg. Past history included umbilical hernia repair and back surgery; no regular medications or substance use. On presentation he was confused, cold, and clammy, with otherwise unremarkable physical examination. Laboratory findings showed hypoglycemia (glucose 2.4 mmol/L) with elevated insulin and C-peptide, normal HbA1c, and a hypervascular 1.8 × 1.3 cm lesion in the pancreas on MRCP.

A pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that secretes insulin autonomously, causing recurrent fasting hypoglycemia. It is the most likely diagnosis given endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and a hypervascular pancreatic lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent episodes after several hours without eating
Symptoms worse at night or early morning
Craving sweets and symptomatic relief with cola
Elevated insulin and C-peptide during hypoglycemia

data.diagnosis: Factitious hypoglycemia from sulfonylurea or meglitinide exposure
data.description: Hypoglycemia caused by use of insulin-secretagogue diabetes medications, which increases endogenous insulin and C-peptide and can closely mimic insulinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Weight gain due to frequent carbohydrate intake
symptoms_not_in_common: No regular medication use reported
Hypervascular pancreatic lesion suggests a structural pancreatic cause
No known access to or use of diabetes medication

data.description: Diffuse pancreatic beta-cell hyperfunction causing excessive endogenous insulin secretion and recurrent hypoglycemia, usually without a discrete insulin-secreting tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated insulin and C-peptide during hypoglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: A discrete 1.8 cm hypervascular pancreatic lesion is more typical of insulinoma
Symptoms are mainly fasting-related rather than clearly postprandial
No history of bariatric or upper gastrointestinal surgery

data.description: A rare cause of hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia caused by insulin autoantibodies that bind and later release insulin, often associated with certain medications or autoimmune disease.
symptoms_in_common: Relief after consuming sugary drinks or food
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated C-peptide with a pancreatic mass favors insulinoma
No reported autoimmune disease
No reported exposure to common triggering medications or supplements
Predominantly fasting and nocturnal symptoms are less characteristic than variable or postprandial episodes

data.description: Insufficient cortisol production can impair glucose maintenance during fasting and cause fatigue, weakness, neurocognitive symptoms, and hypoglycemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated insulin and C-peptide are not typical
Hypervascular pancreatic lesion is not explained
Weight gain is less typical; weight loss is more common
No reported hypotension, hyperpigmentation, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or salt craving

data.description: A 39-year-old male, with no prior relevant medical history, presents with atraumatic intermittent sharp pain in the lower segment of the right anterior thoracic wall. The symptoms began two months earlier when the patient started exercising (CrossFit), mostly triggered by training (especially abdominal crunches) whilst being asymptomatic in normal daily activities.

Hypermobility or subluxation of the false-rib costal cartilage, most often involving ribs 8 to 10, causing intermittent pain from intercostal nerve irritation. The ultrasound appearance of abnormal relative position/motion of the lower ribs is supportive.
symptoms_in_common: Sharp intermittent pain in the lower anterior thoracic wall
Pain localized near the 8th and 9th rib region
Symptoms provoked by exercise and trunk movement
Pain especially triggered by abdominal crunches
Minimal or no symptoms during ordinary daily activities
symptoms_not_in_common: No clicking, popping, or palpable rib movement was reported
No radiation of pain around the chest or abdomen was reported

data.description: Overuse or minor tearing of an intercostal muscle caused by repetitive forceful trunk motion, heavy exercise, or twisting.
symptoms_in_common: Pain began after starting CrossFit training
Pain is provoked by abdominal exercise and muscular exertion
Absence of pain during normal low-demand daily activities
symptoms_not_in_common: Two months of intermittent focal symptoms may be longer than expected for a simple mild muscle strain
The apparent lower-rib alignment abnormality on ultrasound is not typical of an isolated intercostal muscle strain

data.description: Mechanical irritation or sprain at the junction between a rib and its cartilage, or between adjacent costal cartilages, often following repetitive loading or forceful trunk movement.
symptoms_in_common: Pain triggered by trunk flexion during abdominal crunches
symptoms_not_in_common: The lower false-rib location involving the 8th and 9th ribs is more characteristic of slipping rib syndrome than a typical costochondral sprain
No focal swelling, bruising, or persistent tenderness was reported

data.diagnosis: Rib stress fracture or stress reaction
data.description: A repetitive-loading injury of a rib that can occur with sudden increases in training intensity, producing localized pain that worsens with activity.
symptoms_in_common: Recent increase in physical training intensity
Focal sharp pain in the chest wall
symptoms_not_in_common: The pain is intermittent and absent during normal activities, whereas stress fractures often become progressively painful with daily movement or respiration
No reported focal bony tenderness, pain with breathing, or traumatic event
The ultrasound appearance suggests lower-rib mechanical instability rather than a definite cortical fracture

data.description: Pain caused by irritation or compression of an intercostal nerve, producing sharp, stabbing, or burning pain along the course of a rib. It can occur secondary to chest-wall movement or rib/cartilage instability.
symptoms_in_common: Pain in the distribution of lower anterior ribs
Symptoms may be triggered by movement that stretches or compresses the intercostal spaces
symptoms_not_in_common: No burning, tingling, numbness, or band-like radiation was reported
The close association with abdominal crunches and lower-rib ultrasound findings favors a mechanical rib disorder as the underlying cause

data.description: A 31-year-old woman underwent barium enema examination as part of a medical checkup. She had been healthy without specific complaints and had no significant past medical or family history. The patient was 161 cm in height and weighed 44 kg, appeared well, and the physical examination showed no abnormalities. Complete blood cell count and biochemical analysis of the blood for hepatic and renal function, urine analysis, and fecal occult blood test were all within normal limits. The tumor markers for CEA and CA 19-9 were also normal. No lesions were observed on the upper endoscopy and the abdominal ultrasound.

67-year-old previously healthy man with 4 months of dry cough, wheezing, and mild dyspnea, worsening despite inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids after being diagnosed elsewhere with eosinophilic asthma. No smoking history or significant past medical history. On examination, he required 1 L/min nasal cannula oxygen (SaO2 96%) and had decreased breath sounds with fine crackles in the right lower lung field; no JVP elevation, murmurs, gallop, or peripheral edema. Chest x-ray showed right-sided ground-glass opacities, and HRCT demonstrated ground-glass opacities with surrounding consolidation in the right lower lung field. Labs showed marked eosinophilia, elevated CRP, anemia, and mild hypoxemia.

data.diagnosis: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, not otherwise specified (CEL-NOS)
data.description: A clonal myeloid neoplasm characterized by persistent marked eosinophilia, dysplastic or immature eosinophil precursors, cytopenias, and possible organ infiltration, including pulmonary disease.
symptoms_in_common: Immature and dysplastic eosinophil-lineage cells on blood smear
Hypersegmented neutrophils and megaloblast-like cells suggesting marrow dysplasia
Abnormal cytogenetic findings involving chromosomes 1 and 7
Poor response to inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are clearly atypical; pulmonary eosinophilic infiltration can occur in CEL-NOS

data.description: An eosinophilic lung disease causing subacute respiratory symptoms, blood or bronchoalveolar eosinophilia, and peripheral pulmonary infiltrates; it usually responds promptly to systemic corticosteroids.
symptoms_not_in_common: Anemia
Dysplastic eosinophils and immature eosinophil precursors on smear
Megaloblast-like cells and irregular hypersegmented neutrophils
Abnormal cytogenetic findings involving chromosomes 1 and 7
Worsening despite corticosteroid treatment

data.description: A syndrome of sustained eosinophilia with eosinophil-mediated organ damage after secondary causes have been excluded; the lungs, heart, skin, nervous system, and gastrointestinal tract may be involved.
symptoms_not_in_common: Anemia
Dysplastic and immature eosinophil precursors
Megaloblast-like cells and abnormal neutrophil segmentation
Clonal-appearing chromosomal abnormality involving chromosomes 1 and 7
No reported cardiac, skin, neurologic, or gastrointestinal involvement

data.diagnosis: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene rearrangement
data.description: A group of clonal hematologic neoplasms driven by rearrangements involving genes such as PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, JAK2, or ABL1. They can cause marked eosinophilia, anemia, marrow abnormalities, and pulmonary or other organ infiltration.
symptoms_not_in_common: The specific molecular rearrangement has not been provided
No reported splenomegaly
No reported hepatomegaly
No reported constitutional symptoms such as fever, night sweats, or weight loss

data.description: A systemic eosinophilic vasculitis typically associated with adult-onset asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis, eosinophilia, transient pulmonary infiltrates, neuropathy, skin lesions, and possible renal or cardiac disease.
symptoms_in_common: Wheezing initially diagnosed as eosinophilic asthma
symptoms_not_in_common: No chronic sinusitis or nasal polyps
No neuropathy
No purpura or other skin manifestations
No renal involvement
No cardiac vasculitic findings
Anemia with dysplastic blood-smear features
Immature eosinophil precursors and chromosomal abnormalities are not typical of EGPA
Poor response to corticosteroid treatment

data.description: A 12-year-old boy presented with a 1-month history of malaise, fevers, abdominal pain, and worsening pallor. His symptoms began with headache and abdominal pain, with an initial temperature of 38.6°C and pale skin. He experienced persistent upper abdominal pain and recurrent fevers. The patient reported nausea, occasional diarrhea, headache, myalgias, fatigue, and occasional dizziness. He described nearly constant periumbilical pain radiating to the left lower quadrant, with occasional blood in stools. His height was 132 cm (1st percentile), weight 26.8 kg (1st percentile), with recent 1 kg weight loss. Physical examination revealed pale skin and mucosa, distended abdomen with mild tenderness in right upper and left lower quadrants, and ecchymoses on the shins. He had visited the Dominican Republic 3 months prior. Laboratory tests showed severe microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 6.7 g/dL), elevated inflammatory markers (ESR >140 mm/hr, CRP 143.2 mg/liter), and elevated ferritin (320 μg/L).

A rare non-Langerhans-cell histiocytic disorder characterized by accumulation of activated histiocytes in lymph nodes or extranodal organs. It can cause systemic inflammation, anemia, abdominal lymphadenopathy, and involvement of the kidneys or gastrointestinal tract.
symptoms_in_common: Possible multifocal lymph node and extranodal disease on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Occasional bloody stools
Prominent microcytic anemia suggesting iron deficiency
Recent travel to the Dominican Republic
Diarrhea

data.description: A rare histiocytic neoplasm driven by ALK gene rearrangements. Systemic disease in children may involve lymph nodes, bone marrow, kidneys, liver, lungs, and gastrointestinal organs and can produce fever, anemia, and inflammatory marker elevation.
symptoms_in_common: Possible renal and abdominal nodal abnormalities on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Bloody stools
Diarrhea
Travel-associated onset
Marked microcytosis as the dominant anemia pattern

data.diagnosis: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including anaplastic large-cell lymphoma
data.description: A malignant lymphoid disorder that may present in children with fever, weight loss, anemia, abdominal pain, mediastinal or abdominal lymphadenopathy, and extranodal organ involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Possible thoracic and abdominal lymphadenopathy on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea
Occasional blood in stools
Microcytic anemia, which is more suggestive of chronic blood loss or iron deficiency than marrow infiltration alone
Travel to the Dominican Republic

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any portion of the gastrointestinal tract, causing abdominal pain, diarrhea, gastrointestinal bleeding, growth failure, anemia, weight loss, and elevated inflammatory markers.
symptoms_in_common: Periumbilical pain radiating to the left lower quadrant
Short stature and poor weight gain
symptoms_not_in_common: Possible widespread thoracic and abdominal lymphadenopathy
Possible renal lesions on imaging
Ecchymoses
Recent travel as a potential exposure-related trigger

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection may cause prolonged fever, weight loss, anemia, abdominal pain, mesenteric lymphadenopathy, and involvement of multiple organs. Exposure risk can be increased by travel to regions where tuberculosis is more prevalent.
symptoms_in_common: Possible abdominal and thoracic lymphadenopathy on imaging
Recent travel to the Dominican Republic
symptoms_not_in_common: Occasional bloody stools
Severe microcytic anemia from apparent iron deficiency
Diarrhea as only an occasional symptom
Ecchymoses

diagnoses.name: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma
diagnoses.title: Mixed cellularity classical Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: 39-year-old man with 4 days of fever with shaking chills, diffuse headache, fatigue, and lower back pain after returning from a 2-week trip to East Africa (Tanzania). During travel he had mosquito bites and later developed nausea, vomiting, and nonbloody diarrhea. After return, he reported weakness, anorexia, decreased urine output with dark urine, and blurry vision during fever episodes. Past history: degenerative knee disease with prior glucocorticoid injections. On exam: temperature 38.9°C, facial flushing, mild scleral icterus, and dark brown urine.

Severe mosquito-borne malaria caused by P. falciparum, common in Tanzania and characterized by high fever, hemolysis, jaundice, renal dysfunction, and potentially high parasitemia. The rapid test and thin blood smear with multiple delicate ring forms, including appliqué forms, strongly support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Dark brown urine consistent with hemoglobinuria
Blood smear showing intraerythrocytic ring forms
symptoms_not_in_common: None; the presentation is highly characteristic of severe falciparum malaria

data.description: A severe hemolytic complication of falciparum malaria in which massive intravascular red-cell destruction causes hemoglobinuria, dark urine, jaundice, and acute kidney injury.
symptoms_in_common: Evidence of falciparum malaria on blood smear
symptoms_not_in_common: Nonbloody diarrhea
Blurry vision
Facial flushing

data.description: A zoonotic spirochetal infection acquired through exposure to water or soil contaminated with animal urine. Severe disease can cause fever, headache, gastrointestinal symptoms, jaundice, acute kidney injury, and dark urine.
symptoms_not_in_common: Mosquito-bite exposure as the primary epidemiologic clue
Blood smear showing intraerythrocytic malaria parasites
Typical malaria rapid-test positivity
Blurry vision occurring specifically during fever episodes

data.description: An Aedes mosquito-borne viral illness that can occur in East Africa and commonly causes abrupt fever, severe headache, fatigue, gastrointestinal symptoms, and occasionally hepatitis or plasma leakage.
symptoms_not_in_common: Dark brown urine suggesting hemoglobinuria
Decreased urine output with jaundice
Prominent shaking chills
Intraerythrocytic ring forms on peripheral blood smear
Malaria rapid-test positivity
Lower back pain as a major symptom

data.diagnosis: Acute viral hepatitis, including hepatitis A or E
data.description: Acute liver inflammation, often acquired during travel through contaminated food or water, that may cause fever, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, jaundice, dark urine, and fatigue.
symptoms_not_in_common: Shaking chills
Mosquito bites as a relevant exposure
Severe episodic febrile illness with blurry vision
Decreased urine output suggestive of renal involvement
Lower back pain
Peripheral smear with malaria ring forms
Malaria rapid-test positivity

data.description: 24-year-old male with quadriplegia from a car accident 5 years prior that required cervical spine stabilization with metal plates. Presented with dysphagia, odynophagia, neck pain, fever, and chills. Medical history significant for quadriplegia requiring cervical spine stabilization with metal plates. CT and MRI showed large paraspinal abscess extending from cervical spine 4 to thoracic spine 11.

data.diagnosis: Delayed pharyngoesophageal perforation from cervical spine hardware erosion
data.description: A late complication of anterior cervical spine fixation in which plates or screws erode into the pharynx or esophagus, causing a perforation, leakage, and deep infection.
symptoms_in_common: History of cervical spine stabilization with metal plates
Imaging evidence of a large cervical-to-thoracic paraspinal abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: Quadriplegia itself is not a symptom of the perforation
No respiratory distress or hematemesis was reported

data.description: A tear or hole in the esophagus permits saliva, bacteria, and food material to enter the mediastinum, producing severe infection and potentially extending into the neck and paraspinal tissues.
symptoms_in_common: Endoscopic/imaging findings consistent with communication to the mediastinum
Deep infection extending from the cervical region into the thoracic region
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain was specifically reported
No shortness of breath was reported
Quadriplegia is not typical of esophageal perforation

data.diagnosis: Infected cervical spinal instrumentation with cervical vertebral osteomyelitis
data.description: Infection involving cervical fixation hardware and adjacent vertebrae can cause osteomyelitis, soft-tissue infection, and formation of extensive paraspinal abscesses; it may also erode into the esophagus.
symptoms_in_common: Prior cervical spinal instrumentation with metal plates
Large paraspinal abscess extending from the cervical spine to T11
symptoms_not_in_common: Dysphagia and odynophagia are less typical unless there is associated anterior soft-tissue or esophageal involvement
Quadriplegia predates the current infectious presentation

data.diagnosis: Retropharyngeal abscess with extension to the mediastinum
data.description: A deep neck-space infection located behind the pharynx that may descend through fascial planes into the upper mediastinum and produce systemic infection.
symptoms_in_common: Cervical deep-space infection with possible mediastinal extension
symptoms_not_in_common: Extension of a paraspinal abscess down to thoracic spine level T11 is unusually extensive for an isolated retropharyngeal abscess
Prior cervical hardware strongly suggests an alternative source of infection
Quadriplegia is not typical

data.description: A severe, rapidly progressive mediastinal infection that spreads downward from an infection in the neck, pharynx, or esophagus and can produce purulent mediastinal collections.
symptoms_in_common: Evidence of pus or infection involving the mediastinum
Deep cervical infection extending into the thoracic region
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain was reported
No respiratory compromise or hemodynamic instability was reported
Quadriplegia and remote cervical hardware are not intrinsic features, although hardware-related esophageal injury could be the source

data.description: A 58-year-old male with worsening nausea for the past 72 hours presented to the emergency department with severe chest pain radiating to the back in the context of 4 recent episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious emesis. He was afebrile, diaphoretic, and mildly tachycardic. Cardiac workup, complete blood count, and electrolytes were normal.

A full-thickness tear of the esophagus caused by a sudden rise in intraesophageal pressure, classically after forceful vomiting. It can produce pneumomediastinum, pleural effusions or hydropneumothorax, and rapidly progressive mediastinitis.
symptoms_in_common: Severe chest pain radiating to the back
Repeated vomiting preceding onset of pain
Left-sided pleural fluid and associated lung-base opacity
symptoms_not_in_common: Afebrile presentation
Normal complete blood count

data.diagnosis: Acute mediastinitis secondary to esophageal perforation
data.description: Inflammation and infection of the mediastinum, commonly caused by leakage from an esophageal rupture. Early imaging may show mediastinal air, pleural fluid, and inflammatory changes before fever or leukocytosis develops.
symptoms_in_common: Pleural effusion, particularly on the left
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Normal complete blood count
Only 72 hours of symptoms without overt sepsis

data.description: A tear in the aortic intima that creates a false lumen within the aortic wall. It can cause abrupt severe chest pain radiating to the back and may be associated with sweating, nausea, and tachycardia.
symptoms_in_common: Severe chest pain radiating to the back
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple episodes of vomiting preceding the chest pain
Pneumomediastinum/subcutaneous emphysema on imaging
Left pleural fluid pattern suggestive of esophageal leakage
Normal cardiac workup does not specifically support dissection

data.description: Myocardial ischemia from reduced coronary blood flow, including unstable angina and myocardial infarction. It commonly presents with pressure-like chest pain, diaphoresis, nausea, and autonomic symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Chest pain radiating predominantly to the back
Repeated vomiting before symptom onset
Pneumomediastinum and pleural abnormalities on imaging
Normal cardiac workup

data.description: Air, with or without fluid, in the pleural space that can cause acute chest pain, dyspnea, tachycardia, and reduced lung expansion. In this setting, a left hydropneumothorax could occur as a complication of esophageal rupture.
symptoms_in_common: Left pleural fluid and adjacent lung-base opacity on imaging
Possible pleural air on chest imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeated vomiting as the precipitating event
Pneumomediastinum and cervical subcutaneous emphysema
Chest pain radiating to the back
Nausea for 72 hours before presentation

data.description: 27-year-old man with 2-year history of recurrent convulsive episodes. Initial events involved shaking of the trunk and limbs lasting 4-5 minutes, preceded by occipital pain radiating to the neck, blurred vision, palpitations, nausea, and difficulty concentrating. Four months before admission, he had an episode after alcohol intake with sudden stiffening, falling backward, generalized shaking for 5-8 minutes, and urinary incontinence. Despite levetiracetam, he continued to have seizures about weekly; one month before admission, he was found on the floor with shaking and clenching movements lasting about 2 minutes. On examination, he was awake and alert but mute, with a stiff posture and intermittent nonrhythmic tremulous movements of the trunk and limbs. He had extensive burn scars on the face, trunk, back, arms, and legs. Past history included febrile seizure in childhood, several concussions, asthma, major depressive disorder, chronic PTSD, and panic disorder with agoraphobia. Family history was notable for a mother with schizoaffective disorder and post-traumatic epilepsy. Labs were largely normal except for mildly elevated lactate and creatine kinase.

Paroxysmal episodes that resemble epileptic seizures but are caused by functional neurologic mechanisms rather than abnormal epileptic brain discharges. They are commonly associated with trauma-related and psychiatric conditions; the EEG image is compatible with prominent movement artifact without a clear evolving ictal epileptiform pattern.
symptoms_in_common: Long episode duration of 4 to 8 minutes
Mute state and stiff posture after or around events
History of chronic PTSD, major depressive disorder, panic disorder, and agoraphobia
History of extensive traumatic burn injuries
No clearly described focal neurologic deficit after events
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary incontinence during one event
Mildly elevated lactate and creatine kinase after convulsive activity
Childhood febrile seizure history
Multiple prior concussions

data.description: Epilepsy characterized by seizures with abrupt tonic stiffening followed by generalized rhythmic clonic shaking, often associated with loss of consciousness, falls, postictal confusion, muscle enzyme elevation, and occasionally urinary incontinence.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden stiffening followed by generalized shaking of the trunk and limbs
Falls to the floor or backward during episodes
Mild elevation of lactate and creatine kinase
symptoms_not_in_common: Episodes lasting 5 to 8 minutes repeatedly, which is longer than many generalized tonic-clonic seizures
Persistent weekly events despite antiseizure treatment
Intermittent nonrhythmic tremulous movements
Mute stiff posture without a clearly described typical postictal recovery period
EEG image without a clear generalized evolving epileptic ictal discharge

data.diagnosis: Post-traumatic focal epilepsy with focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizures
data.description: Epilepsy caused by prior brain injury, in which focal seizures may begin with sensory, autonomic, visual, cognitive, or emotional symptoms and then spread to cause bilateral tonic-clonic convulsions.
symptoms_in_common: Possible focal premonitory symptoms including occipital pain, blurred vision, nausea, palpitations, and difficulty concentrating
Progression from an apparent warning phase to stiffening and generalized shaking
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite focal neurologic deficits or structural brain lesion is provided
No clear stereotyped focal aura is established across all attacks
Nonrhythmic movements and mutism are not classic focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizure features
The EEG image does not clearly demonstrate a focal ictal onset

data.description: Transient loss of consciousness from temporary reduction in cerebral blood flow, sometimes accompanied by brief stiffening or myoclonic/convulsive movements. It may occur with arrhythmia, vasovagal triggers, dehydration, or substance use.
symptoms_in_common: Nausea and blurred vision that can occur as presyncopal symptoms
Sudden fall backward or being found on the floor
Brief shaking or clenching movements can occur during syncope
An event occurred after alcohol intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Convulsive activity lasting 4 to 8 minutes is longer than typical convulsive syncope
Recurrent weekly episodes over two years without a documented cardiovascular cause
Urinary incontinence is less typical, though possible
Stiff posture, mutism, and prolonged intermittent tremulous movements are not typical
No reported prodromal lightheadedness, diaphoresis, or rapid recovery

data.diagnosis: Panic attacks with functional motor manifestations
data.description: Panic attacks are abrupt episodes of intense fear and autonomic arousal; in some patients, especially those with functional neurologic symptoms, they may precede dissociative states, shaking, immobility, or seizure-like behavior.
symptoms_in_common: History of PTSD and major depressive disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized stiffening and prolonged whole-body shaking
Urinary incontinence
Falls with apparent loss of control
Mildly elevated lactate and creatine kinase after events
Recurrent convulsive episodes that closely mimic tonic-clonic seizures

data.description: 92-year-old woman with BMI 14.2 kg/m². Past history: no abdominal surgery, five children by normal vaginal delivery. Presenting with: 2-day history of sudden onset right knee pain, 1-day history of nausea and vomiting. Physical exam: no knee swelling/tenderness, patient frequently flexed right knee for pain relief, abdominal distension present, tenderness to deep palpation but no peritoneal irritation signs, no abdominal mass. Rectal exam revealed small extraluminal mass on right side. Initial abdominal radiograph showed small-bowel obstruction.

A pelvic hernia in which bowel protrudes through the obturator canal, classically occurring in thin, elderly, multiparous women. It can compress the obturator nerve and cause medial thigh or knee pain (Howship-Romberg sign).
symptoms_in_common: Right knee pain relieved by flexing the hip/knee
Right-sided extraluminal mass on rectal examination
CT appearance of bowel herniating through the right obturator region
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable groin mass
No peritoneal irritation signs

data.diagnosis: Femoral hernia with incarcerated small bowel
data.description: A hernia through the femoral canal below the inguinal ligament. It is more common in women and may incarcerate or strangulate bowel, causing acute intestinal obstruction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Right knee pain with relief on knee flexion
No palpable groin swelling or mass
Very low BMI and multiparity are more classically associated with obturator hernia
Right-sided extraluminal mass detected on rectal examination rather than a typical femoral-groin mass

data.description: A protrusion of abdominal contents through the inguinal canal that can trap small bowel and produce mechanical bowel obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Acute presentation compatible with bowel incarceration
symptoms_not_in_common: No groin or labial bulge was described
Right knee pain is not typical
Pain relieved by knee flexion is not typical
Elderly thin multiparous woman is more characteristic of obturator rather than inguinal hernia
Rectal examination finding of a deep right pelvic mass is atypical

data.description: A rare pelvic floor hernia in which bowel protrudes through the greater or lesser sciatic foramen. It may cause bowel obstruction and pelvic, buttock, hip, or leg pain from nerve compression.
symptoms_in_common: Deep pelvic mass may be detectable on rectal examination
Leg-region pain can occur from pelvic nerve irritation
symptoms_not_in_common: Knee pain relieved by flexing the knee is more characteristic of obturator nerve compression
No buttock mass or buttock pain was reported
No sciatic-type posterior thigh pain was reported
Patient characteristics strongly favor obturator hernia over this much rarer condition

data.diagnosis: Small-bowel obstruction due to pelvic malignancy or pelvic mass
data.description: A pelvic tumor, metastatic disease, or enlarged pelvic lymph node can externally compress or invade bowel, causing mechanical obstruction and a palpable pelvic mass.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided extraluminal pelvic mass on rectal examination
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden right knee pain is not typical
Pain relief with knee flexion is not typical
Abrupt onset over 1 to 2 days is less typical for malignancy-related obstruction
No abdominal mass was palpable
CT findings suggesting bowel herniation through the obturator region are not typical of a pelvic malignancy

data.description: 23-year-old Korean female with 1-day history of left eye visual disturbance and visual field defect, preceded by 6 months of recurrent bilateral visual field defects and headache that worsened 1 month before presentation. She later developed sudden left-sided hearing loss, then right eye visual field defect, tinnitus, severe headache, and arm numbness. She denied diabetes, hypertension, connective tissue disease, tuberculosis, hematologic disease, cardiovascular disease, oral contraceptive use, and pregnancy. On examination, pupils were reactive without relative afferent pupillary defect; visual acuity was 20/20 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye; intraocular pressure was 18 mmHg in both eyes; anterior segment examination was normal. Laboratory studies including lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin antibody, ESR, and CRP were normal. CSF showed mildly elevated protein (74.4 mg/dL) without oligoclonal bands, and no specific hematologic or rheumatologic abnormalities were found.
A rare autoimmune endotheliopathy affecting small vessels of the brain, retina, and inner ear, classically causing encephalopathy, branch retinal artery occlusions, and sensorineural hearing loss.
symptoms_in_common: Young woman with severe recurrent headache
Retinal arterial occlusion/ischemic retinal findings on fundus fluorescein angiography
Corpus callosum and periventricular brain lesions on MRI
Normal inflammatory markers and negative rheumatologic/thrombophilia testing
symptoms_not_in_common: Arm numbness is less characteristic than visual, auditory, cognitive, or balance symptoms
No overt encephalopathy, confusion, or cognitive decline was described

data.description: A chronic immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that commonly affects young women and can cause visual, sensory, and brainstem symptoms with white-matter lesions on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent neurologic symptoms over several months
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss is uncommon
Tinnitus is not a typical presenting feature
Retinal branch arterial occlusion/retinal ischemia is not typical of multiple sclerosis
No optic neuritis findings, relative afferent pupillary defect, or reduced color vision were described
No oligoclonal bands were found in CSF

data.description: An autoimmune hypercoagulable disorder causing arterial or venous thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity, and sometimes retinal or cerebral ischemic events.
symptoms_in_common: Visual field defects compatible with retinal ischemia
Focal neurologic symptom of arm numbness
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus are not typical core manifestations
Recurrent bilateral retinal artery involvement in this pattern is less typical
Lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin antibody testing were normal
No history of thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity, or systemic autoimmune disease
Corpus callosum lesions characteristic of Susac syndrome are not typical

data.description: A rare inflammatory disorder characterized primarily by ocular inflammation, especially interstitial keratitis, together with audiovestibular disease such as sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, and vertigo.
symptoms_not_in_common: Anterior segment examination was normal without interstitial keratitis
Retinal branch arterial occlusion is not the usual ocular manifestation
Corpus callosum and cerebral white-matter lesions are not typical
Arm numbness is not a usual feature
No vestibular symptoms such as vertigo or imbalance were reported

data.description: Neurologic involvement of Behcet disease, a systemic inflammatory vasculitis that can cause headaches, focal neurologic deficits, ocular vascular inflammation, and brain lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Visual disturbance and visual field defects
symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent oral ulcers were reported
No genital ulcers, skin lesions, arthritis, or uveitis were reported
Sudden sensorineural hearing loss is not a typical major manifestation
Normal ESR and CRP are less supportive of active systemic inflammatory vasculitis
The combined retinal artery occlusion, hearing loss, and corpus callosum lesion pattern is more characteristic of Susac syndrome

data.description: 73-year-old woman with a 10-year history of severe paraspinal muscle atrophy and cerebellar ataxia. Symptoms began at age 63 with slight stooping posture, then progressive gait instability requiring a walking stick by age 68 and difficulty climbing stairs by age 70. Exam showed moderate neck flexion weakness, mild proximal limb weakness, poor tandem gait balance without limb ataxia, and MMSE score of 25. Labs: elevated creatine kinase, normal resting blood and CSF lactate, slightly low TSH, elevated antithyroglobulin and antithyroid peroxidase antibodies, elevated rheumatoid factor, and mildly positive ANA. EMG showed mild myopathic features. Audiometry revealed sensorineural high-frequency hearing loss, and Holter monitoring showed frequent premature contractions.

data.diagnosis: MERRF syndrome (myoclonic epilepsy with ragged-red fibers), usually due to the m.8344A>G mitochondrial DNA variant
data.description: A maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder characterized by mitochondrial myopathy, ragged-red fibers on muscle biopsy, neurologic manifestations, hearing loss, and sometimes cardiac conduction abnormalities. Phenotypes can be incomplete and may present predominantly with axial myopathy and ataxia.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive muscle weakness with severe paraspinal muscle atrophy and bent-spine posture
Family history suggestive of maternal transmission, with affected female relatives and seizures in a relative
Muscle-biopsy appearance consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction, including ragged-red/oxidative-enzyme-deficient fibers
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported myoclonus
No documented generalized epilepsy in the patient
Normal resting blood and cerebrospinal-fluid lactate
Very late symptom onset at age 63

data.diagnosis: Mitochondrial myopathy due to an mtDNA mutation
data.description: A group of disorders caused by impaired mitochondrial energy production. Adult-onset mitochondrial myopathy may cause axial and proximal weakness, elevated CK, exercise intolerance, hearing loss, cardiomyopathy or arrhythmia, and abnormal mitochondrial staining on muscle biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive axial and proximal muscle weakness
Marked paraspinal muscle atrophy with stooped or bent-spine posture
Muscle pathology compatible with mitochondrial myopathy
Family pedigree compatible with mitochondrial inheritance
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported exercise intolerance or exertional fatigue
No ophthalmoplegia or ptosis
Normal resting lactate in blood and CSF
No diabetes mellitus or stroke-like episodes reported

data.diagnosis: MELAS spectrum disorder (mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes)
data.description: A mitochondrial DNA disorder, most often associated with the m.3243A>G variant, causing variable combinations of myopathy, hearing loss, cognitive impairment, seizures, ataxia, diabetes, cardiomyopathy, and stroke-like episodes. Mild or late-onset phenotypes occur.
symptoms_in_common: Mitochondrial-pattern myopathy with elevated CK and myopathic EMG
symptoms_not_in_common: No stroke-like episodes
No documented lactic acidosis
Normal blood and CSF lactate at rest
No diabetes mellitus reported
Predominant severe paraspinal atrophy and bent-spine syndrome are less typical
Onset at age 63 is unusually late for classic MELAS

data.description: A nuclear-gene mitochondrial disorder caused by pathogenic POLG variants. Presentations may include external ophthalmoplegia, sensory neuropathy, ataxia, seizures, hearing loss, myopathy, and cognitive decline; severity and age at onset are variable.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated CK and myopathic EMG features
Muscle-biopsy features compatible with mitochondrial dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: No sensory neuropathy described
No progressive external ophthalmoplegia or ptosis
No liver dysfunction reported
Pedigree appears more consistent with maternal mitochondrial inheritance than autosomal recessive inheritance
Severe isolated paraspinal atrophy with bent spine is not a classic POLG presentation

data.description: An inherited myofibrillar myopathy that can cause adult-onset axial, neck, and proximal limb weakness, camptocormia or bent-spine syndrome, elevated CK, and potentially serious cardiac conduction disease or arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of similar spinal posture
symptoms_not_in_common: Cerebellar ataxia is not typical
Sensorineural hearing loss is not typical
Mild cognitive impairment is not typical
Mitochondrial-type ragged-red and oxidative-enzyme-deficient muscle fibers would not be expected as the primary biopsy finding
A maternal inheritance pattern would be less typical than autosomal dominant inheritance

data.description: A 2-year-old Korean male was admitted for evaluation and management of left hip pain. Physical examination revealed several palpable lymph nodes in the left inguinal area and an ill-defined heterogeneous mass-like lesion in the left anteromedial muscle. Peripheral blood examination showed hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL, white blood cell count 6.83 × 10^9/L, platelet count 182 × 10^9/L, and 5 atypical lymphocytes per 100 white blood cells. Immunophenotyping of neoplastic cells showed positivity for CD45 (99.0%), CD19 (94.84%), CD10 (27.64%), CD20 (94.24%), HLA-DR (95.70%), surface IgG lambda (96.45%), CD13 (22.46%), and CD117 (22.22%), and negativity for CD34 (0.01%), Tdt (0.64%), myeloperoxidase (0.01%), and various T-cell and myeloid markers.

An aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, often presenting in children with extranodal masses and bone marrow or peripheral-blood involvement. Tumor cells typically express surface immunoglobulin with light-chain restriction, CD19, CD20, CD10, and HLA-DR, while lacking TdT and CD34.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly concerning left anteromedial muscle mass
Hip pain related to adjacent soft-tissue or skeletal involvement
Mature B-cell phenotype with CD45, CD19, CD20, HLA-DR, and surface IgG lambda positivity
Light-chain restriction indicating a clonal mature B-cell population
Negative TdT and CD34, arguing against precursor lymphoblastic leukemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No classic abdominal mass or ileocecal involvement is described
No jaw or facial mass is described
White blood cell count is not elevated

data.description: A mature B-cell lymphoma composed of large malignant lymphoid cells that can involve lymph nodes, extranodal soft tissue, and bone marrow. It is less common than Burkitt lymphoma in very young children but may have a similar mature B-cell immunophenotype.
symptoms_in_common: Hip pain from local tumor involvement
Clonal mature B-cell immunophenotype with CD19, CD20, CD45, HLA-DR, and surface lambda light-chain expression
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 2 years is younger than the usual age for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
CD10 expression and a blast-like circulating-cell appearance may favor Burkitt lymphoma over diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Only a small number of atypical lymphocytes are present in blood rather than a typical nodal-only presentation

data.diagnosis: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC rearrangement
data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma with high-grade morphology and frequently MYC-associated cytogenetic abnormalities. It may overlap biologically and clinically with Burkitt lymphoma and can involve extranodal tissue, marrow, and blood.
symptoms_in_common: Hip pain due to mass effect or local infiltration
Mature clonal B-cell phenotype with CD19, CD20, surface IgG lambda, and HLA-DR positivity
symptoms_not_in_common: This category is much less common in a 2-year-old child than Burkitt lymphoma
No MYC rearrangement result is explicitly provided in the clinical description
No constitutional symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats are reported

data.description: A malignancy of precursor B lymphoblasts that commonly affects young children and can cause bone pain, anemia, lymphadenopathy, and soft-tissue masses. Typical blasts express TdT and CD34 and usually lack surface immunoglobulin light-chain restriction.
symptoms_in_common: Hip pain that could reflect marrow or bone involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong surface IgG lambda expression is not typical of precursor B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma
CD20 expression is unusually strong for typical B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma
TdT is negative
CD34 is negative
The immunophenotype indicates mature rather than precursor B cells

data.diagnosis: B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable/intermediate between Burkitt lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: A mature aggressive B-cell neoplasm with features overlapping Burkitt lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Such tumors can present with extranodal masses, lymphadenopathy, marrow involvement, and a germinal-center B-cell phenotype.
symptoms_in_common: Mature B-cell markers including CD19, CD20, CD45, HLA-DR, and surface IgG lambda
symptoms_not_in_common: This diagnostic category is uncommon in very young children
The strongly mature B-cell phenotype and pediatric presentation more directly favor Burkitt lymphoma
No definitive morphologic or molecular evidence of an intermediate/unclassifiable lymphoma is provided

diagnoses.name: B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable, with features intermediate between diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and Burkitt lymphoma
diagnoses.title: B-cell lymphoma unclassifiable with features intermediate between Burkitt lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

data.description: A 12-year-old Malagasy boy consulted for a fever that had been evolving for two months, with a notion of trauma and pain in the right upper quadrant as well as chronic diarrhoea. A parasitological examination of the stool found eggs of Schistosoma mansoni. An ultrasound and a CT scan were then ordered.

data.diagnosis: Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis due to Schistosoma mansoni
data.description: Chronic intestinal schistosomiasis can cause egg deposition in portal venules, producing periportal fibrosis (Symmers pipestem fibrosis), hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and portal hypertension. The positive stool examination strongly supports this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Stool examination positive for Schistosoma mansoni eggs
Imaging appearance compatible with periportal hepatic involvement and splenomegaly
symptoms_not_in_common: History of trauma

data.description: This is the hepatic manifestation of chronic Schistosoma mansoni infection, characterized by fibrotic thickening around portal tracts, often with portal hypertension and splenic enlargement while liver function may be relatively preserved.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic diarrhoea associated with intestinal schistosomiasis
Imaging findings suggestive of periportal fibrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Two months of persistent fever is not a classic isolated manifestation of chronic periportal fibrosis
History of trauma

data.description: A pyogenic liver abscess is a focal bacterial infection of the liver that commonly causes prolonged fever, right upper-quadrant pain, and a focal hepatic lesion on ultrasound or CT.
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic diarrhoea is not typical unless there is an associated gastrointestinal source of infection
Schistosoma mansoni eggs in the stool do not establish a bacterial liver abscess
Diffuse periportal fibrosis and splenomegaly are not typical primary findings
History of trauma is not a usual cause

data.description: An amoebic liver abscess, caused by Entamoeba histolytica, typically presents with fever and right upper-quadrant pain and may follow amoebic intestinal infection.
symptoms_not_in_common: Schistosoma mansoni eggs, rather than Entamoeba histolytica, were identified in stool
Imaging features of periportal fibrosis and splenomegaly are not typical of an amoebic abscess
History of trauma is not typical

data.diagnosis: Traumatic hepatic hematoma or liver contusion
data.description: Blunt abdominal trauma can cause liver contusion or hematoma, producing right upper-quadrant pain and focal hepatic abnormalities on imaging.
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever persisting for two months is not typical unless the hematoma becomes infected
Chronic diarrhoea is not typical
Schistosoma mansoni eggs in stool are unrelated to traumatic liver injury
Periportal fibrosis and splenomegaly would not be explained by trauma alone

data.description: 44-year-old man with 1 month of intermittent nonexertional substernal burning chest pain, lasting hours to days and partially relieved by antacids/omeprazole, now presenting with a 1-hour episode that woke him from sleep and radiated to the left arm, with nausea and nonbloody vomiting. He denied dyspnea, fever, cough, leg swelling, immobility, or trauma. Past history was unremarkable, but he recalled a platelet count around 600,000/mm³ 12 years earlier and reported intermittent generalized pruritus after hot showers; he denied prior thrombosis, bleeding, headache, neurologic symptoms, or burning pain in the hands/feet. Exam showed marked distress clutching his chest, afebrile, BP 133/83 mmHg, HR 61 bpm, oxygen saturation 97% on room air, with regular cardiac rhythm, no JVD, no edema, clear lungs, and a nontender chest and abdomen. Labs showed troponin 0.08 ng/mL, WBC 22,000/mm³ with neutrophilia and bandemia, platelets 771,000/mm³, hemoglobin 17.5 g/dL, normal coagulation studies, and glucose 192 mg/dL.

data.diagnosis: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (anterior STEMI)
data.description: Acute myocardial infarction due to coronary artery occlusion, with ECG findings consistent with acute anterior wall ischemic injury in the precordial leads.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating to the left arm
Marked distress while clutching his chest
Prominent ST-segment elevation/hyperacute changes in anterior precordial ECG leads
symptoms_not_in_common: One month of intermittent burning pain partially relieved by antacids/omeprazole
Intermittent generalized pruritus after hot showers
Longstanding marked thrombocytosis
Leukocytosis with neutrophilia and bandemia

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome due to coronary thrombosis associated with a myeloproliferative neoplasm
data.description: Acute myocardial ischemia or infarction caused by arterial thrombosis; markedly elevated platelets and erythrocytosis raise concern for an underlying myeloproliferative disorder predisposing to coronary thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Radiation of pain to the left arm
symptoms_not_in_common: Chest discomfort partially relieved by antacids/omeprazole
No prior history of thrombosis
No headache, focal neurologic symptoms, or erythromelalgia
No dyspnea

data.description: A chronic JAK2-associated myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by increased red cell mass and often increased white blood cells and platelets, causing pruritus after warm bathing and increased arterial or venous thrombosis risk.
symptoms_in_common: Possible arterial thrombosis presenting as myocardial infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute burning substernal pain partially relieved by antacids
Left arm radiation of chest pain
Nausea and vomiting
No prior thrombosis
No headache, visual symptoms, neurologic symptoms, or erythromelalgia
No splenomegaly reported on examination

data.description: A chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm marked by persistent clonal thrombocytosis that can cause microvascular symptoms and arterial thrombosis, including myocardial infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent history of markedly elevated platelet counts
Possible coronary arterial thrombosis with acute chest pain and troponin elevation
Leukocytosis can occur in this disorder
No obvious reactive cause for severe thrombocytosis is provided
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated hemoglobin and hot-shower pruritus, which more strongly suggest polycythemia vera
No prior thrombosis
No erythromelalgia or burning pain in the hands or feet
No headaches or neurologic symptoms
No bleeding symptoms

data.description: Acid reflux or esophageal inflammation can cause recurrent nonexertional burning substernal discomfort, often occurring at night and improving with antacids or proton-pump inhibitors.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent nonexertional substernal burning pain for one month
Partial relief with antacids and omeprazole
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain radiating to the left arm
Marked distress with acute severe chest pain
Elevated troponin
Anterior ST-segment elevation/hyperacute ECG changes
Marked thrombocytosis, erythrocytosis, and leukocytosis
Hot-shower-associated generalized pruritus

diagnoses.name: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
diagnoses.title: Acute ST segment elevation myocardial infarction

data.description: Newborn girl admitted to the NICU after cardiorespiratory arrest at delivery. Pregnancy was complicated by maternal hepatitis C infection, treated Chlamydia trachomatis infection, gestational hypertension, and prenatal right urinary tract dilatation on serial ultrasounds from 20 weeks to term. At 40 weeks, after prolonged labor and cesarean delivery for nonreassuring fetal status with meconium-stained fluid, the infant was born breech, limp, and apneic. Required 16 minutes of resuscitation with intubation, CPR, epinephrine, and saline boluses before return of spontaneous circulation. Apgar scores were 1, 0, 0, 1, and 3 at 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20 minutes. On NICU arrival, she was hypothermic (34.9°C) with heart rate 141 bpm and blood pressure 84/59 mm Hg; therapeutic hypothermia was started.

data.diagnosis: Scimitar syndrome (partial anomalous pulmonary venous return with right lung hypoplasia)
data.description: A congenital cardiopulmonary malformation in which part or all of the right pulmonary venous drainage enters the inferior vena cava rather than the left atrium, often with right lung hypoplasia, dextroposition of the heart, anomalous systemic arterial supply, and pulmonary hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Severe cardiorespiratory compromise immediately after birth
Apnea and need for prolonged resuscitation
Abnormal chest imaging with asymmetric lung appearance and vascular abnormalities
Possible anomalous vessel arising from the aorta on imaging
Possible pulmonary hypertension contributing to neonatal instability
symptoms_not_in_common: Meconium-stained amniotic fluid
Breech presentation
Prenatal right urinary tract dilatation
Maternal hepatitis C infection
Treated maternal Chlamydia trachomatis infection
