symptoms_in_common: Cancer therapy may increase susceptibility to infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No erythema, warmth, or swelling reported
No systemic infectious symptoms reported
MRI appearance does not primarily suggest joint effusion or diffuse infectious marrow edema

data.diagnosis: Osseous metastasis involving the distal radius or wrist
data.description: Spread of malignancy to bone can cause focal pain, tenderness, reduced motion, and abnormal marrow signal; however, distal extremity metastasis is uncommon for pilocytic astrocytoma.
symptoms_in_common: Known multiply recurrent tumor with ventricular metastases
symptoms_not_in_common: Pilocytic astrocytoma rarely metastasizes outside the central nervous system
No reported destructive bone mass or soft-tissue mass
MRI appearance is more compatible with osteonecrosis than marrow-replacing tumor

data.description: 10-month-old male admitted with fever. Born at 38 weeks gestation after unremarkable pregnancy, birth weight 2,960g. History of cephalhematoma over parietooccipital region at birth, bilateral inguinal hernia repair at 2 months, recurrent pneumonia and urinary tract infection. Growth parameters below 3rd percentile (weight: 7,500g, length: 73.7cm). Physical exam showed pale skin, sparse/light/curly hair with pili torti on microscopy. Neurologic exam revealed diffuse hypotonia with poor head/trunk support, no visual fixing/following, hyperreflexic deep tendon reflexes bilaterally with ankle clonus, bilateral Babinski extension. Lab results: serum copper 27 μg/dL (normal 70-130), ceruloplasmin 9.07 μg/dL (normal 20-60).

An X-linked disorder of intestinal copper transport causing systemic copper deficiency, low ceruloplasmin, neurodegeneration, connective-tissue abnormalities, characteristic sparse kinky hair, and tortuous cerebral vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Male infant with onset in the first year of life
Sparse, light, curly hair with pili torti
Failure to thrive and growth below the 3rd percentile
Diffuse hypotonia and poor head/trunk control
Severe developmental impairment with absent visual fixing/following
Hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and bilateral Babinski signs
MRI diffusion abnormalities compatible with ischemic injury
Marked tortuosity of cerebral arteries on MR angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not a characteristic primary manifestation
Recurrent pneumonia and urinary tract infection are not defining features, although they may occur secondarily

data.description: Copper deficiency caused by inadequate intake, malabsorption, prolonged parenteral nutrition, excess zinc exposure, or severe gastrointestinal disease; it can produce low copper and ceruloplasmin with anemia and neurologic dysfunction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pili torti and sparse kinky hair
Male infant with severe early neurodegeneration
History of cephalhematoma and inguinal hernias
Marked cerebral arterial tortuosity
Characteristic diffuse upper-motor-neuron signs with ankle clonus and Babinski responses
No stated history of malabsorption, parenteral nutrition, dietary restriction, or zinc exposure

data.description: A milder allelic ATP7A disorder causing impaired copper transport and connective-tissue abnormalities, classically with occipital bone horns, joint laxity, bladder diverticula, vascular tortuosity, and sometimes mild neurologic impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Male sex and possible X-linked ATP7A-related condition
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe infantile neurologic deterioration at 10 months
Sparse light kinky hair with pili torti
Profound hypotonia with absent visual fixing/following
Diffuse hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and bilateral Babinski signs
No reported occipital horns, joint laxity, bladder diverticula, or skeletal exostoses
Acute ischemic-appearing brain lesions are less typical

data.diagnosis: Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome / mitochondrial encephalopathy
data.description: A group of inherited energy-metabolism disorders that may present in infancy with failure to thrive, hypotonia, developmental regression, recurrent illness, and brain injury, often with lactic acidosis or liver/muscle involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Infantile onset of severe neurologic dysfunction
Diffuse hypotonia and poor head control
Brain MRI abnormalities that may occur with metabolic decompensation
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly low serum copper and ceruloplasmin are not typical primary findings
Pili torti with sparse light kinky hair is not typical
Cerebral arterial tortuosity is not typical
Inguinal hernias and cephalhematoma are not characteristic
No reported lactic acidosis, hepatopathy, myopathy, or metabolic crisis

data.description: An ATP7B-related disorder of impaired biliary copper excretion causing copper accumulation, usually presenting later in childhood or adulthood with liver disease, psychiatric symptoms, movement disorders, and low ceruloplasmin.
symptoms_in_common: Neurologic abnormalities can occur in copper-metabolism disorders
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at 10 months is highly atypical
Low serum copper with systemic copper-deficiency features is more consistent with Menkes disease
Pili torti and sparse kinky hair are not typical
Failure to thrive with profound infantile hypotonia is not typical
Cerebral arterial tortuosity is not typical
No liver disease, jaundice, hemolysis, psychiatric symptoms, tremor, dystonia, or Kayser-Fleischer rings are reported

data.description: 47-year-old female with an incidentally found right adrenal mass discovered 3 years ago, initially 2.2 × 3.1 cm and untreated. Recent enhanced CT 10 days ago showed interval growth to 5.8 × 4.7 cm. She remained asymptomatic throughout. Past history negative for hypertension, diabetes, cardiac, pulmonary, or cerebrovascular disease; no smoking or alcohol use; reduced menstrual flow. Physical examination was unremarkable: vital signs stable, normal cardiopulmonary exam, soft non-tender abdomen without palpable mass or renal percussion pain.

A rare adrenal cortical tumor composed of eosinophilic, mitochondria-rich oncocytic cells. Most are nonfunctioning, incidentally discovered, and benign, although large size or growth can raise concern for uncertain malignant potential.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive enlargement of a unilateral adrenal mass
Asymptomatic presentation despite a relatively large tumor
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow is not a typical feature of a nonfunctioning adrenal oncocytoma

data.description: A rare aggressive malignant tumor of the adrenal cortex that may be hormonally active or nonfunctioning. Large size, heterogeneous imaging appearance, and interval growth are concerning features.
symptoms_not_in_common: No hypertension
No diabetes or features of cortisol excess
No virilization or overt androgen-excess symptoms
No abdominal pain, palpable mass, or systemic symptoms such as weight loss

data.description: A catecholamine-producing tumor arising from adrenal medullary chromaffin cells. Some pheochromocytomas are clinically silent and are identified as enlarging adrenal masses on imaging.
symptoms_not_in_common: No hypertension
No episodic headaches
No palpitations
No diaphoresis
No tremor, anxiety episodes, or catecholamine-type spells

data.description: A common benign adrenal cortical tumor, often found incidentally during imaging performed for unrelated reasons. Most nonfunctioning adenomas cause no clinical symptoms, although marked growth and a size near 6 cm are less typical.
symptoms_in_common: No clinical evidence of excess adrenal hormone production
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapid interval enlargement from approximately 3 cm to nearly 6 cm over 3 years is less typical for a benign adenoma
Reduced menstrual flow is not typical of a nonfunctioning adrenal adenoma

data.description: A rare, usually benign and nonfunctioning tumor derived from sympathetic neural crest tissue. It is often discovered incidentally and may become large before producing symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Can show slow enlargement over time
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow is not a typical manifestation
Relatively substantial increase in size over 3 years may be less typical than the slow growth usually seen

data.description: 34-year-old white male presented with an indurated plaque on the forehead that extended onto the scalp over approximately 1 year. Initial laboratory findings showed positive antinuclear antibodies (1:200) and slightly increased C3d complement; other laboratory tests were normal.

data.diagnosis: Linear morphea (linear localized scleroderma, "en coup de sabre")
data.description: A localized autoimmune fibrosing disorder causing a linear indurated plaque, classically affecting the forehead and scalp and sometimes producing alopecia and facial asymmetry.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive indurated plaque over approximately 1 year
Linear lesion involving the forehead and extending onto the scalp
Scalp hair loss/alopecia within the affected plaque
Positive antinuclear antibodies can occur in localized scleroderma
Histology appears to show dermal sclerosis with inflammatory infiltrates
symptoms_not_in_common: Slightly increased C3d complement is not a classic or required finding
Adult onset at age 34 is less typical than childhood or adolescent onset

data.description: A rare condition characterized by progressive unilateral loss of facial skin, subcutaneous tissue, muscle, and sometimes bone; it may overlap clinically with linear scleroderma en coup de sabre.
symptoms_in_common: Forehead/scalp involvement in a linear distribution
Positive antinuclear antibodies may be present in some patients
symptoms_not_in_common: No described unilateral facial atrophy or loss of facial volume
No reported involvement of deeper facial tissues, muscle, or bone
An indurated sclerotic plaque is more characteristic of linear morphea than primary Parry-Romberg syndrome

data.description: A form of chronic cutaneous lupus in which inflammation affects subcutaneous fat, producing firm plaques or nodules that may heal with depressed scars and alopecia when the scalp is involved.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammatory infiltrate involving deeper dermal/subcutaneous tissue may be seen histologically
symptoms_not_in_common: The linear forehead-to-scalp distribution is more characteristic of en coup de sabre morphea
No reported painful subcutaneous nodules or depressed lipoatrophic scars
No reported photosensitivity, malar rash, oral ulcers, arthritis, or other lupus manifestations
Normal laboratory studies aside from ANA provide limited support for systemic lupus

data.diagnosis: Discoid lupus erythematosus of the scalp
data.description: A chronic cutaneous lupus variant that causes well-demarcated inflammatory, scaly plaques with scarring alopecia, pigment alteration, and follicular plugging, commonly on sun-exposed scalp and face.
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is described as an indurated linear plaque rather than a scaly discoid plaque
No follicular plugging, adherent scale, dyspigmentation, or atrophic scarring is described
Extension in a forehead-to-scalp linear band favors linear morphea
Histologic dermal sclerosis would not be the dominant expected finding in discoid lupus

data.description: An uncommon scleroderma-like inflammatory disorder involving fascia and deep soft tissue, usually causing symmetric painful swelling and subsequent induration of the extremities.
symptoms_in_common: Possible inflammatory infiltrates in deeper tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is localized to the forehead and scalp rather than the limbs
No symmetric extremity swelling, pain, or groove sign is reported
No peripheral eosinophilia or elevated inflammatory markers is reported
A sharply linear scalp/forehead plaque is not typical

data.description: A 14-year-old girl with no prior medical history presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain for 2 days, accompanied by non-bilious vomiting. Physical examination revealed pallor, diffuse abdominal tenderness with guarding, and sluggish bowel sounds but no rigidity. Her recent history included two episodes of multiple oral ulcers that had resolved spontaneously. Laboratory findings showed hemoglobin 88 g/L, total leucocyte count 3.6 × 10⁹/L, platelets 96 × 10⁹/L, and ESR 54 mm/h. Urinalysis was normal, and blood and urine cultures were sterile. Initial ANA testing by indirect immunofluorescence with HEp-2 cell substrate was negative. Subsequent repeat ANA testing at a different laboratory remained negative, but dsDNA and anti-Ro antibodies were strongly positive with low concentrations of C3 and C4. Echocardiography showed a mild pericardial effusion.

data.diagnosis: ANA-negative systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus enteritis
data.description: A rare form of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in which ANA is negative but other lupus-specific antibodies and complement consumption are present. Lupus enteritis results from immune-mediated small-bowel vasculitis and edema.
symptoms_in_common: Bowel-wall edema and dilated bowel loops on imaging consistent with enteritis/ileus
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeated negative ANA testing by HEp-2 indirect immunofluorescence

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with mesenteric vasculitis
data.description: SLE-associated mesenteric vasculitis is immune-complex inflammation of mesenteric vessels that can cause bowel ischemia, intestinal wall thickening, abdominal pain, vomiting, and paralytic ileus.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe abdominal pain with guarding
Cytopenias including anemia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia
symptoms_not_in_common: No rigidity despite marked abdominal tenderness
Repeated negative ANA testing
No urinary abnormalities or evident renal involvement

data.description: Behcet disease is a multisystem inflammatory vasculitis characterized by recurrent oral aphthous ulcers and, in some patients, gastrointestinal ulceration causing abdominal pain and vomiting.
symptoms_in_common: Possible intestinal inflammatory changes on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Strongly positive anti-dsDNA antibodies
Low C3 and C4 complement levels
Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia
Mild pericardial effusion
No reported genital ulcers
No reported eye inflammation
No reported skin lesions or pathergy reaction

data.diagnosis: Polyarteritis nodosa or another medium-vessel systemic vasculitis
data.description: Medium-vessel vasculitis can involve mesenteric arteries, causing abdominal pain, vomiting, bowel ischemia, and intestinal edema. Polyarteritis nodosa usually does not cause glomerulonephritis.
symptoms_in_common: Bowel-wall abnormalities that may reflect intestinal ischemia or vasculitis
Normal urinalysis can occur in polyarteritis nodosa
symptoms_not_in_common: Strongly positive anti-dsDNA antibodies
Low complement levels
Recurrent oral ulcers
Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia
Pericardial effusion
No reported hypertension, neuropathy, skin nodules, livedo reticularis, or renal vascular disease

data.diagnosis: Crohn disease or other inflammatory bowel disease
data.description: Inflammatory bowel disease can cause abdominal pain, vomiting, anemia, elevated inflammatory markers, and bowel-wall thickening, particularly when there is small-bowel inflammation or obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Bowel-wall thickening and dilated bowel loops on imaging
Oral ulcers can occur with Crohn disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute presentation without reported chronic diarrhea or weight loss
Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia
Strongly positive anti-dsDNA antibodies
Low C3 and C4 complement levels
Mild pericardial effusion
No reported hematochezia, chronic diarrhea, perianal disease, or fistulas

data.description: 41-year-old woman with chest pain. One year earlier, she had transient left-sided chest and shoulder tightness. Five days before presentation, she developed acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders with dyspnea while packing for a flight; the pain lasted 1 hour and resolved spontaneously. The day before presentation, similar pain recurred after walking, accompanied by light-headedness and dyspnea. History included laparoscopic surgery for an ovarian cyst and a miscarriage 1 month prior. Family history was notable for hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in her mother, brother, and sister, and a maternal second cousin who died of cerebral aneurysm at age 51. On examination, she was diaphoretic; vital signs were temperature 36.6°C, heart rate 68 bpm, blood pressure 143/87 mmHg bilaterally, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 100%, with no cardiac murmurs, rubs, or gallops.

A nontraumatic separation of layers within a coronary artery wall that creates an intramural hematoma or false lumen, obstructing coronary blood flow and causing acute coronary syndrome. It commonly affects younger women and is associated with fibromuscular dysplasia and pregnancy-related hormonal changes.
symptoms_in_common: Acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Coronary angiographic appearance consistent with a long smooth narrowing/dissection of the left anterior descending artery
Recent miscarriage, a potential pregnancy-associated hormonal trigger
Female sex and age younger than typical patients with atherosclerotic coronary disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Transient left-sided chest and shoulder tightness one year earlier is not specific for SCAD
Family history of hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is not a typical direct cause of SCAD

data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disease causing stenosis, aneurysm, dissection, or arterial tortuosity, most often involving renal and carotid arteries. It is strongly associated with SCAD.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings compatible with renal-artery fibromuscular dysplasia, including multifocal narrowing and beading
Coronary artery dissection, which has a well-established association with FMD
Woman in the typical demographic group for FMD
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw is not usually caused directly by renal FMD
Dyspnea
Diaphoresis
Light-headedness
No reported resistant hypertension, headache, pulsatile tinnitus, or cervical bruit

data.description: SCAD occurring during pregnancy or in the postpartum period, likely related to hormonal and hemodynamic effects on vulnerable arterial walls. It can also occur after pregnancy loss.
symptoms_in_common: Recent miscarriage one month before presentation
Pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Coronary angiographic findings consistent with SCAD
Age and sex typical for pregnancy-associated SCAD
symptoms_not_in_common: The patient is not described as currently pregnant or recently postpartum after a live birth
Prior transient chest and shoulder tightness one year earlier is not necessarily related to the recent miscarriage
Renal artery abnormalities are not explained solely by pregnancy-associated SCAD

data.description: A hereditary connective-tissue disorder, usually due to pathogenic COL3A1 variants, characterized by fragile arteries and organs, arterial aneurysm or dissection, and risk of spontaneous rupture. Coronary and renal arterial dissections can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Possible arterial fragility manifested by coronary artery dissection
Family history of a connective-tissue disorder labeled hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
Family history of cerebral aneurysm-related death
History of miscarriage may occur in some hereditary connective-tissue disorders
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported thin translucent skin, characteristic facial features, easy bruising, organ rupture, or major arterial rupture
The documented family diagnosis is hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome rather than vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
No reported history of recurrent joint dislocations or marked skin hyperextensibility

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome due to atherosclerotic coronary artery disease
data.description: Myocardial ischemia caused by coronary plaque rupture, erosion, or progressive atherosclerotic narrowing, producing unstable angina or myocardial infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Radiation of pain to the jaw and shoulders
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 41 years with no stated traditional atherosclerotic risk factors
Coronary angiography suggests dissection rather than focal plaque-related stenosis
Associated renal-artery fibromuscular dysplasia favors nonatherosclerotic arteriopathy
Recent miscarriage and possible connective-tissue disease family history are not typical explanations for atherosclerotic acute coronary syndrome

data.description: Patient is a 2 month-old male, full-term infant, with severe malnutrition and failure to thrive, admitted to the intensive care unit, with long term feeding difficulties. The study was performed initially to rule out malrotation.
Hypertrophy of the pyloric muscle causes progressive gastric outlet obstruction in early infancy; upper gastrointestinal contrast studies may show an elongated, narrowed pyloric channel.

data.diagnosis: Pyloric stenosis due to pyloric/antral web
data.description: A congenital mucosal diaphragm or web at the gastric antrum or pylorus can partially obstruct gastric emptying and cause chronic feeding intolerance and poor growth.
symptoms_not_in_common: Male sex is not specifically characteristic

data.diagnosis: Intestinal malrotation with intermittent midgut volvulus
data.description: Congenital abnormal rotation and fixation of the intestine can lead to intermittent or acute duodenal obstruction and may be evaluated with an upper gastrointestinal contrast study.
symptoms_in_common: The examination was initially performed to exclude malrotation
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe chronic malnutrition is less typical than acute episodic illness
No bilious vomiting is described
No acute abdominal distension is described

data.diagnosis: Congenital duodenal stenosis or duodenal web
data.description: Partial congenital obstruction of the duodenum from narrowing or an intraluminal web can produce chronic impaired feeding, vomiting, and poor weight gain; incomplete obstruction may present after birth rather than immediately.
symptoms_not_in_common: No bilious vomiting is described
No abdominal distension is described

data.description: A congenital ring of pancreatic tissue surrounding the duodenum may cause partial duodenal obstruction, resulting in feeding intolerance and poor growth in infancy.
symptoms_not_in_common: No bilious vomiting is described
No abdominal distension is described
No associated congenital anomalies are reported

data.description: 47-year-old man with a history of hypertension presented with 3 days of left periorbital swelling, throat tightness, hoarseness, and dysphagia to solids. He had no pruritus, visual symptoms, pain, dyspnea, wheezing, fever, or recent illness. Exam showed periorbital edema with faint erythema, mildly enlarged tongue, hoarse muffled voice, no stridor, normal eye movements and pupils, and clear lungs. Two weeks later, he developed worsening dysphonia, increased throat swelling, nasal regurgitation of liquids, shoulder and hip pain, and difficulty jumping. Re-exam showed tenderness of the anterior/lateral neck muscles, subcutaneous edema in both upper arms, normal arm strength, reduced hip strength, and difficulty rising from a seated position. Labs showed normal TSH, elevated AST/ALT, markedly elevated CK, mildly elevated ESR/CRP, positive ANA, and negative myositis-specific antibodies. Left deltoid biopsy showed mild fiber size variability, perivascular inflammatory infiltrate, and patchy MHC class I staining on nonnecrotic fibers.

An inflammatory myopathy characterized by proximal muscle weakness, markedly elevated muscle enzymes, characteristic cutaneous findings, and sometimes prominent generalized or localized subcutaneous edema. Bulbar, pharyngeal, and laryngeal muscle involvement can cause dysphagia and dysphonia.
symptoms_in_common: Periorbital edema with faint erythema resembling a heliotrope rash
Subcutaneous edema of the upper arms and neck
Progressive proximal weakness, including reduced hip strength and difficulty rising from a chair
Dysphagia, nasal regurgitation, throat tightness, and hoarse muffled voice from pharyngeal/laryngeal muscle involvement
Markedly elevated CK and elevated AST/ALT consistent with muscle injury
Muscle biopsy showing perivascular inflammation and MHC class I expression on nonnecrotic muscle fibers
MRI evidence of diffuse edema involving facial, tongue, pharyngeal, and cervical muscles
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of more classic widespread dermatomyositis skin lesions such as Gottron papules
Very acute initial presentation resembling angioedema

data.description: A systemic autoimmune inflammatory myopathy that causes symmetric proximal muscle weakness, elevated CK, and possible involvement of swallowing and respiratory muscles; unlike dermatomyositis, it does not usually produce characteristic skin findings.
symptoms_in_common: Difficulty rising from a seated position and difficulty jumping
Marked CK elevation with elevated AST and ALT
Dysphagia and dysphonia due to bulbar muscle involvement
Inflammatory changes and MHC class I staining on muscle biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Periorbital edema with faint erythema suggestive of a heliotrope-type eruption
Prominent facial, tongue, pharyngeal, and subcutaneous edema
Perivascular biopsy inflammation, which is more suggestive of dermatomyositis than polymyositis

data.description: A severe autoimmune myopathy causing rapidly progressive proximal weakness and very high CK levels, often associated with statin exposure, anti-SRP antibodies, anti-HMGCR antibodies, or malignancy. Biopsy usually shows myofiber necrosis with relatively limited inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Difficulty standing from a seated position
Elevated AST and ALT due to skeletal muscle injury
Dysphagia and dysphonia can occur in severe disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Periorbital erythema and edema resembling dermatomyositis skin disease
Prominent subcutaneous edema of the face, neck, and upper arms
Perivascular inflammatory infiltrates on biopsy rather than predominantly necrotizing pathology
No reported statin exposure or myositis-specific antibodies

data.description: Nonpruritic swelling of the lips, tongue, face, and upper airway caused by increased bradykinin activity. It may occur in patients taking ACE inhibitors for hypertension and can cause hoarseness, throat tightness, and dysphagia without urticaria.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of wheezing, dyspnea, fever, and urticaria
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive proximal hip weakness and difficulty rising from a chair
Shoulder and hip muscle pain
Markedly elevated CK
Elevated AST and ALT from muscle injury
Inflammatory muscle biopsy findings
Diffuse edema within facial, pharyngeal, and cervical muscles on MRI
Symptoms progressing over weeks with systemic myositis features

data.description: An inflammatory myopathy occurring as a manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus or an autoimmune overlap syndrome. It can cause proximal weakness, myalgia, elevated CK, dysphagia, positive ANA, and inflammatory muscle biopsy findings.
symptoms_in_common: Proximal muscle weakness involving the hips
Difficulty rising from a seated position
Myalgia involving the shoulders, hips, and neck
Markedly elevated CK with elevated AST and ALT
Dysphagia and dysphonia from possible bulbar muscle involvement
Perivascular inflammatory changes on muscle biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, arthritis, nephritis, cytopenias, or serositis
Prominent periorbital and subcutaneous edema is less typical of lupus myositis
Heliotrope-like periorbital erythema is more characteristic of dermatomyositis

data.description: 11-year-old boy who received his first black henna tattoo while on holiday in Portugal in August 2013. One week after getting the tattoo, the area became hot, red, raised and itchy. Physical exam showed bullae with clear yellow-orange discharge and golden crusting on a background of erythematous plaque.

data.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis due to para-phenylenediamine (PPD) in black henna
data.description: A delayed type IV hypersensitivity reaction to PPD, a common additive in black henna tattoos. The eruption often precisely follows the tattoo pattern and can be severe with vesicles or bullae.
symptoms_in_common: Rash began about one week after black henna tattoo application
Hot, red, raised, intensely itchy skin
Erythematous plaque corresponding to the tattoo design
symptoms_not_in_common: Golden crusting may indicate secondary bacterial infection rather than uncomplicated allergic dermatitis

data.description: A superficial Staphylococcus aureus skin infection that produces fragile bullae, erosions, yellow fluid, and honey-colored or golden crusts.
symptoms_not_in_common: Intense itch and precise tattoo-shaped distribution are more suggestive of contact dermatitis
Onset after exposure to black henna is not typical as the primary cause

data.description: Allergic contact dermatitis complicated by secondary bacterial infection, commonly with Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes. This can cause oozing, pustules, and honey-colored crusting over an allergic rash.
symptoms_in_common: Delayed itchy, red, raised eruption after black henna exposure
Lesion conforms to the tattoo pattern
Golden crusting consistent with secondary impetigo
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, spreading redness, pain, or systemic illness is described

data.diagnosis: Irritant contact dermatitis from tattoo dye or application chemicals
data.description: Inflammation caused by direct chemical injury to the skin from tattoo additives, solvents, or prolonged exposure to dye. It can cause erythema, burning, itching, blistering, and oozing.
symptoms_in_common: Localized redness and warmth at the site of chemical exposure
Rash limited to the tattooed area
symptoms_not_in_common: A reaction beginning one week after exposure is more characteristic of allergic rather than irritant contact dermatitis
Golden crusting is more suggestive of secondary infection
Black henna is especially associated with PPD allergy

data.diagnosis: Cellulitis or erysipelas complicating a skin reaction
data.description: A bacterial infection of the deeper skin and subcutaneous tissue, usually causing expanding warmth, erythema, swelling, tenderness, and sometimes fever. It may occur after disruption of the skin barrier from dermatitis or blistering.
symptoms_in_common: Skin barrier disruption from bullae and discharge
symptoms_not_in_common: Itching is more typical of dermatitis than cellulitis
Tattoo-patterned distribution is not typical of cellulitis
Bullae with golden crusting are more consistent with allergic dermatitis and/or impetigo
No pain, rapidly spreading erythema, fever, or systemic symptoms are reported

data.description: 59-year-old man with multiple nodules on his joints. Patient had history of gouty arthritis (confirmed by visualization of negative birefringent crystals in joint aspirate), hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Physical examination showed multiple gouty nodules in the auricle, knee, ankle, and toe joints, with severe loss of flexion and extension in hands. Laboratory findings showed elevated creatine (137 μmol/L; normal range 62–115 μmol/L) and uric acid (725 μmol/L; normal range 208–428 μmol/L).
Advanced gout caused by long-term deposition of monosodium urate crystals in joints and soft tissues, producing tophi, erosive arthritis, and deformity.
symptoms_in_common: History of gout confirmed by negatively birefringent crystals in joint aspirate
Multiple large nodules involving hands, auricles, knees, ankles, and toes
Severe hand deformity with loss of flexion and extension
Nodules centered around joints and periarticular soft tissues
Mildly elevated creatinine, which may reduce urate excretion
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are atypical; the findings are highly characteristic of severe chronic tophaceous gout

data.description: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis that usually affects small joints symmetrically and may produce subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules and hand deformities.
symptoms_in_common: Severe bilateral hand deformity and reduced joint motion
symptoms_not_in_common: Confirmed monosodium urate crystals in joint fluid
Marked hyperuricemia
Tophi involving the auricles, toes, ankles, and knees are more typical of gout
No reported prolonged morning stiffness, symmetric inflammatory small-joint arthritis, or rheumatoid factor/anti-CCP positivity

data.description: Deposition of calcium salts in skin and periarticular soft tissues, sometimes forming large lobulated masses near major joints and causing restricted movement.
symptoms_in_common: Large deforming soft-tissue masses around the hands and joints
Mild renal dysfunction can contribute to disordered mineral metabolism
symptoms_not_in_common: Confirmed negatively birefringent urate crystals
Marked hyperuricemia strongly supports gout instead
Auricular tophi and involvement of toe joints are classic for gout
No reported calcium, phosphate, or parathyroid abnormality

data.description: A rare systemic histiocytic disorder causing destructive polyarthritis and multiple reddish-brown or yellowish papulonodular skin lesions, often affecting the hands and face.
symptoms_in_common: Severe destructive-appearing hand arthropathy with loss of motion
symptoms_not_in_common: Confirmed urate crystals in aspirated joint fluid
Severe hyperuricemia
Nodules in the auricles, toes, ankles, and knees fit tophi better
No reported characteristic facial papules, periungual lesions, or mucosal involvement

data.description: A proliferative disorder in which cartilaginous nodules form within synovium, usually affecting one large joint and causing swelling, pain, restricted motion, and loose bodies.
symptoms_in_common: Knee and ankle involvement can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse involvement of many joints, both hands, auricles, and toes is unusual
Confirmed monosodium urate crystals
Marked hyperuricemia
Large subcutaneous hand and auricular nodules are not typical
Synovial chondromatosis is usually monoarticular rather than systemic

data.description: A 25-year-old man was referred to the oncology unit with a three-week history of a progressively enlarging neck lump and atypical lymphoid cells found on fine needle aspiration cytology. He reported mild exertional dyspnea and drenching night sweats, but denied weight loss, occupational exposure to harmful substances, recent travel, or high-risk sexual behavior. He had a smoking history since age 16. On physical examination, a palpable right supraclavicular lymph node measuring 3 cm in diameter was found. Chest radiography revealed a widened mediastinum but no lung lesions. Core biopsy of the lymph node showed partial effacement of nodal architecture by scattered large cells in a background of reactive lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells with some collagen fibrosis. These large cells stained positive for CD15 and CD30 and negative for CD45.

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype
data.description: A common subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma in young adults, frequently presenting with mediastinal and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. It is characterized by Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells that are typically CD15-positive, CD30-positive, and CD45-negative, often with fibrosis and an inflammatory background containing eosinophils.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively enlarging right supraclavicular lymph node
Mild exertional dyspnea from mediastinal involvement
Large atypical cells positive for CD15 and CD30 and negative for CD45
Reactive background with eosinophils, plasma cells, and collagen fibrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss

data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that commonly arises as a bulky anterior mediastinal mass in young adults and can cause dyspnea or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Tumor cells are CD15-positive
Tumor cells are CD30-positive in a pattern typical of classical Hodgkin lymphoma
Tumor cells are CD45-negative
Prominent eosinophil-rich inflammatory background with collagen fibrosis
Scattered large cells rather than sheets of large B cells

data.description: A CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma that may present with lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms. It can occasionally involve the mediastinum but usually has a different immunophenotype and morphology from classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positivity is less typical
CD45 negativity is less typical
Fibrotic, eosinophil-rich background is more characteristic of nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma
No reported ALK positivity or T-cell marker expression

data.description: An aggressive immature T-cell neoplasm that often affects adolescent or young adult males and commonly presents with a large anterior mediastinal mass, respiratory symptoms, and lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Large cells positive for CD15 and CD30 are not typical
CD45-negative tumor cells are not typical
Eosinophil-rich reactive background and collagen fibrosis are not typical
No immature lymphoblast markers such as TdT are reported

data.description: A germ cell tumor arising in the anterior mediastinum, most often in young men. It may cause mediastinal widening, dyspnea, chest symptoms, and occasionally constitutional symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Supraclavicular lymph node biopsy showing atypical lymphoid cells
Drenching night sweats are less typical
CD15-positive and CD30-positive large lymphoid cells are not characteristic
CD45-negative Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg-like immunophenotype is not characteristic
Reactive eosinophils, plasma cells, and nodal fibrosis favor Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: A 45-year-old man presented with dry cough and breathlessness. During the investigation, he was found to be infected with HIV. Physical examination and other baseline clinical details were not specifically described in this brief case report.
An opportunistic fungal pneumonia in people with advanced HIV infection, typically causing diffuse bilateral interstitial or perihilar lung infiltrates and progressive hypoxemic respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral diffuse/perihilar interstitial pulmonary opacities on chest radiograph

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving the lungs; HIV increases the risk of both typical and atypical radiographic presentations, including diffuse infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Dry cough is less characteristic than a persistent productive cough
No fever, night sweats, weight loss, hemoptysis, or lymph node enlargement were described
No upper-lobe cavitation was described on the radiograph

data.description: A viral opportunistic pneumonia that can occur in severely immunocompromised people with HIV, producing dyspnea, cough, and diffuse interstitial or patchy lung opacities.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever was reported
No systemic cytomegalovirus manifestations, such as visual symptoms, gastrointestinal symptoms, or neurologic symptoms, were described

data.description: A vascular tumor associated with human herpesvirus 8 that may involve the lungs in advanced HIV, causing cough, dyspnea, and bilateral perihilar or interstitial infiltrates.
symptoms_not_in_common: No skin, oral, or other visible Kaposi sarcoma lesions were described
No pleural effusion was described
No hemoptysis was reported

data.description: Pneumonia caused by organisms such as Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydia pneumoniae, or respiratory viruses, often producing a dry cough and diffuse or patchy interstitial radiographic infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral patchy/interstitial pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: HIV infection raises stronger concern for opportunistic pneumonia such as Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
No fever, sore throat, headache, or myalgia was reported

data.description: A 65-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history presented with a one-month history of worsening breathlessness and chest discomfort on walking. He came to hospital following a collapse that occurred after self-administering sublingual glyceryl trinitrate to relieve his symptoms. He reported no history of cough or coryza, had not lost weight, and experienced no haemoptysis. Laboratory testing revealed a raised serum D-dimer level.

Diffuse infiltration of pulmonary lymphatic vessels by metastatic carcinoma, producing interlobular septal and peribronchovascular thickening; it may be asymmetric and can present with rapidly progressive dyspnea.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening breathlessness over one month
Imaging showing asymmetric right-sided interstitial and septal thickening
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No cough
No haemoptysis
Collapse after taking sublingual glyceryl trinitrate

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arterial blood flow by thrombus, commonly causing acute or subacute dyspnea, pleuritic or nonspecific chest pain, syncope, and an elevated D-dimer.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms gradually worsening for one month rather than abrupt onset
Imaging pattern of unilateral interstitial septal thickening rather than a typical vascular filling defect
No haemoptysis

data.description: A rare cancer-related condition in which microscopic tumor emboli and secondary small-vessel remodeling cause rapidly progressive pulmonary hypertension, hypoxemia, and dyspnea; D-dimer may be elevated.
symptoms_in_common: Possible asymmetric interstitial abnormalities on chest imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No known malignancy
No weight loss
No cough
No haemoptysis

data.diagnosis: Congestive heart failure with pulmonary interstitial edema
data.description: Elevated left-sided cardiac filling pressures can cause exertional dyspnea and interstitial pulmonary edema, visible as septal thickening and increased lung markings on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Interstitial septal thickening on chest imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly asymmetric right-sided lung abnormality
Raised D-dimer level
Collapse after glyceryl trinitrate
No reported orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, or peripheral edema

data.diagnosis: Primary lung cancer with associated interstitial or lymphatic spread
data.description: Lung cancer is strongly associated with tobacco exposure and may cause progressive dyspnea through airway obstruction, pleural disease, lymphangitic spread, or cancer-associated thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Raised D-dimer level, which may occur with cancer-associated thrombosis
Unilateral right-sided abnormal interstitial lung changes
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No cough
No haemoptysis
No discrete lung mass described on the provided imaging

data.description: A 56-year-old woman presented with a 1-week history of shortness of breath and sore throat. Her medical history included smoking, obesity, type 2 diabetes On examination, her oxygen saturation was 81% on room air, dropping to 71% with exertion. She was afebrile with a normal white blood cell count. Chest examination revealed soft heart sounds, decreased air entry, wheeze, and aegophony at the lung bases bilaterally. Abdominal examination was normal except for obesity.

Congenital or acquired thinning and abnormal elevation of an intact hemidiaphragm, causing reduced lung expansion and basal compressive atelectasis. The imaging shows marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hypoxemia at rest and with exertion
Decreased air entry at the lung bases
Bibasal aegophony consistent with reduced basal lung aeration
Obesity, which can worsen restrictive respiratory impairment
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze
Acute onset over only 1 week

data.diagnosis: Right phrenic nerve palsy causing unilateral diaphragmatic paralysis
data.description: Loss of phrenic nerve function causes elevation and reduced movement of one hemidiaphragm, producing restrictive ventilatory impairment and basal atelectasis. It can be especially symptomatic in patients with obesity or underlying lung disease.
symptoms_in_common: Obesity, which may increase symptoms from diaphragmatic weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze
Aegophony is not a classic primary feature
Severe hypoxemia is less typical with isolated unilateral paralysis unless there is additional lung disease

data.diagnosis: Right basal compressive atelectasis secondary to elevated hemidiaphragm
data.description: Partial collapse of the lower lung due to external compression or inadequate ventilation, in this case likely related to the markedly elevated right hemidiaphragm. It can impair gas exchange and cause abnormal basal chest findings.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced air entry at the lung bases
Imaging evidence of reduced right basal lung volume adjacent to the elevated diaphragm
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze
Normal white blood cell count and absence of fever do not suggest an infectious cause of atelectasis

data.description: Chronic hypoventilation related to severe obesity, often associated with sleep-disordered breathing, hypercapnia, and resting or exertional hypoxemia. An elevated hemidiaphragm can further reduce respiratory reserve.
symptoms_in_common: Soft heart sounds and reduced chest excursion may be more difficult to assess in obesity
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Focal elevation of the right hemidiaphragm on imaging
Aegophony at both lung bases
Acute 1-week presentation without reported chronic daytime somnolence or sleep apnea symptoms

data.diagnosis: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation
data.description: COPD is an obstructive lung disease commonly caused by smoking and may present with dyspnea, wheeze, and hypoxemia. A viral upper respiratory illness can precipitate an exacerbation.
symptoms_in_common: Sore throat, which may indicate a viral trigger for an exacerbation
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked unilateral elevation of the right hemidiaphragm on imaging
Aegophony at the lung bases
No reported chronic cough or sputum production
No fever or elevated white blood cell count

data.description: 67-year-old female patient presented with chief complaint of swelling in right cheek. History of unhealed tooth extraction sockets from right upper posterior tooth extraction performed approximately one month previously. Past medical history significant for colorectal cancer treatment. Intraoral examination revealed localized, well-defined swelling measuring 4 cm × 5 cm obliterating buccal and palatal vestibules in region of unhealed extraction sockets of teeth 14, 15, and 16. Laboratory examination showed abnormal GTP level and slightly elevated serum CRP level.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL-NOS) of the maxilla
data.description: An aggressive non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma that commonly presents as a rapidly enlarging extranodal mass. In the oral cavity it can mimic dental infection, cause nonhealing extraction sockets, and produce maxillary bone destruction.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly apparent 4 cm × 5 cm well-defined right maxillary/cheek swelling
Nonhealing extraction sockets after recent extraction
Obliteration of buccal and palatal vestibules by a soft-tissue mass
Imaging appearance of a maxillary soft-tissue lesion with local bone involvement
Cytology/histology showing atypical large lymphoid cells
BCL6 and MUM1 immunoreactivity, supportive of a large B-cell lymphoma phenotype
symptoms_not_in_common: History of colorectal cancer is not a typical cause of DLBCL, although prior cancer treatment may contribute to immune dysregulation
Abnormal GTP level is nonspecific and not a usual presenting feature of DLBCL

data.description: A highly aggressive lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation that often arises in the oral cavity, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. It may present as a rapidly enlarging gingival, palatal, or maxillary mass after dental procedures.
symptoms_in_common: Possible destructive maxillary lesion on imaging
Older age and prior cancer treatment, which may be associated with impaired immune status
Large atypical cells on cytologic examination
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented HIV infection, transplant history, or other major immunodeficiency
The reported BCL6 positivity would be less typical because plasmablastic lymphoma is usually associated with plasma-cell markers such as CD138, CD38, and MUM1 and is often B-cell marker negative
No reported ulceration or extensive mucosal necrosis

data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma characterized by extremely rapid growth and a high proliferation rate. It can involve the jaws and produce dental loosening, swelling, and nonhealing extraction sites, although it is much less common in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Potential osseous destruction and soft-tissue extension on imaging
Large atypical lymphoid-cell population may be seen on cytology
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 67 years is atypical, as Burkitt lymphoma more often affects children, adolescents, or younger adults
No reported very high LDH, tumor lysis findings, or systemic abdominal disease
MUM1 positivity is less typical because classic Burkitt lymphoma is generally MUM1 negative
The lesion appears localized without the classic rapidly disseminated clinical pattern

data.diagnosis: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma to the maxilla/oral cavity
data.description: Metastatic spread of colorectal cancer to the oral cavity or jaw is uncommon but can present as a painful or painless gingival/maxillary mass, swelling, delayed healing after extraction, and bone destruction.
symptoms_in_common: Previous history of colorectal cancer treatment
Potential maxillary bone destruction on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Cytology/histology appears to show atypical lymphoid rather than gland-forming epithelial tumor cells
BCL6 and MUM1 immunostaining supports lymphoid differentiation rather than colorectal adenocarcinoma
No reported gastrointestinal recurrence, liver metastases, lung metastases, or elevated colorectal tumor markers
The localized lymphoid-appearing oral lesion is more typical of lymphoma than metastatic colorectal carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Odontogenic infection with maxillary osteomyelitis or post-extraction abscess
data.description: Bacterial infection of an extraction site can lead to delayed healing, facial swelling, elevated inflammatory markers, abscess formation, and osteomyelitis of the maxilla. It is an important initial clinical differential diagnosis for this presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Swelling in the right cheek/maxillary region
Local swelling involving buccal and palatal vestibules
symptoms_not_in_common: A large, well-defined mass is less typical than diffuse tender inflammatory swelling
No reported fever, severe pain, purulent drainage, foul taste, or marked leukocytosis
Atypical large lymphoid cells on cytology are not expected in bacterial infection
BCL6 and MUM1 immunoreactivity is not compatible with a simple odontogenic infection
The imaging appearance of a discrete mass with destructive features is more concerning for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Primary oral diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphomas

data.description: 24-year-old man presents with severely itchy rash that spread over two months. Had previously used an over-the-counter cream containing clobetasol, ofloxacin, terbinafine, and ornidazole which helped initially.
A dermatophyte fungal infection whose typical scaly, raised ring-like border has been altered and allowed to spread by topical corticosteroid use. It commonly affects the groin, thighs, and trunk.
symptoms_in_common: Large annular and polycyclic erythematous plaques with areas of scale
Involvement of the groin and inner thighs
Partial initial improvement with a cream containing terbinafine and clobetasol
Prior potent topical clobetasol exposure, which can mask and worsen dermatophyte infection

data.description: A superficial dermatophyte infection of glabrous skin and the groin, classically producing pruritic expanding annular plaques with a more active scaly border and central clearing.
symptoms_in_common: Relative central clearing in some lesions
Gradual spread over weeks to months
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesions have unusually extensive, less sharply defined morphology, likely due to prior topical corticosteroid use
Initial improvement with a combination cream containing potent corticosteroid may obscure the classic active border

data.description: A reactive inflammatory eruption characterized by slowly enlarging annular plaques, often with trailing scale inside the advancing edge. It can be itchy and may be triggered by infections, medications, or other inflammatory conditions.
symptoms_in_common: Gradual spread over weeks to months
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe itch is less characteristic than in dermatophyte infection
Prominent groin and inner-thigh distribution is more suggestive of tinea cruris
Multiple large plaques with peripheral active-looking scale favor fungal infection
Initial benefit from terbinafine-containing treatment supports a dermatophyte process

data.description: A chronic eczematous dermatitis causing pruritic coin-shaped erythematous, scaly plaques, usually on the limbs. Lesions may become extensive and excoriated.
symptoms_in_common: Some transient improvement with topical clobetasol
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are predominantly annular with central clearing rather than uniformly coin-shaped
Progressive centrifugal expansion and polycyclic borders are more typical of tinea
Prominent groin involvement is less typical
The rash spread despite use of a potent topical corticosteroid-containing product

data.description: A chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease producing well-demarcated erythematous plaques with scale. Inverse psoriasis may involve the groin, although scale is often reduced in moist folds.
symptoms_in_common: Temporary improvement can occur with potent topical corticosteroids
symptoms_not_in_common: Large annular lesions with central clearing are not classic for psoriasis
Centrifugal spread over two months is more characteristic of dermatophyte infection
The distribution is concentrated on groin and inner thighs rather than classic extensor surfaces
The steroid-modified ring-like morphology strongly favors tinea incognito

data.description: 72-year-old man with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease controlled on daily omeprazole until 11 months before admission, when heartburn recurred despite treatment. He developed postprandial nausea and early satiety, with gradually worsening symptoms over 9 months and progressive dietary intolerance from solid food to soft solids, then blended foods, then mainly liquids over the next 2 months. Two months before admission, evaluation at another hospital included EGD after 24 hours without food, but the stomach could not be adequately visualized because of large retained food; no intraluminal mass was seen. When he became unable to tolerate liquids, he presented to the emergency department. On examination, he was thin, had a nasogastric tube in place, temperature 37.7°C, pulse 105 beats/min, blood pressure 128/76 mm Hg, and mild epigastric tenderness without abdominal distension.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma (linitis plastica/signet-ring cell carcinoma) causing gastric outlet obstruction
data.description: An infiltrative gastric cancer that spreads diffusely through the stomach wall, producing marked wall thickening, rigid folds, impaired gastric emptying, and sometimes no obvious intraluminal mass. The imaging, endoscopic appearance, and deep-wall histology are highly suggestive of this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive intolerance of solids followed by liquids
Large retained gastric contents despite prolonged fasting
Thin appearance consistent with weight loss/malnutrition
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent heartburn is not a defining symptom
Lack of a clearly visible intraluminal mass on the initial endoscopy

data.diagnosis: Gastric outlet obstruction due to peptic ulcer-related pyloric or duodenal stricture
data.description: Chronic peptic ulcer disease can cause inflammation and fibrosis at the pylorus or proximal duodenum, narrowing the gastric outlet and resulting in retention of food, nausea, and vomiting or inability to tolerate oral intake.
symptoms_in_common: Retained food in the stomach after fasting
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked diffuse gastric wall thickening and nodular enlarged gastric folds are less typical
Progressive severe obstruction despite daily omeprazole
Histologic evidence of infiltrative malignant-appearing cells would not be typical

data.description: Lymphoma involving the stomach can cause diffuse gastric wall thickening, enlarged folds, early satiety, nausea, and occasionally gastric outlet obstruction. It may appear as an infiltrative rather than discrete mass lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse gastric wall/fold abnormality rather than a clearly defined intraluminal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Gradual progression from solids to liquids due to severe mechanical gastric outlet obstruction is less common than with antral carcinoma
The described histologic appearance is more suggestive of infiltrating epithelial carcinoma than lymphoma
No reported systemic lymphoma symptoms such as drenching night sweats or lymphadenopathy

data.description: A GIST is a mesenchymal tumor arising from the gastric wall. Large tumors can compress or obstruct the gastric outlet and cause early satiety, nausea, abdominal discomfort, and poor oral intake.
symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete intraluminal or exophytic mass was identified on initial endoscopy
Diffuse thickening of the stomach wall and diffusely nodular mucosa are less typical than a focal mass
The extensive retained food and linitis-like pattern are more suggestive of infiltrative carcinoma

data.description: Gastroparesis is delayed gastric emptying caused by impaired gastric motility, often related to diabetes, medications, neurologic disease, or idiopathic dysfunction. It causes nausea, early satiety, and retained food without a mechanical obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Retained food in the stomach despite fasting
Thin appearance consistent with poor nutritional intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive transition from solid-food intolerance to inability to tolerate liquids strongly suggests mechanical obstruction
Marked gastric wall thickening and abnormal nodular folds are not typical
Mild epigastric tenderness is less characteristic
No reported diabetes, neurologic disorder, or medication trigger for gastroparesis
