diagnoses.title: Intestinal infections due to Clostridioides difficile

data.description: 29-year-old man with 6 weeks of unintentional 10 kg weight loss, followed by severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the throat and worsened by eating. Three weeks before presentation, he developed nausea, occasional vomiting, decreased oral intake, one episode of hematemesis, sore throat, and fever. Past history notable for a respiratory illness about 2 years earlier and chronic macular hyperpigmentation of the feet and legs for 10 years. On examination, he was cachectic, tachycardic, and febrile later in the course, with low body weight/BMI, soft abdomen initially then firm without distention, coarse breath sounds with scattered fine rales at both lung bases, white exudate on the underside of the tongue, and multiple nontender, mobile 1–2 cm submandibular, submental, and cervical lymph nodes.

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with miliary pulmonary and abdominal involvement
data.description: Widespread Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can produce diffuse micronodular lung disease, fever, profound weight loss, lymphadenopathy, and gastrointestinal or abdominal involvement, particularly in an immunocompromised person.
symptoms_in_common: Severe unintentional weight loss and cachexia
Diffuse fine rales at both lung bases
Diffuse tiny pulmonary nodules consistent with a miliary pattern on imaging
Abdominal pain and poor oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: White oral/tongue exudate suggestive of candidiasis
Pain radiating to the throat and worsened specifically by eating
Hematemesis
Chronic macular hyperpigmentation of the feet and legs for 10 years

data.diagnosis: Advanced HIV infection/AIDS with opportunistic infections
data.description: Advanced HIV infection causes severe weight loss, generalized lymphadenopathy, oral candidiasis, recurrent or unusual infections, and susceptibility to disseminated fungal or mycobacterial disease.
symptoms_in_common: Marked unintentional weight loss and low BMI
Oral white exudate compatible with oral candidiasis
Diffuse pulmonary micronodules that could reflect an opportunistic infection
Nausea, vomiting, and decreased oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe focal upper abdominal pain radiating to the throat
Postprandial worsening of pain
Hematemesis
Chronic stable hyperpigmented macules on the feet and legs

data.description: Disseminated Histoplasma capsulatum infection, especially in people with advanced HIV, can cause fever, wasting, diffuse pulmonary nodules, lymphadenopathy, mucosal lesions, and gastrointestinal disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: White tongue exudate more typical of Candida infection than histoplasmosis
Pain clearly radiating to the throat and precipitated by eating
Hematemesis
Long-standing hyperpigmentation of the feet and legs

data.description: Talaromycosis is an opportunistic fungal infection, classically associated with advanced HIV in Southeast Asia, that causes fever, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, and skin or gastrointestinal manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal symptoms including pain, nausea, vomiting, and reduced intake
Possible chronic or abnormal skin pigmentation
Findings suggestive of underlying immunosuppression, including oral candidiasis
symptoms_not_in_common: No described characteristic umbilicated papules with central necrosis
Hematemesis is not a common presenting feature
Pain radiating to the throat and strongly worsened by meals
The skin hyperpigmentation had been present for 10 years, which is less typical of acute disseminated talaromycosis

data.diagnosis: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including HIV-associated lymphoma with gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: Aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma can cause constitutional symptoms, enlarged lymph nodes, abdominal pain from gastrointestinal or abdominal disease, and occasionally pulmonary nodules; risk is increased in advanced HIV infection.
symptoms_in_common: Nausea, vomiting, and decreased oral intake
Diffuse pulmonary abnormalities can occur with extranodal lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: White oral exudate suggestive of candidiasis
Miliary-pattern diffuse pulmonary micronodules are more suggestive of disseminated infection
Fine bibasal rales are less typical of isolated lymphoma
Long-standing macular hyperpigmentation of the feet and legs

data.description: 65-year-old Haitian man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, bicuspid aortic valve with ascending/aortic-root aneurysm, prior positive tuberculin skin test, treated secondary syphilis, and recent HTLV-1 positivity. He had 12 kg unintentional weight loss over 2 years and presented with a leg injury and diffuse pruritic rash. Examination showed bilateral wrinkling axillary plaques, multiple thin brown macules and patches with collarette scale on the palms and some soles, and bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy.

data.diagnosis: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma with cutaneous involvement
data.description: An aggressive mature CD4-positive T-cell neoplasm caused by HTLV-1 infection that can involve skin, lymph nodes, blood, and other organs.
symptoms_in_common: Brown macules and patches with scale
Older adult from an HTLV-1 endemic region
symptoms_not_in_common: End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis
Leg injury
Bicuspid aortic valve and aortic aneurysm

data.description: The most common primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, typically causing slowly progressive pruritic patches, plaques, and sometimes tumors with epidermotropic atypical T cells.
symptoms_in_common: Plaques in intertriginous areas including the axillae
Weight loss can occur in advanced disease
symptoms_not_in_common: HTLV-1 positivity is not typical
Palmar and plantar collarette-scaled lesions are less typical
Rapid concern for systemic disease with prominent inguinal lymphadenopathy is less typical in early mycosis fungoides

data.description: A leukemic variant of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma characterized by generalized itchy erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and malignant T cells in the blood.
symptoms_not_in_common: No generalized erythroderma is described
No circulating malignant lymphocytes or leukocytosis is reported
Discrete brown macules and collarette scaling on the palms and soles are not classic
HTLV-1 positivity favors adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma rather than Sézary syndrome

data.description: The disseminated stage of Treponema pallidum infection, often producing a diffuse papulosquamous rash that may involve the palms and soles with generalized lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Thin brown macules and patches with collarette scale
symptoms_not_in_common: He was previously treated for secondary syphilis
Wrinkled axillary plaques are not typical
Two years of substantial weight loss is not typical of uncomplicated secondary syphilis
HTLV-1 positivity raises concern for an alternative lymphoproliferative disorder

data.description: A severe infestation with Sarcoptes scabiei, often occurring in immunocompromised or chronically ill patients and causing widespread pruritic scaling and crusting.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic renal failure and hemodialysis, which may increase susceptibility to severe skin disease
Possible involvement of hands and feet
symptoms_not_in_common: No burrows, thick crusts, or classic web-space involvement are described
Inguinal lymphadenopathy is not a usual prominent feature
Unintentional 12 kg weight loss is not typical
Wrinkled axillary plaques and brown palmar collarette-scaled macules are not classic for scabies

data.description: 52-year-old man with 2 weeks of exertional central chest fullness and dyspnea, absent at rest, without light-headedness or syncope. Past history includes type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, and family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; prior screening echocardiogram 3 years earlier showed mild left ventricular hypertrophy with otherwise normal structure and function. On exam: afebrile, BP 146/70 mmHg, HR 70/min, RR 14/min, BMI 36.2; normal JVP, regular rhythm without murmurs/rubs/gallops, clear lungs, normal abdomen, warm legs without edema, symmetric distal pulses. Initial labs showed WBC 10,900/mm3, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL (baseline 1.0), potassium 5.4 mmol/L, and normal INR, BUN, sodium, thyrotropin, and troponin I.

A rare, rapidly progressive inflammatory myocarditis characterized by myocardial destruction, lymphocytic inflammation, and multinucleated giant cells on biopsy. It commonly causes ventricular arrhythmias, conduction disease, heart failure, and sudden cardiac death.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid clinical course over approximately 2 weeks
Histology showing multinucleated giant cells with inflammatory myocardial injury
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms at rest
No light-headedness or syncope
No peripheral edema
Normal jugular venous pressure
Normal troponin I

data.description: Inflammatory cardiac involvement by sarcoidosis, typically producing noncaseating granulomas that may lead to conduction block, ventricular tachycardia, cardiomyopathy, and heart failure.
symptoms_not_in_common: No known pulmonary sarcoidosis or systemic sarcoid manifestations
No syncope or presyncope
No documented atrioventricular block
Biopsy appearance of diffuse giant-cell myocarditis rather than well-formed noncaseating granulomas
No edema or clinical heart failure findings

data.description: An inherited myocardial disease characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy, often asymmetric, which can cause exertional dyspnea, angina, arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death.
symptoms_in_common: Previously documented mild left ventricular hypertrophy
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset and progression over only 2 weeks
No systolic murmur on examination
No syncope or presyncope
Histology with inflammatory infiltrates and multinucleated giant cells
Prior echocardiogram otherwise showed normal cardiac structure and function

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome due to obstructive coronary artery disease
data.description: Myocardial ischemia caused by coronary atherosclerotic plaque rupture or severe fixed coronary stenosis. Diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity substantially increase risk.
symptoms_in_common: Ventricular arrhythmia can occur with ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest discomfort at rest
Normal troponin I
No ischemic ST-segment elevation described on the initial ECG
No acute heart failure signs such as rales, elevated JVP, or edema
Myocardial biopsy findings of giant-cell inflammatory myocarditis are not typical of coronary atherosclerotic disease

data.description: A genetic myocardial disorder, usually involving the right ventricle but sometimes the left ventricle, that predisposes to ventricular tachycardia, sudden death, and progressive ventricular dysfunction due to fibrofatty myocardial replacement.
symptoms_in_common: Chest discomfort may occur during tachyarrhythmia
symptoms_not_in_common: Age of presentation is later than typical
No reported palpitations, syncope, or family history of sudden cardiac death
No reported right ventricular abnormalities
Prior echocardiogram was largely structurally normal
Histology shows inflammatory giant-cell myocarditis rather than fibrofatty replacement

data.description: 32-year-old woman, pregnant for the first time, with history of CIN II treated by loop excision 2 years earlier, prior bilateral breast reduction with delayed but spontaneous wound healing, and chronic hypertension diagnosed at 18 weeks’ gestation. At 31 weeks and 4 days, she presented with 2 weeks of flu-like symptoms followed by lower abdominal pain and fever. Examination showed temperature 38.3°C, uterine contractions, fundal height at 29 weeks, and cervix 1 cm dilated and fully effaced with intact membranes. Ultrasound showed fetal growth at the 5th percentile and oligohydramnios; fetal monitoring showed heart rate 160 bpm with late decelerations. Labs showed leukocytosis with neutrophilia and elevated CRP. After cesarean section for suspected fetal distress, she developed persistent postoperative fever, rising inflammatory markers, and a non-healing surgical wound despite treatment.

A rare neutrophilic inflammatory skin disease causing rapidly progressive painful ulceration, often triggered by surgical trauma (pathergy). It can mimic wound infection but worsens despite antibiotics and debridement.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcerated wound with violaceous/purple undermined borders on the image
Persistent postoperative fever and elevated inflammatory markers
Poor wound healing after prior breast surgery
Failure to improve with treatment for presumed infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Flu-like illness preceding the obstetric presentation
Preterm uterine contractions and cervical effacement
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
Late fetal heart-rate decelerations

data.diagnosis: Post-cesarean surgical-site infection with wound dehiscence
data.description: A bacterial infection involving the cesarean incision that may cause cellulitis, purulent drainage, separation of wound edges, fever, and delayed healing.
symptoms_in_common: Inflamed wound margins and yellow wound exudate
symptoms_not_in_common: Violaceous undermined wound borders, which are more suggestive of pyoderma gangrenosum
History of delayed spontaneous healing after breast reduction
Failure to improve despite treatment
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios

data.description: A rapidly progressive, life-threatening deep soft-tissue infection that can occur after surgery and causes systemic toxicity, severe pain, tissue necrosis, and wound breakdown.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly abnormal postoperative wound appearance with tissue breakdown
Possible skin discoloration around the wound
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported pain out of proportion to examination
No documented rapidly spreading skin necrosis, bullae, crepitus, or shock
No reported hemodynamic instability
Prior delayed breast-surgery wound healing is not specifically typical
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios are not typical consequences

data.description: Infection and inflammation of the amniotic fluid, placenta, membranes, or uterus, usually presenting in pregnancy with maternal fever, uterine tenderness or contractions, maternal leukocytosis, and fetal tachycardia.
symptoms_in_common: Lower abdominal pain and uterine contractions
Preterm labor with cervical dilation and full effacement
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent postoperative wound ulceration with violaceous borders
Non-healing cesarean incision despite treatment
History of poor healing after breast reduction surgery
Chronic hypertension

data.description: A hypertensive disorder of pregnancy that can impair placental function, leading to fetal growth restriction, oligohydramnios, and nonreassuring fetal testing. It may coexist with infection or another inflammatory condition.
symptoms_in_common: Fundal height smaller than expected for gestational age
Fetal heart-rate late decelerations suggesting placental insufficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever
Flu-like symptoms
Leukocytosis with neutrophilia
Elevated inflammatory markers due to acute inflammation
Uterine contractions with cervical change from suspected infection
Persistent postoperative fever
Non-healing ulcerative surgical wound

data.description: An 87-year-old man presented with a one-year history of difficulty swallowing, with episodes of choking and aspiration that progressively increased in frequency. Laryngeal examination revealed extraluminal obstruction from behind. The patient had multiple comorbidities as mentioned in the case.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH, Forestier disease) with large anterior cervical osteophytes
data.description: A noninflammatory disorder characterized by flowing calcification and ossification along spinal ligaments, often producing large anterior cervical osteophytes that can compress the pharynx or esophagus.
symptoms_in_common: Extraluminal posterior compression seen on laryngeal examination
Imaging appearance of prominent anterior cervical bony bridging/osteophytes
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms clearly atypical for this diagnosis are reported

data.diagnosis: Cervical spondylosis with anterior cervical osteophyte formation
data.description: Age-related degeneration of the cervical spine can cause osteophytes; very large anterior osteophytes may mechanically obstruct the hypopharynx or cervical esophagus and cause swallowing impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Posterior extraluminal compression of the laryngeal/pharyngeal region
Cervical spine degenerative bony changes on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No neck pain or restricted neck motion is reported
No arm pain, numbness, weakness, or other cervical radiculopathy symptoms are reported

data.diagnosis: Ossification of the anterior longitudinal ligament
data.description: Pathologic calcification or ossification of the anterior longitudinal ligament can create a prominent anterior cervical mass effect, sometimes overlapping with DISH and causing dysphagia.
symptoms_in_common: Mechanical obstruction from behind the larynx
Radiographic suggestion of extensive anterior cervical ligamentous ossification
symptoms_not_in_common: No neck stiffness or neck pain is reported
No neurologic symptoms related to spinal cord or nerve compression are reported

data.description: A mass in the retropharyngeal space or hypopharynx can externally compress the larynx, pharynx, or esophagus and lead to progressive dysphagia and aspiration.
symptoms_in_common: Extraluminal posterior obstruction on laryngeal examination
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging favors a bony cervical spine process rather than a soft-tissue mass
No weight loss is reported
No throat pain, neck mass, hoarseness, bleeding, or enlarged cervical lymph nodes are reported

data.description: A pharyngoesophageal pouch that can retain food and secretions, causing dysphagia, regurgitation, coughing, choking, and aspiration, particularly in older adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Posterior extraluminal laryngeal obstruction is not typical of Zenker diverticulum
Imaging suggests cervical bony compression rather than a pharyngoesophageal pouch
No regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis, gurgling in the neck, or recurrent pneumonia is reported

data.description: A 22-year-old African American/Asian college-age woman presented with a 3-month history of mild exertional dyspnea that progressively worsened despite treatment with inhalers for suspected reactive airway disease. She reported shortness of breath with mild exertion, nonproductive cough for several weeks, and a 5-lb weight loss. She denied fever, chills, headaches, syncope, dizziness, bone pain, nausea, or vomiting. Physical examination was unremarkable except for decreased breath sounds and slight dullness to percussion on the left. Routine laboratory work-up was unremarkable. Initially, chest x-ray showed mediastinal widening, which led to further imaging and biopsy. An open mediastinal biopsy was performed after CT-guided biopsy failed, revealing a poorly differentiated carcinoma initially thought to be thymic carcinoma. Flow cytometry from tissue showed T cells and polyclonal B cells with no immunophenotypic evidence of malignancy.

data.diagnosis: NUT carcinoma (NUT midline carcinoma) of the mediastinum
data.description: A rare, highly aggressive poorly differentiated carcinoma driven by rearrangement of the NUTM1 gene, often arising in the mediastinum of adolescents and young adults and frequently initially mistaken for thymic carcinoma.
symptoms_in_common: No evidence of a lymphoid malignancy on flow cytometry
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild initial symptom severity despite a large mediastinal process
Absence of fever or other systemic inflammatory symptoms

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising from the thymus in the anterior mediastinum. It can cause cough, dyspnea, chest symptoms, and weight loss due to local compression or invasion.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion on the left
Poorly differentiated carcinoma reported on mediastinal biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Very young age, as thymic carcinoma more commonly occurs in middle-aged or older adults
No chest pain
No superior vena cava syndrome symptoms such as facial swelling or upper-extremity edema
No myasthenia gravis symptoms

data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that commonly affects young women and presents as a bulky anterior mediastinal mass causing respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Possible left-sided pleural involvement suggested by decreased breath sounds and dullness
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy interpreted as poorly differentiated carcinoma rather than lymphoma
Flow cytometry showed polyclonal B cells without immunophenotypic evidence of lymphoma
No fever
No night sweats
No palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy reported

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma with mediastinal involvement
data.description: A lymphoid malignancy frequently affecting adolescents and young adults; nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymphoma often presents with a bulky anterior mediastinal mass in young women.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive dyspnea due to thoracic compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy described a poorly differentiated carcinoma
No fever
No night sweats
No pruritus
No peripheral lymphadenopathy reported
Flow cytometry did not demonstrate a malignant lymphoid population

data.description: A germ cell tumor arising in the anterior mediastinum, including seminomatous and nonseminomatous tumors, which can produce a large mass causing cough, dyspnea, and chest radiographic widening.
symptoms_in_common: Possible mass effect associated with decreased left-sided breath sounds
symptoms_not_in_common: Female sex, since primary mediastinal germ cell tumors are more common in males
Biopsy described as poorly differentiated carcinoma rather than germ cell tumor
No reported elevated tumor markers such as alpha-fetoprotein or beta-hCG
No nausea, vomiting, or endocrine manifestations

data.description: 71-year-old woman with hematuria evaluated by abdominal CT. Past history included nephrolithiasis at age 41, long-standing easy bruising that worsened at age 66, and osteoporosis (T-score -2.6 at the left femoral neck). Physical examination showed bruising on the lower extremities. Serial testing at a tertiary center showed elevated late-night serum cortisol and abnormal Dex-CRH testing (cortisol 1.8 µg/dL at 0 minutes and 2 µg/dL at 15 minutes).

data.diagnosis: Primary bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia (PBMAH) causing ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome
data.description: A bilateral adrenal disorder with nodular enlargement of both adrenal glands that can autonomously produce cortisol, often presenting subtly in older adults. The CT appearance of bilateral adrenal nodularity/enlargement and abnormal cortisol testing strongly support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal Dex-CRH test consistent with hypercortisolism
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria

data.description: A benign adrenal cortical tumor that autonomously secretes cortisol and causes ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome. Bilateral adrenal nodules can occasionally represent adenomas, although a single unilateral lesion is more typical.
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral adrenal abnormalities rather than a solitary unilateral mass
Hematuria

data.diagnosis: Cushing disease due to an ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma
data.description: Pituitary overproduction of ACTH stimulates both adrenal glands to produce excess cortisol. It is the most common endogenous cause of Cushing syndrome but does not usually cause discrete bilateral adrenal masses.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal Dex-CRH testing suggestive of Cushing syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral nodular adrenal imaging findings are more suggestive of a primary adrenal disorder
Hematuria
No reported pituitary mass symptoms such as headache or visual field changes

data.description: Excess ACTH produced by a non-pituitary tumor, such as a small-cell lung cancer or neuroendocrine tumor, causes marked cortisol excess and bilateral adrenal stimulation. It often develops more rapidly and can be clinically severe.
symptoms_in_common: Potential bilateral adrenal enlargement from chronic ACTH stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported rapidly progressive muscle weakness, severe hypokalemia, hyperpigmentation, or weight loss
Discrete bilateral adrenal nodularity favors PBMAH over ACTH-driven adrenal stimulation
Hematuria

data.description: A malignant adrenal cortical tumor that may produce cortisol and cause Cushing syndrome. It typically appears as a large, irregular, unilateral adrenal mass and may cause rapid onset of severe cortisol-excess manifestations.
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral small/nodular adrenal abnormalities rather than a large unilateral invasive mass
Long, slowly progressive course of bruising
Hematuria without evidence of tumor invasion
No reported abdominal pain, weight loss, or metastatic symptoms

data.description: 40-year-old black woman with 10 months of progressive lower-extremity edema and abdominal distention/pain. Symptoms began with episodic pain and swelling of the feet and ankles after prolonged standing, then progressed to involve the lower legs and thighs. Five months before evaluation, she developed left back and flank pain. Past history includes hypothyroidism, latent tuberculosis, hysterectomy for fibroid uterus, appendectomy, two spontaneous vaginal deliveries, and ectopic pregnancy. On examination, she had 2+ edema of the lower and upper legs, jugular venous pressure of 8 cm H2O, and a distended, mildly tender abdomen. Laboratory studies showed hypoalbuminemia, low total protein, hypocalcemia, elevated TSH with low free thyroxine, positive ANA at 1:40 with a speckled pattern, and urinalysis with 3+ protein and 1+ blood.

data.diagnosis: Nephrotic syndrome, likely due to membranous nephropathy
data.description: A glomerular kidney disorder causing heavy urinary protein loss, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and increased risk of venous thrombosis. Membranous nephropathy is particularly associated with renal-vein and inferior-vena-cava thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal distention consistent with ascites or generalized fluid retention
Hypocalcemia, which can occur with low albumin and urinary protein loss
Flank pain and hematuria, which may occur with renal-vein thrombosis complicating nephrotic syndrome
Imaging findings concerning for extensive venous thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated TSH with low free thyroxine
Positive low-titer speckled ANA

data.diagnosis: Extensive inferior vena cava thrombosis with renal and iliac venous involvement
data.description: Thrombosis of the inferior vena cava, often extending into renal and iliac veins, obstructs venous return from the legs and abdomen. It can produce marked bilateral leg edema, abdominal wall collateral vessels, flank pain, and renal dysfunction or hematuria.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive bilateral edema beginning in the feet and ankles and extending to the thighs
CT appearance consistent with central abdominal venous obstruction/thrombosis and collateral venous circulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked proteinuria as the primary urinary abnormality
Hypoalbuminemia and low total protein, which suggest an underlying nephrotic process
Hypothyroidism

data.diagnosis: Renal vein thrombosis secondary to nephrotic syndrome
data.description: A clot in a renal vein, commonly associated with nephrotic syndrome and especially membranous nephropathy. It may extend into the inferior vena cava and cause flank pain, hematuria, worsening proteinuria, and lower-extremity edema.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings suggestive of renal/central venous thrombosis
Possible extension into the inferior vena cava
symptoms_not_in_common: Abdominal distention may be more prominent with extensive inferior vena cava obstruction or ascites than with isolated renal-vein thrombosis
Elevated TSH with low free thyroxine
Positive ANA

data.description: Kidney involvement from systemic lupus erythematosus can cause proteinuria, hematuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and nephrotic syndrome. Lupus may also increase thrombotic risk, particularly if antiphospholipid antibodies are present.
symptoms_in_common: Black woman in an age group commonly affected by systemic lupus erythematosus
Venous thrombosis can occur in lupus, especially with antiphospholipid syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, inflammatory arthritis, serositis, or cytopenias
ANA titer of 1:40 is low and nonspecific
No reported complement levels, anti-double-stranded-DNA antibodies, or antiphospholipid antibody results

data.description: An autoimmune hypercoagulable disorder characterized by arterial or venous thrombosis and/or characteristic pregnancy morbidity in the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies. It may be primary or associated with systemic lupus erythematosus.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings concerning for extensive venous thrombosis involving the inferior vena cava and pelvic/renal venous system
Progressive bilateral lower-extremity edema from venous obstruction
Abdominal and flank pain that can occur with abdominal venous thrombosis
Positive ANA, which can coexist with secondary antiphospholipid syndrome
History of pregnancy complications may warrant consideration of an autoimmune thrombophilia
symptoms_not_in_common: Proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and low total protein are more suggestive of nephrotic syndrome than isolated antiphospholipid syndrome
No documented antiphospholipid antibodies
No documented recurrent spontaneous miscarriages, arterial thrombosis, thrombocytopenia, or livedo reticularis
Hypothyroidism is not a typical defining manifestation

diagnoses.name: Membranous nephropathy
diagnoses.title: Glomerular disease associated with thin basement membrane nephropathy

data.description: A 22 year old man presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain, jaundice, itching, and fever. His urine was dark and stools pale. Physical examination revealed temperature of 38.7°C, icterus, abdominal tenderness worst in the right upper quadrant with negative Murphy's sign, impalpable gall bladder, inflamed oropharynx with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Laboratory tests showed liver function abnormalities with alkaline phosphatase 327, aspartate aminotransferase 358, and bilirubin 109 suggesting cholestasis. White cell count was elevated at 20.8, C reactive protein was raised at 17, and platelets were low at 168. Monospot test was positive for Epstein Barr virus, confirmed by positive Epstein Barr virus serology. Hepatitis A, B, and C serology were negative.
A systemic Epstein-Barr virus infection that commonly causes fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, and sometimes hepatitis with splenic enlargement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked jaundice
Dark urine
Pale stools
Prominent cholestatic liver test pattern
Severe right-upper-quadrant abdominal tenderness

data.description: An uncommon hepatic manifestation of acute Epstein-Barr virus infection in which inflammation of the liver causes predominantly cholestatic jaundice, sometimes without viral hepatitis A, B, or C.
symptoms_in_common: Negative hepatitis A, B, and C serology
symptoms_not_in_common: Inflamed oropharynx
Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Marked leukocytosis
Localized right-upper-quadrant tenderness

data.diagnosis: Acute acalculous cholecystitis associated with Epstein-Barr virus infection
data.description: Gallbladder inflammation without gallstones, which can occur during Epstein-Barr virus infection because of gallbladder wall edema and systemic inflammation. Imaging may show gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid without stones.
symptoms_in_common: Gallbladder wall edema/thickening on ultrasound and MRI
Negative Murphy's sign can occur in acalculous cholecystitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Inflamed oropharynx
Cervical lymphadenopathy
Axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot test
Splenic enlargement

data.description: A bacterial infection of the biliary tree, usually caused by obstruction such as a bile duct stone or stricture. It classically presents with fever, jaundice, and right-upper-quadrant pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: Inflamed oropharynx
Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Epstein-Barr virus serology
Possible splenic enlargement
No clear obstructing bile duct stone or ductal dilation reported on imaging

data.description: Obstruction of the common bile duct by a gallstone, producing conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and cholestasis; it may precipitate cholecystitis or cholangitis.
symptoms_in_common: Fever may occur if infection develops
symptoms_not_in_common: No gallstones reported on ultrasound or MRI
Inflamed oropharynx
Cervical lymphadenopathy
Axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot and Epstein-Barr virus serology
Possible splenic enlargement

data.description: 41-year-old man with sudden, severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the right groin and flank, slightly relieved by lying down, associated with nausea and one episode of nonbloody, nonbilious vomiting. Two weeks earlier, he had a similar but milder left lower quadrant pain radiating to the left flank that resolved spontaneously. He also reported several months of fatigue. He denied fever, weight loss, chest pain, diarrhea, and urinary symptoms. Exam showed an uncomfortable-appearing man with diffuse abdominal tenderness on deep palpation without rebound or guarding and bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness, worse on the right. Vitals: T 37.4°C, BP 188/116 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm. Labs showed leukocytosis, mild anemia, creatinine 1.5 mg/dL, elevated LDH, elevated ESR/CRP, and bland urinalysis with 1+ protein.

A necrotizing medium-vessel vasculitis that can cause renal arterial microaneurysms, stenoses, thrombosis, and renal infarctions; angiography often shows multiple small aneurysms and irregular arterial narrowing.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe flank and abdominal pain
Mild proteinuria with otherwise bland urinalysis
Elevated LDH consistent with tissue infarction
Multifocal renal infarct-like imaging abnormalities and renal arterial aneurysmal changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Nausea and a single episode of nonbloody, nonbilious vomiting

data.description: Acute ischemic necrosis of renal tissue caused by occlusion or severe narrowing of renal arterial branches, producing wedge-shaped renal perfusion defects, flank pain, hypertension, elevated LDH, and kidney dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe right lower quadrant and flank pain
Prior episode of contralateral flank pain
Renal imaging showing multifocal perfusion defects
symptoms_not_in_common: Several months of fatigue
Markedly elevated ESR and CRP, which suggest an underlying inflammatory cause rather than isolated embolic infarction

data.description: A rare noninflammatory arteriopathy involving medium-sized abdominal arteries that can cause arterial dissections, stenoses, aneurysms, thrombosis, and renal or visceral infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt severe abdominal and flank pain
Multifocal renal ischemic or infarct-like lesions
Renal arterial irregularity and aneurysmal changes on vascular imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated ESR and CRP
Leukocytosis
Several months of fatigue
Mild anemia

data.description: A nonatherosclerotic arterial disorder that causes alternating renal artery stenosis and aneurysmal dilation, often described as a string-of-beads appearance, and may lead to severe hypertension or renal ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Renal arterial aneurysmal or stenotic abnormalities on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden severe bilateral or recurrent colicky abdominal pain
Nausea and vomiting
Leukocytosis
Elevated ESR and CRP
Mild anemia
Elevated LDH suggesting acute infarction
Fatigue

data.description: A group of small-vessel autoimmune vasculitides that can cause constitutional symptoms, elevated inflammatory markers, hypertension, acute kidney injury, and glomerulonephritis; renal disease usually produces an active urinary sediment.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal or flank pain can occur with systemic vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Bland urinalysis without hematuria or red blood cell casts
Sudden severe pain radiating to the groin
Elevated LDH from apparent renal infarction
Renal arterial microaneurysms and segmental arterial abnormalities, which are more characteristic of polyarteritis nodosa
Nausea and isolated vomiting

data.description: 80-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, coronary arteriosclerosis, congestive heart failure, hyperlipidemia, and gout, emigrated from Southeast Asia 22 years earlier, admitted with anorexia, weight loss, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. On examination, he was thin and chronically ill-appearing, with tachycardia, posterior lower-lung crackles, mild abdominal tenderness, and leg edema.

data.diagnosis: Intestinal tuberculosis with disseminated tuberculosis and tuberculous aortitis
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving the ileocecal bowel, lungs, lymph nodes, and potentially the aortic wall, which can cause an infected inflammatory aneurysm.
symptoms_in_common: Southeast Asian origin, a higher-prevalence tuberculosis region
Pulmonary crackles and an upper-lung lesion on imaging
Ileocecal or right-colonic inflammatory/ulcerative lesion on imaging and endoscopy
Abdominal aortic aneurysm with surrounding inflammatory change
symptoms_not_in_common: Leg edema
Congestive heart failure
Extensive pre-existing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease

data.diagnosis: Colorectal adenocarcinoma, particularly cecal or ascending-colon cancer
data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the colon that may cause constitutional symptoms, abdominal pain, altered bowel habits, and an ulcerated colonic mass.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided colonic or ileocecal abnormality on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Upper-lung lesion, which would be atypical unless metastatic or due to a separate process
Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm
Southeast Asian origin as a specific risk factor
Posterior lower-lung crackles

data.description: Lymphoid malignancy involving the gastrointestinal tract, often affecting the ileocecal region and causing abdominal pain, weight loss, diarrhea, bowel-wall thickening, or ulceration.
symptoms_in_common: Ileocecal or right-colonic mass-like inflammatory lesion
Possible pulmonary or nodal lesion on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Abdominal aortic aneurysm with marked atherosclerotic calcification
Severe peripheral arterial disease as an explanation for the presentation
Leg edema
Posterior lower-lung crackles

data.diagnosis: Chronic mesenteric ischemia with ischemic colitis
data.description: Insufficient intestinal blood flow from severe atherosclerotic mesenteric arterial disease, producing postprandial abdominal pain, food avoidance, weight loss, diarrhea, and sometimes colonic ulceration.
symptoms_in_common: Severe atherosclerotic risk factors including diabetes, peripheral arterial disease, coronary artery disease, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia
Abdominal aortic aneurysm and extensive vascular calcification
Colonic ulceration or inflammatory bowel-wall changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Pulmonary lesion on imaging
Southeast Asian epidemiologic association
Chronically progressive systemic illness that may suggest infection or malignancy
Possible lymph-node uptake on PET imaging

data.diagnosis: Infected abdominal aortic aneurysm (mycotic aneurysm), such as Salmonella-associated aortitis
data.description: Bacterial infection of the aortic wall causing rapid aneurysmal enlargement, periaortic inflammation, abdominal or back pain, and systemic illness; older patients with atherosclerosis are at increased risk.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal aortic aneurysm with surrounding inflammatory soft-tissue change
Extensive atherosclerosis and peripheral arterial disease
Diarrhea, which can occur with enteric bacterial infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic ileocecal ulcerative lesion, which suggests a primary bowel process
Upper-lung lesion
Long-term constitutional and gastrointestinal symptoms without reported fever
Leg edema and lower-lung crackles, which are more consistent with heart failure

data.description: A 62-year-old man with chronic hepatitis C virus infection and alcohol-induced cirrhosis presented with 10 days of epigastric pain and vomiting. Laboratory findings revealed an elevated serum lipase level of 6715 U per liter (reference range 0 to 160). On hospital day five, the patient developed nodules measuring 1 cm by 1 cm that became increasingly tender over the following days.

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic panniculitis secondary to acute pancreatitis
data.description: A rare inflammatory skin manifestation caused by release of pancreatic enzymes into the bloodstream, leading to enzymatic fat necrosis in subcutaneous tissue. It classically produces tender erythematous nodules and histologic 'ghost adipocytes.'
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings consistent with acute pancreatitis
Tender 1-cm subcutaneous nodules developing after onset of pancreatitis
Histology showing lobular fat necrosis with ghost-like adipocytes
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic hepatitis C infection
Alcohol-induced cirrhosis

data.description: Acute inflammation of the pancreas, commonly caused by heavy alcohol use, characterized by abdominal pain, vomiting, and substantial elevation of pancreatic enzymes. Severe pancreatitis can cause pancreatic panniculitis.
symptoms_in_common: History of alcohol-induced cirrhosis suggesting substantial alcohol exposure
Serum lipase of 6715 U per liter
Abdominal CT findings compatible with pancreatic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Tender erythematous skin nodules are not a usual feature, although they can occur as pancreatic panniculitis
Chronic hepatitis C infection is not a typical manifestation of acute pancreatitis

data.description: A rare systemic syndrome caused by pancreatic enzyme release, most often from pancreatitis or pancreatic malignancy. It includes pancreatitis, painful panniculitic nodules from fat necrosis, and inflammatory arthritis caused by periarticular fat necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Skin biopsy features of enzymatic fat necrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No joint pain, swollen joints, or polyarthritis is described
Chronic hepatitis C infection
Alcohol-induced cirrhosis

data.description: An inflammatory panniculitis that produces painful red nodules, usually on the shins, and may be associated with infections, inflammatory bowel disease, medications, or systemic inflammatory disorders. Histology is typically septal panniculitis without vasculitis.
symptoms_in_common: Tender erythematous nodules on the lower extremities
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated serum lipase
Epigastric pain and vomiting due to acute pancreatitis
CT evidence of pancreatic inflammation
Histology showing lobular fat necrosis and ghost adipocytes rather than typical septal panniculitis
The nodules developed in close association with pancreatitis

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma with pancreatic panniculitis
data.description: A rare pancreatic tumor that can produce excessive lipase and other pancreatic enzymes, causing panniculitis with tender nodules and enzymatic fat necrosis; it may also cause pancreatitis-like abdominal symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Histologic fat necrosis with ghost adipocytes
symptoms_not_in_common: The presentation is more suggestive of acute pancreatitis than a documented pancreatic tumor
No pancreatic mass, metastatic disease, weight loss, or persistent tumor-related symptoms are described
Alcohol-related pancreatic disease provides an alternative explanation for pancreatitis

data.description: A 50-year-old man presented with a 3-week history of back pain and a skull mass that had been growing slowly for 7 months. Physical examination revealed a smooth, firm, and non-tender mass on his skull that gave him the appearance of having a high domed forehead. Laboratory investigations showed renal impairment, hypercalcaemia, anaemia, and immunoparesis. Lambda light chains were detected in both urine and serum. Bone marrow aspirate showed a low level infiltration of plasma cells, though the patient could not tolerate a bone marrow biopsy. A biopsy of the thoracic lesion revealed a monomorphic population of plasma cells that were strongly positive for CD138 and lambda light chain restricted.
A malignant clonal plasma-cell disorder causing monoclonal light-chain production, bone lesions, anaemia, renal dysfunction, hypercalcaemia, and focal plasmacytomas.
symptoms_in_common: Lambda light chains in serum and urine
Thoracic lesion composed of CD138-positive lambda-restricted plasma cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Low level of plasma-cell infiltration on marrow aspirate despite extensive clinical features

data.description: A less common variant of multiple myeloma characterized by multiple lytic bone or soft-tissue plasma-cell lesions with relatively low marrow plasma-cell involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Back pain suggestive of skeletal involvement
Skull mass consistent with a focal osseous plasmacytoma
Low level plasma-cell infiltration in the bone marrow aspirate
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked immunoparesis may be less prominent in some macrofocal cases

data.description: A plasma-cell neoplasm with more than one localized bone or extramedullary plasmacytoma, potentially representing an early or marrow-sparse form of systemic myeloma.
symptoms_in_common: Thoracic lesion containing monomorphic plasma cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcaemia
Renal impairment
Anaemia
Immunoparesis
Detectable serum and urine lambda light chains

data.diagnosis: Solitary osseous plasmacytoma of the skull
data.description: A localized collection of neoplastic plasma cells arising in a single bone, commonly causing a painless enlarging mass; it can progress to multiple myeloma.
symptoms_in_common: Plasma-cell neoplasm demonstrated by CD138-positive lambda-restricted cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Back pain with a separate thoracic lesion
Renal impairment
Hypercalcaemia
Anaemia
Immunoparesis
Lambda light chains in both serum and urine
Bone marrow plasma-cell infiltration

data.diagnosis: Metastatic plasma-cell neoplasm with extramedullary disease
data.description: Systemic plasma-cell myeloma may form destructive bone masses and extend into adjacent soft tissues, including the skull and thoracic skeleton.
symptoms_not_in_common: The skull lesion was described as slowly growing over several months rather than rapidly progressive
Only low-level marrow plasma-cell infiltration was identified

data.description: A 13-year-old male presented with pain in the right hypochondrium and loss of appetite for 1 month. There was no history of fever. The patient has a history of a successfully treated abdominal tuberculosis, for which he had taken anti-tubercular treatment for 1 year.
Tuberculous infection of the liver can produce single or multiple focal hypodense lesions (tuberculomas or microabscesses), particularly in patients with prior abdominal tuberculosis.
symptoms_in_common: History of previously treated abdominal tuberculosis
Multiple focal liver lesions on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever

data.description: Bacterial infection of the liver may cause one or multiple focal hepatic abscesses, usually associated with abdominal pain, systemic illness, fever, and inflammatory laboratory abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No reported chills or toxic systemic illness
One-month relatively indolent course

data.description: Lymphoma may involve the liver as solitary or multiple hypodense lesions and can cause abdominal pain, anorexia, hepatomegaly, and constitutional symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever
No reported weight loss or night sweats
Prior abdominal tuberculosis is not typical of lymphoma

data.description: Primary hepatic malignancies can present as focal or multifocal liver masses with abdominal pain, anorexia, and liver enlargement; hepatoblastoma is much more common in younger children, while hepatocellular carcinoma may occur in older children with chronic liver disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 13 years is atypical for hepatoblastoma
No known chronic liver disease or hepatitis
No reported abdominal mass, jaundice, or weight loss
History of treated abdominal tuberculosis is not typical

data.description: An inflammatory pseudotumor is a benign but mass-forming inflammatory lesion of the liver that can mimic malignancy or infection and may occur in children and adolescents.
symptoms_in_common: Mass-like focal liver lesions on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No reported elevated inflammatory symptoms
History of abdominal tuberculosis is not specifically typical

data.description: A man in his 70s with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and mild aortic stenosis presented with altered mental status, acute kidney injury requiring dialysis, and painful, dusky skin discoloration on his distal extremities. Three weeks prior to presentation, he had undergone coronary angiography and coronary artery bypass graft surgery after myocardial infarction. Laboratory examination revealed a white blood cell count of 9100/μL with 22% eosinophils, blood urea nitrogen level of 70 mg/dL (25 mmol/L), and creatinine level of 6.1 mg/dL (539.2 μmol/L). Urinalysis showed 1+ blood and 2+ protein.

data.diagnosis: Cholesterol crystal embolization syndrome (atheroembolic renal disease)
data.description: Embolization of cholesterol crystals from disrupted aortic or arterial atherosclerotic plaques, often after angiography, vascular surgery, or anticoagulation. It commonly causes acute or subacute kidney failure, eosinophilia, and painful blue or purple distal digits with preserved large-vessel pulses.
symptoms_in_common: Presentation approximately 3 weeks after coronary angiography and CABG surgery
Painful dusky purple discoloration of toes and fingers consistent with blue toe syndrome
Peripheral skin lesions with livedoid or ischemic appearance
Known severe atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and recent myocardial infarction
Altered mental status, which may occur with systemic embolization or severe uremia
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly atypical symptoms; the clinical timing and findings are highly characteristic

data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can cause renal ischemia, hypertension, skin nodules, livedo reticularis, digital ischemia, neuropathy, and systemic inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Painful distal digital ischemia and dusky skin discoloration
Altered mental status could result from severe hypertension, uremia, or central nervous system vascular involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset shortly after coronary angiography and CABG strongly favors cholesterol embolization instead
Marked eosinophilia is not a classic feature
Hematuria and proteinuria are less typical because polyarteritis nodosa usually spares glomeruli
No reported fever, weight loss, abdominal pain, mononeuritis multiplex, or myalgias

data.diagnosis: ANCA-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis)
data.description: A small-vessel necrotizing vasculitis that commonly produces rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and may cause purpura, systemic inflammation, pulmonary disease, and neurologic manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Hematuria and proteinuria suggesting renal inflammatory injury
Skin lesions that could be interpreted as purpura or ischemic vasculitic lesions
Altered mental status in the setting of severe renal failure
symptoms_not_in_common: Painful blue/purple toes and fingers after an arterial procedure are more typical of cholesterol emboli than small-vessel vasculitis
Marked eosinophilia is not typical of granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis
No reported pulmonary hemorrhage, cough, sinus disease, nasal ulcers, otitis, or constitutional symptoms
No report of active urinary sediment such as red blood cell casts

data.description: An immune-mediated inflammatory injury of the renal interstitium, commonly triggered by medications such as antibiotics, proton-pump inhibitors, NSAIDs, or other drugs. It can cause acute kidney injury, pyuria, mild proteinuria, hematuria, and eosinophilia.
symptoms_in_common: Recent hospitalization and surgery, which may involve exposure to multiple medications
symptoms_not_in_common: Painful dusky ischemic discoloration of distal fingers and toes is not typical
The close relationship to coronary angiography and vascular surgery favors atheroembolism
No reported fever, diffuse drug rash, arthralgias, pyuria, or eosinophiluria
Acute digital ischemia cannot be explained by isolated interstitial nephritis

data.description: Infection of a cardiac valve or endocardial surface that may produce emboli to the brain, kidneys, and peripheral arteries, causing altered mental status, renal injury, and painful ischemic digits or other skin findings.
symptoms_in_common: Altered mental status, potentially from cerebral emboli or severe systemic illness
Acute kidney injury with hematuria and proteinuria
Painful distal ischemic lesions of the fingers and toes from embolic disease
Recent major cardiac surgery, which increases risk for healthcare-associated infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever, heart murmur change, positive blood cultures, or systemic infectious syndrome
Marked eosinophilia is not typical of infective endocarditis
The delayed onset after angiography with blue toe-type lesions strongly favors cholesterol embolization
No described splinter hemorrhages, Janeway lesions, Osler nodes, or valve vegetations

data.description: A 79-year-old man with a history of hypertension, stroke, and glaucoma was brought to the emergency department after being found unresponsive by a caregiver. He was cold to the touch with vital signs showing blood pressure of 85/55 mm Hg, heart rate of 36/min, respiratory rate of 14/min, and pulse oximetry of 100% on ambient air. Multiple temperature measurements, including core temperature assessment via rectal method, did not yield a detectable temperature. Physical examination revealed clear bilateral chest auscultation. Chest radiographs and computed tomography of the head were negative for any acute pathology.
A life-threatening reduction in core body temperature, often causing depressed consciousness, bradycardia, hypotension, and characteristic J (Osborn) waves on ECG.
symptoms_in_common: Undetectable core temperature by rectal measurement
ECG findings consistent with prominent J (Osborn) waves
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal oxygen saturation of 100% on ambient air
Clear bilateral chest examination

data.description: A severe, decompensated form of hypothyroidism characterized by altered mental status, hypothermia, bradycardia, hypotension, and hypoventilation.
symptoms_not_in_common: No known history of hypothyroidism
No reported dry skin, coarse hair, facial puffiness, constipation, or weight gain
Normal respiratory rate and oxygen saturation
J waves are more specifically suggestive of hypothermia than hypothyroidism itself

data.description: Severe infection causing circulatory failure and altered mental status; elderly patients may become hypothermic rather than febrile.
symptoms_in_common: Unresponsiveness or severely altered mental status
Hypothermia can occur in severe sepsis, particularly in older adults
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked bradycardia rather than the more typical tachycardia
No fever reported
Clear lung examination
Negative chest radiograph for acute pulmonary infection
No described infectious source or systemic inflammatory symptoms
ECG J waves favor severe hypothermia

data.description: Acute adrenal insufficiency causing severe hypotension, weakness, confusion or coma, and sometimes hypothermia, usually precipitated by illness or physiologic stress.
symptoms_in_common: Bradycardia can occur in severe metabolic decompensation
symptoms_not_in_common: No known history of adrenal insufficiency or chronic steroid use
No reported abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, or hyperpigmentation
No electrolyte abnormalities or hypoglycemia provided
ECG J waves are not typical of adrenal crisis itself

data.diagnosis: Beta-blocker or other rate-limiting medication toxicity
data.description: Toxicity from beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers, digoxin, or similar agents can cause profound bradycardia, hypotension, and depressed consciousness.
symptoms_in_common: History of hypertension, which may involve treatment with rate-limiting medications
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound undetectable body temperature is not typical
Cold skin and hypothermia-associated J waves favor hypothermia as the primary process
No medication ingestion, overdose history, or characteristic toxidrome described
No reported hypoglycemia, bronchospasm, or conduction block beyond bradycardia

data.description: 34-year-old man previously well, presented with generalized tonic-clonic seizure and transient right-sided weakness, with recurrent hemoptysis for 1 month. Exam and labs showed normal renal ultrasound, hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL, normal WBC, normal complement, normal creatinine, and urinalysis without proteinuria but with a few old red blood cells. Anti-GBM, ANCA, dsDNA, and anti-smooth muscle antibodies were negative. Bronchoscopy cultures, viral serology, and echocardiography were negative. Immunofluorescence showed linear and granular IgG deposits in lung and renal tissues.

data.diagnosis: Seronegative anti-glomerular basement membrane disease (seronegative Goodpasture syndrome)
data.description: An autoimmune pulmonary-renal syndrome caused by antibodies targeting basement-membrane components, sometimes with negative circulating anti-GBM testing. It commonly produces diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis; linear IgG staining along basement membranes is characteristic.
symptoms_in_common: CT findings compatible with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
Microscopic hematuria with old red blood cells in urine
Linear IgG deposits in lung and renal tissues
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized tonic-clonic seizure
Transient right-sided weakness
Normal creatinine
Absence of proteinuria
Negative serum anti-GBM antibody test

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
data.description: A multisystem immune-complex autoimmune disease that can cause diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, lupus nephritis, seizures, and focal neurologic deficits. Renal immunofluorescence usually shows granular immune-complex deposition rather than isolated linear IgG staining.
symptoms_in_common: Hemoptysis consistent with possible diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
Granular IgG deposits in renal and lung tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative anti-dsDNA antibodies
Normal complement levels
Male sex
No proteinuria
Normal creatinine
Prominent linear IgG deposition

data.description: An ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis that may cause pulmonary capillaritis with hemoptysis and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. Neurologic involvement can occur, but tissue immunofluorescence is usually pauci-immune rather than IgG-positive.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary imaging compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
Possible neurologic involvement with seizure and transient weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative ANCA testing
Linear and granular IgG deposits in lung and renal tissue
No reported chronic sinus, nasal, or ear disease
No reported pulmonary nodules or cavitary lesions
Normal creatinine and absent proteinuria

data.description: A rare disorder characterized by recurrent diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, iron-deficiency anemia, and pulmonary hemosiderin deposition, without an identifiable systemic vasculitis or anti-GBM antibody. Renal disease is generally absent.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse pulmonary ground-glass-type imaging abnormalities compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
Negative bronchoscopy cultures and viral studies
symptoms_not_in_common: Microscopic hematuria
Linear and granular IgG deposits in renal tissue
Generalized tonic-clonic seizure
Transient right-sided weakness
Evidence suggesting renal basement-membrane immune involvement

data.diagnosis: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system with pulmonary hemorrhage from systemic small-vessel vasculitis
data.description: Inflammatory vasculitis affecting small cerebral vessels can cause seizures and transient focal deficits. If part of an occult systemic vasculitic syndrome, pulmonary capillaritis and renal urinary abnormalities may also occur.
symptoms_in_common: Brain MRI abnormalities potentially compatible with inflammatory or vascular CNS involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Primary CNS vasculitis does not usually cause hemoptysis
Primary CNS vasculitis does not usually cause renal IgG deposits
Linear IgG staining is more characteristic of anti-GBM disease
No reported angiographic or biopsy confirmation of cerebral vasculitis
Normal renal function and no proteinuria

data.description: 30-year-old Hispanic male with history of heavy NSAID use. Presented with melena and severe abdominal pain for 3 weeks, with similar but milder symptoms over prior 4-5 months. Initial hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume 78 fL. Later endorsed having a right swollen testicle (initially missed on previous exams). Physical exam revealed nontender enlarged right testicle. Laboratory markers showed: human chorionic gonadotropin 50 mIU/mL (normal <10), α-fetoprotein 1,990 ng/mL (normal <8), lactate dehydrogenase 534 IU/L (range 25-175).

data.diagnosis: Metastatic mixed nonseminomatous testicular germ cell tumor
data.description: A testicular cancer containing one or more nonseminomatous components, commonly embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma, or teratoma. It can metastasize through retroperitoneal lymph nodes to the gastrointestinal tract and cause ulceration and bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Iron-deficiency pattern anemia with hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL and low MCV
Imaging findings consistent with abdominal/retroperitoneal metastatic disease and bowel involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Heavy NSAID use is not a typical cause of germ cell tumor, although it could independently contribute to ulcer disease

data.diagnosis: Testicular embryonal carcinoma with gastrointestinal metastasis
data.description: Embryonal carcinoma is an aggressive nonseminomatous germ cell tumor of the testis that commonly occurs in young adult men and may produce AFP and/or hCG. It frequently spreads early to retroperitoneal lymph nodes and can involve the gastrointestinal tract.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain from retroperitoneal or gastrointestinal metastases
Melena and severe anemia due to bleeding gastrointestinal metastatic lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Several months of milder dyspeptic or abdominal symptoms before presentation is less specific for embryonal carcinoma
Heavy NSAID exposure is not typical of embryonal carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Testicular yolk sac tumor with metastatic gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: A yolk sac tumor is a nonseminomatous testicular germ cell tumor characterized by substantial AFP production. In adults it often occurs as part of a mixed germ cell tumor and may metastasize to retroperitoneal nodes and distant organs.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain associated with metastatic disease
Melena and anemia from gastrointestinal tumor involvement or ulceration
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated human chorionic gonadotropin is not typical of a pure yolk sac tumor, though it can occur in a mixed germ cell tumor
Heavy NSAID use is not typical of yolk sac tumor

data.diagnosis: Testicular choriocarcinoma or a mixed germ cell tumor containing choriocarcinoma
data.description: Choriocarcinoma is a highly vascular nonseminomatous germ cell tumor that can metastasize hematogenously and cause prominent bleeding, including gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Pure choriocarcinoma usually produces markedly high hCG.
symptoms_in_common: Melena due to a hemorrhagic gastrointestinal lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: The hCG level of 50 mIU/mL is much lower than is usual for pure choriocarcinoma
Marked alpha-fetoprotein elevation is not expected in pure choriocarcinoma and suggests a mixed tumor with a yolk sac component
Heavy NSAID use is not typical of choriocarcinoma

data.diagnosis: NSAID-induced peptic ulcer disease with upper gastrointestinal bleeding
data.description: Frequent NSAID use can cause gastric or duodenal mucosal injury and peptic ulcers, leading to epigastric pain, melena, and iron-deficiency anemia. This may explain the initial gastrointestinal presentation but does not account for the tumor-marker pattern or testicular mass.
symptoms_in_common: Low mean corpuscular volume consistent with blood-loss iron deficiency
Endoscopic ulcerated and bleeding-appearing gastrointestinal lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Nontender enlarged right testicle
Marked elevation of alpha-fetoprotein
Elevated human chorionic gonadotropin
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase
Abdominal imaging findings suggestive of metastatic retroperitoneal disease

data.description: 55-year-old man with heart failure and a history of obesity, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and smoking presented with 3 days of sudden, progressively worsening pain and swelling of the right foot, calf, and upper leg without trauma. On the day of presentation, he developed dusky discoloration of the right toes. Exam showed hypotension (96/50 mmHg), marked asymmetric leg swelling with 4+ pitting edema of the right upper thigh and 2+ pitting edema of the left calf, and the right leg/foot was dusky and cold with distal pulses detectable only by Doppler.
A severe form of extensive deep venous thrombosis causing near-total venous outflow obstruction, massive edema, cyanosis, arterial compromise, and risk of venous gangrene.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden progressively worsening unilateral right leg pain
Marked asymmetric swelling of the right foot, calf, and thigh
Severe pitting edema of the right upper thigh
Dusky or cyanotic discoloration of the toes and foot
Distal pulses detectable only by Doppler
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild pitting edema of the left calf
History of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation

data.diagnosis: Extensive acute iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis
data.description: Acute thrombus involving the deep veins of the thigh and pelvis, producing unilateral limb pain, swelling, venous congestion, and potentially progressing to phlegmasia cerulea dolens.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly progressive swelling involving the foot, calf, and upper thigh
Dusky discoloration from severe venous congestion
Obesity and heart failure as thrombotic risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: Cold limb with markedly impaired distal pulses
Severe toe ischemia or threatened gangrene
Hypotension

data.diagnosis: Acute arterial limb ischemia due to arterial embolism
data.description: Sudden interruption of arterial blood flow to a limb, often caused by embolization from atrial fibrillation, leading to pain, pallor or cyanosis, coldness, pulselessness, sensory loss, and possible tissue necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Distal pulses detectable only by Doppler
Smoking and hypertension as vascular risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: Massive swelling of the entire right leg
Marked 4+ pitting edema of the upper thigh
Progressive edema over several days
Contralateral calf edema

data.description: A limb-threatening condition in which increased pressure within a fascial compartment compromises tissue perfusion, causing severe pain, swelling, neurologic deficits, and late pulselessness or cyanosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No trauma, fracture, crush injury, or recent limb procedure
Prominent pitting edema rather than tense compartment swelling
Swelling extending from foot through upper thigh
No reported pain with passive stretch
No reported paresthesias or motor weakness

data.diagnosis: Occult gastric adenocarcinoma with cancer-associated thrombosis (Trousseau syndrome)
data.description: Gastric adenocarcinoma can produce a hypercoagulable state that predisposes to extensive venous thrombosis; the abdominal imaging, endoscopic mass, and histology are consistent with an underlying gastric malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe unilateral leg swelling consistent with thrombotic disease
No trauma preceding the thrombotic event
Imaging and endoscopic appearance of a gastric mass
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported abdominal pain
No reported weight loss
No reported nausea or vomiting
No reported gastrointestinal bleeding or anemia symptoms
Cold dusky foot and impaired pulses are consequences of severe limb thrombosis rather than typical direct symptoms of gastric cancer
