diagnoses.title: Adenocarcinoma of stomach

data.description: 76-year-old man from the Indian subcontinent presented with fever and priapism. Physical exam showed painful, engorged penis with intact skin, no lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, or splenomegaly. No skin rash or nodules were found.

data.diagnosis: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma with penile involvement
data.description: A rare aggressive extranodal lymphoma in which malignant large B cells proliferate mainly within small blood vessels. It commonly causes fever and may lack lymphadenopathy or organ enlargement; penile vascular involvement can cause ischemic priapism.
symptoms_in_common: FDG-avid penile/pelvic abnormality on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Intact penile skin without rash or nodules

data.diagnosis: Primary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the penis
data.description: An uncommon extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma involving penile erectile tissue. It can infiltrate the corpora cavernosa and impair venous drainage, producing painful priapism.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of palpable lymphadenopathy can occur in localized disease
Absence of skin lesions can occur when disease is confined to deeper penile tissues
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable penile mass or ulceration described
No inguinal lymphadenopathy

data.diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukemia or other myeloproliferative neoplasm causing leukostasis
data.description: Myeloproliferative blood cancers can produce marked leukocytosis and hyperviscosity, leading to sludging in the corpora cavernosa and ischemic priapism.
symptoms_in_common: Fever may occur with hematologic malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: No splenomegaly
No hepatomegaly
No lymphadenopathy
Advanced age is less typical for initial presentation with priapism

data.diagnosis: Penile metastasis from prostate, bladder, colorectal, or other pelvic malignancy
data.description: Secondary spread of a pelvic or systemic cancer to the penis can obstruct venous or lymphatic drainage and cause malignant priapism, often with deep corporal infiltration.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic and penile FDG uptake on imaging
Fever can occur in advanced malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary malignancy described
No penile nodule, ulcer, or skin lesion
No lymphadenopathy

data.diagnosis: Penile tuberculosis or granulomatous infection involving the corpora cavernosa
data.description: Tuberculosis and other granulomatous infections can involve genitourinary structures and produce fever and inflammatory penile disease, although priapism from corporal involvement is rare.
symptoms_in_common: Origin from the Indian subcontinent, where tuberculosis is more prevalent
Painful penile swelling or engorgement can occur with local inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Priapism is uncommon
No penile ulcer, sinus tract, rash, or nodules
No lymphadenopathy
No hepatosplenomegaly

data.description: 50-year-old postmenopausal woman with 1 year of menopause presented with abdominal distention, anorexia, and exertional dyspnea. Exam showed a markedly distended abdomen. CT and MRI demonstrated gross ascites and a heterogeneous left adnexal/pelvic mass with enhancing solid components and thick septa, small calcifications along the cystic wall, and no lymphadenopathy, peritoneal dissemination, or fatty component. Serum CA 125 was markedly elevated at 1237 U/ml; CEA, CA 19-9, and SCC were normal. Repeated paracentesis showed benign mesothelial cells without malignant cells. Thyroid function tests were normal, and there were no symptoms or signs of thyroid dysfunction.

A rare monodermal ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of thyroid tissue. It can cause ascites, pleural effusion, and marked CA-125 elevation despite being benign; thyroid function is often normal.
symptoms_in_common: Postmenopausal adnexal/pelvic mass with solid and cystic components
Gross ascites causing marked abdominal distention
Exertional dyspnea, consistent with pleural effusion
Benign mesothelial cells and no malignant cells in ascitic fluid
Normal thyroid function tests, which are common in struma ovarii
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear fatty component typical of a conventional mature cystic teratoma
Anorexia is nonspecific and not a classic presenting feature

data.description: A malignant ovarian epithelial tumor, particularly high-grade serous carcinoma, commonly presents with an adnexal mass, ascites, abdominal symptoms, and elevated CA-125.
symptoms_in_common: Complex left adnexal mass with enhancing solid components and thick septa
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeated ascitic-fluid cytology showed no malignant cells
No peritoneal dissemination
No lymphadenopathy
No obvious metastatic disease on imaging
Small wall calcifications are not specific for high-grade epithelial ovarian carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Ovarian fibroma or fibrothecoma with Meigs syndrome
data.description: A benign ovarian sex-cord stromal tumor that may be associated with ascites and pleural effusion, known as Meigs syndrome. CA-125 can rise substantially because of peritoneal and pleural irritation.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional dyspnea compatible with pleural effusion
Elevated CA-125 despite benign ascitic cytology
symptoms_not_in_common: The mass is heterogeneous with cystic areas, thick septa, and wall calcifications rather than a predominantly solid fibrous ovarian mass
Enhancing solid components within a complex cystic lesion are less typical
CA-125 of 1237 U/ml is possible but relatively unusual in uncomplicated Meigs syndrome

data.diagnosis: Granulosa cell tumor of the ovary
data.description: A sex-cord stromal ovarian tumor that may be solid and cystic and can occur around menopause. Some tumors produce estrogen and cause endometrial stimulation or postmenopausal bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral complex adnexal mass with solid and cystic components
Abdominal distention from a large pelvic mass and ascites
symptoms_not_in_common: No postmenopausal vaginal bleeding or other estrogen-excess manifestations
Marked CA-125 elevation is not typical
Massive ascites and pleural effusion are less characteristic
No reported endometrial thickening or uterine abnormality

data.diagnosis: Metastatic ovarian malignancy (Krukenberg tumor or other metastatic tumor)
data.description: Secondary ovarian involvement by a gastrointestinal, breast, or other primary cancer can produce complex ovarian masses, ascites, and elevated CA-125.
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is unilateral rather than the commonly bilateral pattern of many ovarian metastases
CEA and CA 19-9 are normal
No known gastrointestinal or other primary malignancy
No lymphadenopathy or peritoneal metastatic implants
Repeated ascitic cytology did not show malignant cells

data.description: A 32 year-old male presented to his primary care provider with unremitting neck pain. He denied any history of trauma. The patient was unresponsive to conservative therapy and plain-film radiographic evaluation was negative. Patient was subsequently referred for a cervical spine MR for further evaluation.

data.diagnosis: Primary osseous lymphoma of the cervical spine
data.description: A malignant lymphoid tumor arising in bone that may produce extensive marrow replacement and a large paraspinal or epidural soft-tissue component while early plain radiographs remain normal.
symptoms_in_common: Failure to improve with conservative treatment
Negative plain-film radiographs despite clinically significant symptoms
MRI appearance of infiltrative cervical vertebral marrow and adjacent soft-tissue abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as fever, night sweats, or weight loss were reported
No neurologic deficits were reported

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the spine causing vertebral marrow destruction, paravertebral or prevertebral inflammatory soft tissue, and possible epidural extension; early radiographs can be unrevealing.
symptoms_in_common: Poor response to routine conservative therapy
MRI findings concerning for destructive cervical vertebral and prevertebral soft-tissue disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss, or pulmonary symptoms were reported
No known tuberculosis exposure or immunosuppression was reported
No neurologic symptoms were reported

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic cervical discitis-osteomyelitis with epidural or prevertebral phlegmon
data.description: Bacterial infection involving vertebral endplates and intervertebral discs that can extend into prevertebral tissues or the epidural space, causing persistent focal spinal pain and potential cord compression.
symptoms_in_common: MRI evidence of cervical spinal marrow and adjacent soft-tissue abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or systemic illness was reported
No history of bacteremia, intravenous drug use, recent surgery, or immunosuppression was provided
No reported neurologic deficit
Plain radiographs may eventually show endplate/disc changes, although they can be negative early

data.diagnosis: Chordoma involving the clivus and upper cervical spine
data.description: A rare slow-growing malignant tumor derived from notochordal remnants, usually centered in the midline clivus or sacrum; skull-base lesions can extend into the upper cervical region and cause pain.
symptoms_in_common: MRI showing a midline skull-base/upper cervical destructive soft-tissue process
symptoms_not_in_common: Chordoma more often produces headache, diplopia, cranial neuropathies, dysphagia, or other skull-base symptoms, none of which were reported
The described extensive multilevel cervical marrow involvement is less typical than a single focal midline osseous lesion
No neurologic deficits were reported

data.diagnosis: Metastatic malignancy involving the cervical spine
data.description: Secondary malignant involvement of vertebral marrow, which can cause persistent pain, pathologic fracture, epidural disease, or paraspinal soft-tissue extension; MRI is more sensitive than radiographs early in disease.
symptoms_in_common: Normal or nondiagnostic plain radiographs can occur early
MRI appearance of abnormal vertebral marrow with associated soft-tissue disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary cancer was reported
Age 32 is younger than the usual age for most metastatic cancers
No weight loss, fatigue, or other systemic cancer symptoms were reported
No neurologic deficits were reported

data.description: A 13-month-old male infant presented to the Department of Dermatology with a single asymptomatic plaque on the lower back that was first noticed by parents at approximately 4 months of age. During observation, the lesion gradually became larger and firmer, and intermittent sweating on the surface was noticed.

A benign developmental overgrowth of arrector pili smooth muscle in the skin, usually present at birth or early infancy and often occurring on the trunk or lumbosacral region. It may appear as a skin-colored or hyperpigmented plaque, sometimes with increased hair growth or sweating.
symptoms_in_common: Solitary plaque on the lower back
Gradual enlargement as the child grows
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion was first noticed at approximately 4 months rather than clearly at birth
No reported hypertrichosis or hyperpigmentation
No reported pseudo-Darier sign or transient piloerection with rubbing

data.description: A rare benign hamartoma characterized by increased or enlarged eccrine sweat glands. It usually presents in childhood as a localized skin-colored plaque or nodule with focal hyperhidrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Localized intermittent sweating on the plaque
symptoms_not_in_common: Lower-back location is less common than extremity involvement
Marked firmness is less characteristic
No report of sweating being triggered by heat, stress, or exercise

data.description: A benign congenital or childhood-onset hamartoma composed of eccrine sweat glands and vascular structures. It commonly presents as a slowly enlarging plaque or nodule and may cause localized hyperhidrosis, pain, or color change.
symptoms_in_common: Usually benign and without systemic symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is asymptomatic, whereas pain or tenderness is common
No bluish, red, violaceous, or brown discoloration is described
Lower-back involvement is less typical than distal extremity involvement

data.description: A benign, poorly circumscribed fibrous and fatty soft-tissue tumor that develops during the first two years of life. It often presents as a painless, firm, progressively enlarging subcutaneous mass on the trunk or upper extremities.
symptoms_in_common: Presentation during the first year of life
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent localized sweating is not typical
The lesion is described primarily as a plaque rather than a subcutaneous mass
No rapid growth or large bulky mass is reported

data.description: A benign cutaneous hamartoma caused by excess collagen, elastin, or other dermal connective tissue. It presents as a firm skin-colored plaque, often on the trunk, and may become more noticeable as the child grows.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of pain or other symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Localized intermittent sweating is not typical
Presentation in early infancy is less characteristic for many connective tissue nevi
No associated systemic findings or features of tuberous sclerosis are described

data.description: A 15-year-old boy presented with recent onset of breathlessness, weight loss, and tiredness for two months and a crusting erythematous scalp rash for six months. The investigations revealed neutrophilia, raised C-reactive protein (CRP), and Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT). The blood urea and electrolytes, thyroid function tests, anti-nuclear antibodies, and clotting studies were normal

data.diagnosis: SAPHO syndrome (synovitis, acne, pustulosis, hyperostosis, osteitis)
data.description: An autoinflammatory osteoarticular syndrome characterized by sterile osteitis/hyperostosis, often involving the anterior chest wall, together with severe acne, pustulosis, or other inflammatory skin disease. Pulmonary inflammatory involvement and bronchiectasis are uncommon but reported.
symptoms_in_common: Crusting erythematous scalp rash consistent with an inflammatory acneiform/pustular skin disorder
Raised CRP and neutrophilia indicating systemic inflammation
Imaging evidence of sternal/anterior chest-wall bony abnormality compatible with osteitis or hyperostosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Weight loss is not a defining feature
Raised ALT is not typical
Bronchiectasis is an unusual manifestation of SAPHO syndrome

data.description: An inherited CFTR-related disorder causing thick airway secretions, recurrent respiratory infection, upper-lobe-predominant bronchiectasis, nutritional problems, and possible liver disease.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral cystic bronchiectasis, including upper-lung involvement
Neutrophilia and elevated CRP, which may occur with pulmonary infection or exacerbation
Raised ALT, which can occur with CF-associated liver involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Crusting erythematous scalp rash is not typical
Sternal osteitis/hyperostosis-type imaging abnormality is not typical
No chronic productive cough, recurrent childhood chest infections, pancreatic symptoms, or malabsorption are reported

data.diagnosis: Primary immunodeficiency with recurrent sinopulmonary infection (such as common variable immunodeficiency)
data.description: Antibody or combined immune deficiencies can cause recurrent bacterial respiratory infections leading to chronic bronchiectasis, systemic inflammation, fatigue, and weight loss.
symptoms_in_common: Neutrophilia and raised CRP compatible with active or recurrent bacterial airway infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Crusting erythematous scalp rash is not a typical defining feature
Sternal hyperostosis or sterile osteitis is not typical
Raised ALT is not a usual primary manifestation
No history of recurrent infections, chronic diarrhea, or opportunistic infection is provided

data.description: A genetic disorder of impaired mucociliary clearance that causes recurrent airway infection and bronchiectasis, often beginning in childhood and frequently associated with chronic sinus or ear disease.
symptoms_in_common: Neutrophilia and elevated CRP that can accompany airway infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Crusting erythematous scalp rash is not typical
Weight loss is not a classic presenting feature
Raised ALT is not typical
Sternal osteitis/hyperostosis is not typical
No neonatal respiratory distress, chronic rhinitis, otitis, hearing problems, or situs abnormality is reported

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can produce constitutional symptoms and chronic upper-lung disease; longstanding infection can lead to bronchiectasis and fibrotic or cavitary lung destruction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse bilateral cystic bronchiectasis without described cavitation or focal consolidation is less typical for active tuberculosis
Neutrophilia is less characteristic than lymphocyte-predominant or variable inflammatory findings
Crusting erythematous scalp rash is not typical
Sternal hyperostosis/sterile osteitis-type appearance is not typical
Raised ALT is not a typical untreated presentation

diagnoses.name: Pulmonary involvement in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
diagnoses.title: Adult pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis

diagnoses.name: Skeletal involvement in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
diagnoses.title: Langerhans cell histiocytosis

data.description: A 40-year-old woman presented with a palpable lump in her left superior breast. Mammography and US and biopsy performed, confirming invasive carcinoma NST Grade 2. MRI performed pre-operatively due to occult on mammography. Subsequent left breast mastectomy and reconstruction with right breast mastopexy.

data.diagnosis: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (NST), grade 2
data.description: The most common form of invasive breast cancer, arising from breast ducts and infiltrating surrounding breast tissue. This diagnosis was confirmed on biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable lump in the left superior breast
Irregular hypoechoic breast mass on ultrasound
Marked enhancing mass on contrast-enhanced breast MRI
Mammographically occult lesion in dense breast tissue
Biopsy confirmation of invasive carcinoma NST, grade 2
symptoms_not_in_common: No breast pain, nipple discharge, skin retraction, or inflammatory skin changes were reported

data.diagnosis: Multifocal or multicentric invasive breast carcinoma
data.description: Breast cancer involving more than one distinct tumor focus in the same breast, which may be in the same quadrant or in different quadrants. MRI is particularly useful for defining the full extent of disease.
symptoms_in_common: Large irregular enhancing left breast abnormality on MRI
MRI performed because the lesion was occult or incompletely assessed on mammography
Treatment with mastectomy, which may be selected when disease extent is broad or multifocal
symptoms_not_in_common: Separate tumor foci were not explicitly confirmed in the provided biopsy description
No definite additional malignant lesion in another quadrant was described

data.diagnosis: Invasive ductal carcinoma with possible internal mammary nodal metastasis
data.description: Invasive breast carcinoma can spread to regional lymph nodes, including axillary and internal mammary nodes. A suspicious enhancing parasternal/internal mammary focus on MRI can represent nodal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing primary breast mass on MRI
Small enhancing focus in the parasternal/internal mammary region indicated on MRI images
symptoms_not_in_common: Pathologic confirmation of lymph-node metastasis was not provided
No axillary lymphadenopathy or systemic metastatic symptoms were reported

data.description: A common benign fibroepithelial breast tumor that often presents as a palpable breast lump, particularly in younger women. It is usually circumscribed and noninvasive on imaging and pathology.
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy showed invasive carcinoma rather than a benign fibroepithelial lesion
The imaging appearance is described as suspicious/irregular rather than a typical well-circumscribed oval mass
Strong suspicious enhancement on MRI is less typical
Mastectomy for confirmed malignancy is not typical management for fibroadenoma

data.description: A fibroepithelial breast neoplasm that can be benign, borderline, or malignant and often presents as a rapidly enlarging palpable mass. It can be difficult to distinguish from fibroadenoma without tissue diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Breast lesion visible on ultrasound and MRI
Can occur in women around 40 to 50 years of age
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy established invasive carcinoma NST rather than a fibroepithelial tumor
No rapid enlargement was reported
The MRI appearance and management are being interpreted in the setting of biopsy-proven invasive carcinoma
Possible regional nodal concern is less characteristic because phyllodes tumors usually spread hematogenously rather than through lymph nodes

data.description: A 68-year-old woman with a longstanding history of non-specific inflammatory arthritis presented with a three-month history of flashing lights and blurred vision. She had been taking 400 mg hydroxychloroquine daily for 15 years, along with meloxicam, omeprazole, and amitriptyline. She was of normal body weight. Ophthalmological assessment revealed reduced visual acuity at 6/18 in the right eye and 6/12 in the left eye, with mild depression in color vision on Ishihara plate testing. Early cataracts were present.

A toxic maculopathy caused by cumulative hydroxychloroquine exposure, characterized by parafoveal photoreceptor and retinal pigment epithelium damage, often producing bilateral bull's-eye macular changes and paracentral ring scotomas.
symptoms_in_common: Long-term hydroxychloroquine use at 400 mg daily for 15 years
Bilateral macular pigmentary changes consistent with bull's-eye maculopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Flashing lights are less typical than blurred vision and paracentral scotomas
Early cataracts are not caused by hydroxychloroquine retinopathy

data.description: An inherited retinal degeneration in which cone photoreceptors are affected first, causing reduced central vision, impaired color discrimination, photophobia, and sometimes bull's-eye macular atrophy; rod dysfunction may develop later.
symptoms_in_common: Possible bilateral symmetric macular atrophy and ring scotomas
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at age 68 is less typical, as many inherited cone-rod dystrophies begin earlier in life
Long-term hydroxychloroquine exposure strongly favors drug toxicity instead
No reported photophobia
No reported night blindness or peripheral visual loss

data.description: A rare immune-mediated retinal disorder, sometimes associated with systemic autoimmune disease or malignancy, that causes progressive photoreceptor dysfunction with visual-field loss, photopsias, reduced color vision, and decreased visual acuity.
symptoms_in_common: History of inflammatory arthritis suggesting an autoimmune background
symptoms_not_in_common: The characteristic bull's-eye pattern and high cumulative hydroxychloroquine exposure more strongly support hydroxychloroquine toxicity
No reported rapid generalized peripheral field loss
No reported marked night blindness
No known malignancy is described

data.diagnosis: Age-related macular degeneration, particularly geographic atrophy
data.description: A degenerative macular disease in older adults involving retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptor loss, causing progressive central visual impairment and, in advanced atrophic disease, central scotomas.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral macular retinal pigment epithelial abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Flashing lights are not a typical presenting symptom
Paracentral ring scotomas and a bull's-eye pattern are less typical than central distortion or central scotoma
Mild color vision loss is less characteristic early in age-related macular degeneration
The prolonged hydroxychloroquine exposure provides a more likely explanation

data.diagnosis: Macular dystrophy, such as Stargardt-like or pattern dystrophy
data.description: A group of inherited disorders affecting the macula and retinal pigment epithelium that can cause bilateral reduction in central vision, color vision abnormalities, and pigmentary macular changes that may occasionally resemble a bull's-eye lesion.
symptoms_not_in_common: New presentation at 68 years is less typical for many inherited macular dystrophies
Flashing lights are not a prominent feature of most macular dystrophies
The visual-field ring defects together with extensive hydroxychloroquine exposure favor toxic maculopathy
No family history of similar visual problems is reported

data.description: 50-year-old woman with right nasal congestion and right parotid swelling, unresponsive to antibiotics and steroids. Exam and nasal endoscopy showed right-predominant adenoid/nasopharyngeal swelling; CT demonstrated a 4.1 cm nasopharyngeal soft tissue mass. She had no significant past medical history but was a current smoker (35 pack-years). Initial biopsy showed atypical lymphoid hyperplasia with scattered large atypical CD30-positive cells. After adenoidectomy, a 3-month MRI showed recurrence; repeat excision revealed a nodular infiltrate of small lymphocytes. PET-CT showed FDG uptake confined to the nasopharynx without lymphadenopathy, and bone marrow biopsy was negative.

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal classic Hodgkin lymphoma of the nasopharynx
data.description: A rare localized form of classic Hodgkin lymphoma arising in nasopharyngeal lymphoid tissue, characterized by scattered Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background; these cells commonly express CD30 and CD15.
symptoms_in_common: FDG uptake localized to the nasopharynx
No lymphadenopathy or bone marrow involvement, consistent with localized stage I extranodal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Right parotid swelling is not a classic presenting feature
No reported B symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss
Nasal congestion is less common than cervical lymph-node enlargement in classic Hodgkin lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia of the nasopharynx
data.description: A benign enlargement of lymphoid tissue due to chronic inflammation, infection, irritation, or immune stimulation; it can resemble lymphoma on small biopsy specimens.
symptoms_in_common: Initial biopsy interpreted as atypical lymphoid hyperplasia
Nodular infiltrate of small lymphocytes on repeat excision
symptoms_not_in_common: Large atypical cells expressing CD30 and CD15 are concerning for Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells rather than uncomplicated reactive hyperplasia
Rapid recurrence after adenoidectomy is atypical
A discrete 4.1 cm FDG-avid mass is less typical of benign reactive enlargement
Lack of response to antibiotics and steroids is less supportive of an inflammatory reactive process

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising from the nasopharyngeal mucosa, often presenting with nasal obstruction, ear symptoms, or cervical lymph-node metastases; smoking is a risk factor for head and neck malignancies.
symptoms_in_common: Nasopharyngeal mass on CT and MRI
Persistent disease despite antibiotics and steroids
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsies showed lymphoid infiltrates rather than malignant epithelial cells
CD30-positive and CD15-positive large atypical lymphoid cells favor Hodgkin lymphoma rather than carcinoma
No cervical lymphadenopathy was identified
The recurrent lesion was described as a nodular infiltrate of small lymphocytes rather than carcinoma

data.description: An aggressive Epstein-Barr virus-associated lymphoma that commonly involves the nasal cavity or nasopharynx and may cause obstructive, destructive, or ulcerative sinonasal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Failure to improve with antibiotics and steroids
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported nasal ulceration, tissue necrosis, epistaxis, or destructive midline lesion
Histology described small lymphocytes with scattered CD30-positive and CD15-positive large cells rather than an angiocentric cytotoxic NK/T-cell infiltrate
No reported EBV association
The course appears localized and relatively indolent rather than typically aggressive

data.description: A distinct, usually indolent Hodgkin lymphoma composed of nodular B-cell-rich infiltrates containing LP cells; it more often presents with peripheral lymph-node enlargement than extranodal disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Nasopharyngeal extranodal presentation is uncommon
The atypical large cells were CD30-positive and CD15-positive, whereas LP cells are usually CD20-positive and typically negative for CD30 and CD15
Scattered Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg-like cells in an inflammatory background favor classic Hodgkin lymphoma rather than nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma
Nasal congestion and parotid swelling are not typical primary manifestations

data.description: 83-year-old woman with hypertension and biopsy-proven vaginal melanoma diagnosed 4 months earlier, with invasive locoregional disease and a 3-mm left upper lobe lung nodule on PET-CT. She received four cycles of ipilimumab, last dose 3 weeks before admission, and developed pruritus, lethargy, malaise after the third dose and diarrhea after the fourth. She presented with 2 weeks of progressively worsening substernal chest pain and dyspnea. On admission, ECG showed sinus tachycardia with 1 mm ST elevations in leads I, V2, and V3; troponin-I was elevated at 0.98 ng/mL and ESR was 65 mm/hour. Echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 50% with LV outflow tract obstruction and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. Cardiac angiography revealed 30% proximal LAD stenosis without thrombus.

An immune-mediated inflammation of the heart muscle caused by ipilimumab, a CTLA-4 immune checkpoint inhibitor. It can produce chest pain, ECG abnormalities, troponin elevation, arrhythmias, and reduced cardiac function despite nonobstructive coronary arteries.
symptoms_in_common: ST-segment elevations in leads I, V2, and V3
Recent ipilimumab exposure, with the last dose 3 weeks earlier
No obstructive coronary lesion on angiography
FDG uptake involving the myocardium on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea
Pruritus
Known vaginal melanoma

data.description: Inflammation involving the myocardium and sometimes the pericardium, which may be infectious, autoimmune, malignant-associated, or medication-induced. It can mimic acute myocardial infarction with chest pain, ST elevation, and elevated troponin.
symptoms_in_common: Myocardial FDG uptake on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea
Pruritus
LV outflow tract obstruction with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
Known vaginal melanoma

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA)
data.description: Myocardial infarction or ischemic myocardial injury with elevated troponin and ischemic ECG changes but without obstructive epicardial coronary artery disease. Possible mechanisms include coronary vasospasm, microvascular dysfunction, embolism, or transient plaque disruption.
symptoms_in_common: ST elevations in anterior and lateral leads
Only mild 30% proximal LAD stenosis without thrombus on angiography
Hypertension as a cardiovascular risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated ESR
Pruritus, diarrhea, lethargy, and malaise after ipilimumab
Myocardial inflammatory FDG uptake on PET imaging
LV outflow tract obstruction with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve

data.diagnosis: Stress-induced cardiomyopathy (Takotsubo syndrome), possibly with dynamic LV outflow tract obstruction
data.description: A transient stress-related myocardial dysfunction, most often affecting older women, that can cause chest pain, dyspnea, ST elevation, modest troponin elevation, and dynamic LV outflow tract obstruction in some cases. Severe illness, cancer, and immunotherapy-related stress can act as triggers.
symptoms_in_common: LV outflow tract obstruction and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
Major physical and emotional stressors from advanced malignancy and cancer treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated ESR
Myocardial FDG uptake suggesting active inflammation
Pruritus and diarrhea after ipilimumab
Ejection fraction of 50% without a described characteristic regional wall-motion pattern

data.description: Melanoma can metastasize to the heart, including the myocardium or pericardium, and may cause chest pain, dyspnea, arrhythmia, myocardial injury, or inflammatory imaging abnormalities. PET avidity can identify metabolically active metastatic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Myocardial FDG uptake on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Temporal onset after four cycles of ipilimumab
Pruritus and diarrhea consistent with immune-related adverse effects
Elevated ESR is nonspecific and does not establish metastasis
No discrete intracardiac mass is described

data.description: 33-year-old bisexual Brazilian man with 4 months of painful bowel movements and rectal bleeding, with one daily bowel movement and bright red blood on toilet paper, not mixed with stool. He denied abdominal pain and weight loss. He reported a sexual encounter with a man 6 weeks before presentation. Initial exam showed a tender external hemorrhoid and normal vital signs. At follow-up, bleeding hemorrhoids were noted around the anus. Surgical evaluation found large superficial anal fissures at the anterior and posterior midline anal verge with small-to-moderate sentinel skin tags and moderate tenderness on digital rectal examination. Anoscopy showed fissures and small internal hemorrhoids, and flexible sigmoidoscopy showed mild-to-moderate inflammation of the distal 10 cm of rectum with edema and patchy erythema.

Rectal involvement by Treponema pallidum, usually sexually acquired. It can cause proctitis, anal fissures, ulcers, bleeding, and a plasma-cell-rich inflammatory infiltrate; spirochetes may be demonstrated by immunohistochemical staining.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sexual encounter with a man
Distal rectal inflammation with edema and patchy erythema
Histology consistent with chronic plasmacytic inflammation and spirochete immunostaining
symptoms_not_in_common: Hemorrhoids are not a defining manifestation of syphilis
A four-month course is longer than many acute presentations
No reported genital or perianal chancre
No systemic secondary-syphilis findings such as rash, fever, or lymphadenopathy

data.description: A sexually transmitted infection caused by invasive Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1-L3. In men who have sex with men, it can cause painful inflammatory proctitis, rectal bleeding, ulceration, and anorectal symptoms that can mimic inflammatory bowel disease.
symptoms_in_common: Distal proctitis with erythema and edema
Anal fissures or ulcer-like lesions can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No rectal discharge or mucus reported
No tenesmus reported
No fever, malaise, or inguinal lymphadenopathy reported
Superficial midline fissures and hemorrhoids are less characteristic than ulcerative proctitis
Spirochete-positive immunohistochemistry would not be expected

data.description: HSV-1 or HSV-2 infection of the rectum and anus, commonly sexually acquired, which may produce severe anorectal pain, painful defecation, ulcers, bleeding, and distal proctitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No vesicles, grouped ulcers, or perianal herpetic lesions described
Symptoms are present for four months, whereas untreated HSV proctitis is usually more acute
No fever, urinary retention, sacral pain, or neurologic symptoms reported
Large superficial midline fissures with sentinel tags are not classic HSV lesions
Spirochete staining would not be expected

data.diagnosis: Ulcerative proctitis (ulcerative colitis limited to the rectum)
data.description: A form of ulcerative colitis confined to the rectum, causing continuous mucosal inflammation, rectal bleeding, urgency, tenesmus, and sometimes painful defecation.
symptoms_in_common: Endoscopic distal rectal inflammation with erythema and edema
No abdominal pain or weight loss can occur in disease limited to the rectum
symptoms_not_in_common: Painful external anal fissures are not typical of ulcerative proctitis
Sentinel skin tags are not typical
Recent sexual exposure suggests an infectious cause
Only one bowel movement daily without urgency or diarrhea is less typical
Spirochete-positive immunohistochemistry would not support ulcerative colitis

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can involve any gastrointestinal segment and may cause perianal fissures, skin tags, rectal inflammation, pain, bleeding, fistulas, and abscesses.
symptoms_not_in_common: Fissures are in the anterior and posterior midline, whereas Crohn-related fissures are often multiple, deep, or off-midline
No abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, or systemic symptoms reported
No fistula, abscess, stricture, or skip lesions described
Recent sexual exposure and spirochete staining favor an infectious proctitis instead

data.description: 65-year-old man with a history of hypertension and prior laminectomy, never smoker, with family history of prostate cancer in his father. He presented for evaluation; PSA and digital rectal examination were normal. Urine dipstick showed trace blood with otherwise negative findings.
Presence of a small amount of blood in urine detected on dipstick or microscopy without visible blood or urinary symptoms; it may be transient or reflect an underlying urinary tract condition.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal PSA
Normal digital rectal examination

data.description: Cancer arising from the lining of the bladder, often presenting with painless microscopic or visible hematuria, especially in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: No reported pain or urinary infection findings
symptoms_not_in_common: Never-smoker status
Only trace rather than persistent or gross hematuria
No reported urinary urgency, frequency, or dysuria

data.description: A kidney cancer that can cause microscopic or gross hematuria and is sometimes discovered incidentally before causing pain or systemic symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: No flank pain
No palpable abdominal mass
No reported weight loss, fever, or fatigue

data.description: Formation of urinary tract stones that can irritate the lining of the kidney or ureter and cause microscopic hematuria.
symptoms_not_in_common: No flank or colicky abdominal pain
No nausea or vomiting
No dysuria or urinary urgency
No reported stone passage

data.description: Noncancerous enlargement of the prostate that commonly affects older men and can occasionally be associated with microscopic hematuria from prostatic bleeding.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal digital rectal examination
No weak urinary stream
No urinary hesitancy, frequency, nocturia, or incomplete bladder emptying

data.description: 20-year-old male with a history of bleeding tendency in the neonatal period and family history of easy bruisability in his father. He also had conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis and was evaluated preoperatively for chronic maxillary sinusitis surgery. Blood counts and serum chemistry were normal, but coagulation screening showed prolonged PT and aPTT with normal bleeding time; mixing studies suggested factor deficiency. Fibrinogen activity was below the detection limit, while fibrinogen antigen was normal. FGA and FGB mutations were not detected. His parents had normal coagulation studies and normal fibrinogen activity.

An inherited qualitative fibrinogen disorder in which fibrinogen antigen is present at a normal level but the fibrinogen molecule functions poorly, causing impaired clot formation and prolonged coagulation tests.
symptoms_in_common: Bleeding tendency beginning in the neonatal period
Mixing study suggesting a coagulation factor deficiency rather than an inhibitor
Fibrinogen activity below the detection limit despite normal fibrinogen antigen
Normal blood counts and serum chemistry
symptoms_not_in_common: Conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: An inherited fibrinogen disorder characterized by both reduced functional fibrinogen activity and an abnormal fibrinogen molecule; antigen levels may be normal or variably reduced depending on the mutation.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly reduced or undetectable functional fibrinogen activity
Correction pattern on mixing studies consistent with factor deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen is less typical when there is a major quantitative component
Conductive hearing loss
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: A severe inherited deficiency of fibrinogen, usually caused by biallelic fibrinogen-gene variants, resulting in absent or extremely low fibrinogen and potentially severe bleeding from birth.
symptoms_in_common: Bleeding tendency in the neonatal period
Very low or undetectable fibrinogen activity
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen, which argues strongly against true afibrinogenemia
Normal coagulation and fibrinogen activity in both parents is less supportive of recessive inherited afibrinogenemia
Only relatively mild bleeding history rather than severe recurrent bleeding
Conductive hearing loss
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.diagnosis: Acquired dysfibrinogenemia due to liver disease or a paraprotein disorder
data.description: An acquired qualitative fibrinogen abnormality that can occur with significant liver disease, plasma-cell disorders, or other systemic illnesses and may cause impaired fibrinogen function with prolonged clotting times.
symptoms_in_common: Potential discrepancy between fibrinogen activity and fibrinogen antigen
symptoms_not_in_common: Bleeding tendency beginning in the neonatal period
Family history of easy bruisability
Normal serum chemistry without evidence of liver dysfunction
Young age and lifelong pattern of illness
Conductive hearing loss
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: A rare inherited coagulation disorder caused by deficiency of factor XIII, which stabilizes fibrin clots. It can produce severe bleeding from birth, including umbilical stump bleeding and delayed postoperative bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Bleeding tendency from the neonatal period
symptoms_not_in_common: Factor XIII deficiency usually has normal PT and aPTT
Undetectable fibrinogen activity is not expected
Normal fibrinogen antigen with absent functional fibrinogen is not characteristic
Mixing-study findings specifically pointing to fibrinogen dysfunction are not typical
Conductive hearing loss
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: 60-year-old man with a 1-year history of progressive exertional dyspnea, worse over the past 4 months, accompanied by persistent nonproductive cough. Five days before admission, he developed sore throat, neck and bilateral arm swelling, orthopnea, and facial flushing/redness; he was transferred for evaluation of new dyspnea, cough, neck swelling, and a lung mass. At the outside hospital, he was afebrile with stable vital signs, had a flushed face, swollen neck, and absent breath sounds over the right lung fields. History includes heavy tobacco use (2 packs/day for 40 years), occasional marijuana use, and regular alcohol intake. Family history notable for pancreatic cancer in his mother.

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary pleomorphic carcinoma (sarcomatoid non-small-cell lung carcinoma)
data.description: A rare, aggressive non-small-cell lung cancer characterized by poorly differentiated epithelial tumor cells with pleomorphic and/or giant-cell features. It commonly occurs in older heavy smokers and may form a large central lung or mediastinal mass.
symptoms_in_common: Findings consistent with superior vena cava obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat is not a classic primary symptom, although it may occur from venous congestion or local compression
No hemoptysis, chest pain, weight loss, or fever is reported

data.description: An aggressive neuroendocrine lung cancer strongly associated with cigarette smoking. It often arises centrally, spreads early to mediastinal lymph nodes, and frequently causes superior vena cava syndrome.
symptoms_not_in_common: One year of slowly progressive symptoms is somewhat less typical because small-cell carcinoma often has a more rapid clinical course
No paraneoplastic manifestations such as hyponatremia, ectopic ACTH syndrome, or Lambert-Eaton symptoms are reported
No weight loss or hemoptysis is reported

data.diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung
data.description: A non-small-cell lung cancer closely linked to tobacco smoking. It commonly arises in the central bronchi, can cause endobronchial obstruction and lung collapse, and may invade mediastinal structures.
symptoms_in_common: Possible endobronchial lesion causing reduced or absent right-sided breath sounds
Neck and arm edema with facial flushing due to superior vena cava compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Nonproductive cough is less classic than cough with hemoptysis or sputum production
No hemoptysis is reported
No chest pain, weight loss, or recurrent post-obstructive pneumonia is reported

data.description: The most common type of non-small-cell lung cancer. Although often peripheral, advanced adenocarcinoma may involve mediastinal lymph nodes or directly invade mediastinal structures, producing airway and superior vena cava obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Orthopnea due to superior vena cava obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent central/endobronchial mass pattern is less typical than the peripheral location often seen in adenocarcinoma
Very heavy smoking favors squamous-cell or small-cell carcinoma more strongly, although adenocarcinoma remains possible
No pleuritic chest pain, weight loss, or malignant pleural effusion is reported

data.description: Lymphoma involving mediastinal lymph nodes or thymic-region lymphoid tissue can create a bulky mediastinal mass and cause superior vena cava syndrome through compression of the vena cava and adjacent airways.
symptoms_in_common: Clinical features of superior vena cava syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Age and extensive tobacco use more strongly favor a primary lung carcinoma
A unilateral lung/endobronchial lesion with absent right-sided breath sounds is less typical for lymphoma
No fever, drenching night sweats, unintentional weight loss, or generalized lymphadenopathy is reported

diagnoses.name: Poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the lung
diagnoses.title: lung adenocarcinoma

data.description: Male term infant presented at 20 days of age with profound T-cell lymphopenia detected on newborn screening, with no detectable TRECs. He had neonatal teeth, hypotonia, umbilical hernia, and erythematous psoriaform dermatitis. Imaging showed wormian skull bones, mild pulmonary artery stenosis, and absence of the corpus callosum. No maternal engraftment was detected.

A rare developmental immunodeficiency caused by pathogenic BCL11B variants. BCL11B is essential for T-cell development and also affects neurodevelopment, craniofacial structures, skin, teeth, and skeletal development.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital cardiac abnormality such as pulmonary artery stenosis
Dysmorphic appearance and excessive body hair/skin-hair abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Umbilical hernia is not a defining feature
No maternal engraftment is neither typical nor atypical but does not specifically support this diagnosis

data.diagnosis: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome with complete DiGeorge syndrome
data.description: A chromosomal disorder that can cause thymic aplasia or severe thymic hypoplasia, resulting in profound T-cell deficiency. It is commonly associated with congenital heart disease, facial differences, and developmental abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital heart disease including pulmonary artery abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Psoriaform dermatitis
Wormian skull bones
Umbilical hernia
Marked hair/skin abnormalities
Absence of the corpus callosum is not a classic feature

data.diagnosis: CHARGE syndrome with thymic hypoplasia or aplasia
data.description: A multisystem developmental disorder usually caused by CHD7 variants. Some affected infants have severe T-cell lymphopenia due to thymic hypoplasia or aplasia, along with heart defects, hypotonia, and central nervous system abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary artery stenosis or other congenital heart disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Psoriaform dermatitis
Umbilical hernia
No reported coloboma, choanal atresia, characteristic ear anomalies, or genital anomalies

data.diagnosis: PAX1-related otofaciocervical syndrome type 2 with severe T-cell immunodeficiency
data.description: A rare autosomal-recessive developmental syndrome caused by PAX1 deficiency. It can produce absent or poorly developed thymic tissue with severe T-cell immunodeficiency, along with facial, skeletal, and sometimes cardiac abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Wormian skull bones or abnormal skull development
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth are not typical
Psoriaform dermatitis is not a usual feature
Absence of the corpus callosum is not a classic finding
Umbilical hernia is not a defining feature
Typical otofaciocervical findings such as branchial defects, low-set ears, or shoulder-girdle abnormalities were not described

data.diagnosis: RAG1/RAG2-associated severe combined immunodeficiency or Omenn syndrome
data.description: Defects in RAG1 or RAG2 impair V(D)J recombination and can cause severe combined immunodeficiency with absent TRECs and profound T-cell lymphopenia. Hypomorphic variants may cause Omenn syndrome, characterized by inflammatory erythroderma and immune dysregulation.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous dermatitis that could resemble early Omenn-associated erythroderma
Absence of maternal engraftment helps support an intrinsic severe immunodeficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Absence of the corpus callosum
Pulmonary artery stenosis
Umbilical hernia
Hypotonia
Congenital dysmorphic, skeletal, and neurodevelopmental findings are not typical of isolated RAG-associated SCID

data.description: 47-year-old male with tenesmus and mucoid stools, admitted from a local clinic. Past history includes pulmonary tuberculosis treated 20 years ago and a 20-pack-year smoking history; no alcohol use. He denied weight loss, fever, or night sweats. On admission, vital signs and physical examination were largely unremarkable except for a depressed anterior chest wall and healed right upper-lung scar on chest radiograph. Upper GI endoscopy showed a healed duodenal bulb ulcer with negative rapid urease test. Abdominal CT showed no lymphadenopathy, and bone marrow aspiration/biopsy was unremarkable.

data.diagnosis: Primary rectal extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma)
data.description: An indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising from mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue. In the rectum it can produce submucosal nodules, erosions, or ulcerated lesions; biopsy commonly shows small lymphoid-cell infiltration with lymphoepithelial lesions and B-cell-marker positivity.
symptoms_in_common: Lack of constitutional symptoms such as fever, night sweats, and weight loss is compatible with an indolent localized lymphoma
No abdominal lymphadenopathy or bone marrow involvement is compatible with localized primary rectal disease

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the rectum that often causes altered bowel habits, rectal bleeding, mucus production, obstructive symptoms, and tenesmus.
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No reported rectal bleeding
No reported abdominal pain or obstructive symptoms

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease causing continuous mucosal inflammation beginning in the rectum. Rectal-predominant disease can cause urgency, tenesmus, mucus, and bleeding.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported bloody diarrhea
No abdominal cramping
No fever or systemic inflammatory symptoms

data.description: Gastrointestinal infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis that may produce ulceration, strictures, mass-like lesions, abdominal pain, altered bowel habits, and constitutional symptoms. Prior pulmonary tuberculosis increases clinical consideration, although rectal involvement is uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Remote history of treated pulmonary tuberculosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No night sweats
No weight loss
No abdominal pain
No abdominal lymphadenopathy

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the rectum
data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can involve the gastrointestinal tract as an ulcerated or mass-like lesion and may cause tenesmus, bleeding, pain, or obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Rectal lesion with lymphoid-appearing histology can raise consideration of lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No fever
No night sweats
No lymphadenopathy
No bone marrow involvement
No reported abdominal pain, bleeding, or bowel obstruction

data.description: 24-year-old woman with no significant past medical history presented with 2 days of left leg pain after training for a 5-km race. Pain was crampy and extended to the left lower abdomen and buttock, with generalized leg swelling and exertional dyspnea. She denied fever, chest pain, dyspnea at rest, or trauma. Exam showed tachycardia, and the left leg had pitting edema, erythema from thigh to calf, and increased warmth. History included oral contraceptive use since age 15, prior smoking, and a family history of DVT in her father after surgery.

data.diagnosis: Acute left iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
data.description: A blood clot in the deep veins of the left pelvis and leg, causing impaired venous drainage and risk of embolization to the lungs.
symptoms_in_common: Increased warmth of the left leg
Risk factors including oral contraceptive use, prior smoking, and family history of DVT
symptoms_not_in_common: Exertional dyspnea

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arteries by embolized thrombus, usually originating from a lower-extremity or pelvic DVT; the chest CT image is consistent with pulmonary arterial filling defects.
symptoms_in_common: Known clinical features suggesting a left-leg DVT
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked unilateral leg pitting edema
Leg erythema and warmth
Pain extending to the left lower abdomen and buttock
No chest pain
No dyspnea at rest

data.diagnosis: May-Thurner syndrome (left iliac vein compression syndrome) with thrombosis
data.description: Compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery, predisposing young women to extensive left-sided iliofemoral DVT and pulmonary embolism; the pelvic imaging is suggestive of left iliac venous thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary embolic symptoms due to associated DVT
Oral contraceptive use as an additional thrombotic risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute erythema and warmth of the entire leg are less specific and can also reflect cellulitis or severe acute DVT
No prior history of chronic leg heaviness, varicose veins, or recurrent left-leg swelling

data.diagnosis: Cellulitis of the left lower extremity
data.description: A bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue that commonly causes a warm, red, swollen, painful limb.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pitting edema involving the entire leg from thigh to calf
Left lower abdominal and buttock pain
Exertional dyspnea
Tachycardia in the setting of suspected venous thromboembolism
No fever
Oral contraceptive use and family history of DVT strongly favor thrombosis rather than infection
Imaging findings consistent with pulmonary emboli

data.diagnosis: Exercise-related muscle strain or delayed-onset muscle soreness
data.description: Muscle injury or soreness after strenuous exercise, typically causing localized pain and tenderness after activity.
symptoms_in_common: Leg pain beginning after training for a 5-km race
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized unilateral leg swelling
Pitting edema
Erythema and increased warmth from thigh to calf
Pain extending to the lower abdomen and buttock
Tachycardia
Exertional dyspnea
Pulmonary arterial filling defects on imaging
Strong thrombotic risk factors

data.description: 3-year-old boy, born at 41 weeks gestation without perinatal problems, birth weight 3.4kg. Parents were not consanguineous and had no medical history. History of 3 prior hospitalizations for viral pneumonia at 12, 18, and 27 months. Presented with recurrent and persistent pneumonia. Current symptoms included cough, sputum and fever. Physical exam showed: temperature 39.5°C, pulse 129/min, respiration 28/min, BP 95/55 mmHg. Weight 15.3kg (50-75th percentile), height 96.5cm (50-75th percentile). Two 3mm ulcers in uvula, fine crackles in both lung fields, palpable liver 1 finger-breadth below right costal margin, palpable spleen tip.

data.diagnosis: X-linked chronic granulomatous disease (CGD, CYBB-related NADPH oxidase deficiency)
data.description: A primary immunodeficiency in which neutrophils cannot generate an effective oxidative burst to kill certain bacteria and fungi. Abnormal dihydrorhodamine flow cytometry and a CYBB mutation pattern support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent severe pneumonia beginning in infancy
Persistent current pneumonia with fever, cough and sputum
Multiple prior hospitalizations for respiratory infections
Oral/uvular ulcers can occur during infection or inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal growth percentiles are not a classic distinguishing feature, although they can be present
No reported history of skin abscesses, lymphadenitis, osteomyelitis or invasive fungal infection

data.description: An inherited disorder characterized by persistently very low neutrophil counts, causing early recurrent bacterial infections, oral ulcers and pneumonia.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent severe bacterial-type respiratory infections in early childhood
Possible mild hepatosplenomegaly during recurrent infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No neutrophil count or persistent neutropenia is provided
The abnormal oxidative-burst flow-cytometry pattern favors CGD rather than isolated neutropenia
No recurrent skin infections, gingivitis, perianal infections or omphalitis are reported

data.description: A primary immunodeficiency caused by defective leukocyte adhesion and migration into tissues, leading to recurrent serious bacterial infections and impaired wound healing.
symptoms_in_common: High fever with persistent respiratory infection
Possible hepatosplenomegaly associated with recurrent infection
Recurrent infections beginning early in life
symptoms_not_in_common: Oral ulcers are less characteristic than severe periodontitis
No delayed separation of the umbilical cord is reported
No poor wound healing, absent pus formation, marked leukocytosis or recurrent skin infections is reported
The oxidative-burst testing pattern is more consistent with CGD

data.description: A primary immunodeficiency, commonly involving impaired STAT3 signaling, characterized by recurrent pneumonias, eczema, skin abscesses, elevated IgE and eosinophilia.
symptoms_in_common: Current fever, cough, sputum production and crackles
Persistent pulmonary infection that may lead to structural lung disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No eczema is reported
No recurrent staphylococcal skin abscesses are reported
No skeletal abnormalities, retained primary teeth or characteristic facial features are reported
Hepatosplenomegaly and oral ulcers are not typical hallmark findings
The abnormal neutrophil oxidative-burst test favors CGD instead

data.description: An inherited mucociliary-clearance disorder causing chronic wet cough, recurrent sinopulmonary infections, bronchiectasis and sometimes situs abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: High fever and severe recurrent infections requiring repeated hospitalization suggest an immunodeficiency more strongly
No chronic nasal congestion, chronic otitis media or neonatal respiratory distress is reported
No situs inversus or other laterality abnormality is reported
Oral ulcers and hepatosplenomegaly are not typical
Abnormal oxidative-burst flow cytometry is not explained by primary ciliary dyskinesia

data.description: A 34-year-old woman presented with acute abdominal and back pain 3 years before evaluation at the oncology clinic. She had been well until this onset. Her medical history was notable for migraines. She did not smoke cigarettes, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She worked full time as a social worker and lived in New Jersey with her husband and child. Family history included breast cancer in maternal grandmother (70s), uterine cancer in paternal aunt (40s), and colon cancer in two paternal cousins (30s and 50s). On physical examination: temperature 36.5°C, blood pressure 108/78 mm Hg, heart rate 78 beats per minute, body-mass index 27.7. The abdomen had well-healed surgical scars; remainder of physical examination was normal. Laboratory results showed elevated tumor marker CA 19-9 at 110 IU per milliliter (reference <35), while alpha-fetoprotein and carcinoembryonic antigen levels were normal.
A primary cancer of the bile ducts within the liver, typically forming infiltrative adenocarcinoma glands in dense fibrous stroma and often associated with elevated CA 19-9.
symptoms_in_common: Histologic appearance of gland-forming adenocarcinoma in desmoplastic stroma
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age of 34 years, since cholangiocarcinoma is more common in older adults
Absence of jaundice
Absence of fever, pruritus, or documented weight loss
Long interval of relative clinical stability after initial pain

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the pancreas that commonly produces CA 19-9 and can spread to the liver, where it appears as multiple metastatic lesions with gland-forming adenocarcinoma histology.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple hepatic lesions compatible with metastases
Adenocarcinoma with desmoplastic stromal reaction on pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: No pancreatic mass described on the provided imaging
No jaundice or biliary obstruction symptoms
No unexplained weight loss or anorexia reported
Age is much younger than typical for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
Three-year course is less typical for untreated pancreatic adenocarcinoma

data.description: Cancer of the colon or rectum that frequently metastasizes to the liver and may show infiltrating malignant glands with fibrotic stroma. CA 19-9 can be elevated in some cases, although CEA is more commonly elevated.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of colon cancer in paternal cousins
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal carcinoembryonic antigen level
No reported rectal bleeding
No change in bowel habits
No anemia or weight loss reported
Age 34 is younger than typical for sporadic colorectal cancer

data.description: A stomach cancer that can produce CA 19-9 and spread to the liver. Histology often shows infiltrating adenocarcinoma, sometimes with prominent stromal fibrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple liver lesions that may represent metastases
symptoms_not_in_common: No dyspepsia, early satiety, nausea, vomiting, or gastrointestinal bleeding reported
No weight loss reported
No anemia described
Young age for typical gastric adenocarcinoma
Back pain is not a prominent presenting symptom in most cases

data.description: A mucin-producing epithelial ovarian malignancy that can elevate CA 19-9 and may metastasize to the liver or liver capsule. It may present with abdominal pain and can show glandular adenocarcinoma histology.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of breast and uterine cancers may suggest a hereditary cancer predisposition
symptoms_not_in_common: No ovarian or pelvic mass described
No abdominal distention, ascites, or pelvic pressure symptoms reported
Liver-dominant multifocal disease without reported peritoneal disease is less typical
No menstrual or gynecologic symptoms reported
