data.description: A 37-year-old woman presented with a 4-month history of right facial pain and a 3-month history of progressive painful swelling beneath the right ear lobe. Physical examination revealed a soft swelling in the anteroinferior auricular area that was smooth, elastic, mobile and painful on pressure, but not fluctuant. The facial nerve function was normal and the cervical lymph node was not palpable. There were no systemic symptoms. The patient was screened for metastases, and no lung or abdomen lesions were detected.

data.diagnosis: Primary leiomyosarcoma of the parotid gland
data.description: A rare malignant smooth-muscle tumor arising in or near the parotid gland, typically composed of intersecting fascicles of spindle cells and often showing smooth-muscle immunohistochemical marker expression.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively enlarging painful swelling beneath the right ear
Spindle-cell fascicular histology on the provided image
No detected lung or abdominal metastases at presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: Soft, mobile, well-circumscribed clinical appearance
Normal facial nerve function despite a painful parotid-region mass
Young age for a sarcoma of the parotid region

data.description: A benign peripheral nerve-sheath tumor that may arise from branches of the facial nerve or adjacent sensory nerves and can present as a slow-growing parotid-region mass.
symptoms_in_common: Painful swelling in the anteroinferior auricular/parotid region
Normal facial nerve function can occur in facial-nerve schwannoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive pain and growth over a relatively short 3-month period
Spindle cells arranged predominantly in smooth-muscle-like intersecting fascicles rather than classic Antoni A/Antoni B areas
No described relationship of the mass to a specific nerve

data.diagnosis: Pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid gland
data.description: The most common benign salivary-gland tumor, usually presenting as a painless, slowly growing, mobile parotid mass with mixed epithelial and myoepithelial elements.
symptoms_in_common: Parotid-region swelling beneath the ear lobe
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain on pressure
Right facial pain
Relatively rapid progressive enlargement
Predominantly spindle-cell fascicular histology without described epithelial or chondromyxoid components

data.diagnosis: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the parotid gland
data.description: A malignant salivary-gland tumor composed of mucous, epidermoid, and intermediate cells; it may cause a painful enlarging parotid mass and, in advanced cases, facial nerve dysfunction or nodal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Potentially malignant behavior prompting metastatic screening
symptoms_not_in_common: Soft, mobile, elastic mass
No facial nerve weakness
No palpable cervical lymph nodes
No systemic metastases detected
Spindle-cell histology rather than mucous and squamoid/epidermoid tumor cells

data.description: A rare malignant spindle-cell tumor showing myofibroblastic differentiation, often with infiltrative fascicular growth and potential local recurrence or metastasis.
symptoms_in_common: Spindle-cell lesion with fascicular arrangement on histology
Absence of distant metastases at initial evaluation can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Soft and freely mobile physical examination findings
No facial nerve dysfunction
No palpable cervical lymphadenopathy
No described infiltrative fixation to surrounding tissues

data.description: At the age of 30 months, the patient began presenting an evolving framework of severe cognitive and neurological impairment, with tetraparesis and mixed spastic-dystonic features, language delay and deafness. Moreover, she has coarse facial features, presenting a high forehead and hypertelorism; her tongue is protruding due to macroglossia.

data.diagnosis: Mucopolysaccharidosis type III (Sanfilippo syndrome), especially type A or B
data.description: An autosomal-recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by impaired degradation of heparan sulfate. It produces progressive neurodevelopmental regression, behavioral/cognitive deterioration, coarse facial features, hearing impairment, and white-matter abnormalities on brain MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive severe cognitive and neurological impairment beginning in early childhood
Progressive motor impairment with spasticity and dystonia
Diffuse cerebral white-matter signal abnormalities and mild ventriculomegaly on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe tetraparesis at approximately 30 months can occur but is relatively early and severe for many Sanfilippo presentations

data.description: A lysosomal disorder due to iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency causing dermatan- and heparan-sulfate accumulation. Severe forms cause developmental delay or regression, coarse facies, macroglossia, hearing loss, joint and skeletal disease, and progressive neurologic involvement.
symptoms_in_common: White-matter abnormalities and ventricular enlargement may be seen on brain MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: The patient is female, whereas classic Hunter syndrome is X-linked and predominantly affects males
No hepatosplenomegaly, joint contractures, skeletal dysplasia, or umbilical/inguinal hernia is described

data.diagnosis: GM1 gangliosidosis type II (late-infantile GM1 gangliosidosis)
data.description: A lysosomal storage disorder caused by beta-galactosidase deficiency, leading to GM1 ganglioside accumulation in the brain and other tissues. Late-infantile disease commonly causes developmental regression, dystonia or spasticity, hearing impairment, coarse features, and progressive white-matter involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Onset in infancy or early childhood with progressive neurologic decline
Severe cognitive impairment and language delay
symptoms_not_in_common: No skeletal abnormalities, kyphosis, hepatosplenomegaly, or cherry-red macular spot is reported
Hypertelorism and high forehead are less characteristic than generalized coarsening of facial features

data.description: An autosomal-recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-mannosidase deficiency. It can cause developmental delay, progressive intellectual disability, hearing loss, coarse facial features, skeletal abnormalities, immune dysfunction, ataxia, and later spasticity.
symptoms_in_common: Developmental delay and severe cognitive impairment
White-matter changes can occur on neuroimaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Macroglossia with persistent tongue protrusion is not a prominent typical feature
Dystonia and severe tetraparesis beginning at 30 months are less typical than ataxia and hypotonia
No recurrent infections, immune deficiency, or skeletal disease is described

data.description: A lysosomal trafficking disorder in which multiple lysosomal enzymes fail to reach lysosomes, causing accumulation of storage material. It may produce coarse facies, gingival or tongue enlargement, developmental impairment, hearing loss, skeletal abnormalities, and progressive motor disability.
symptoms_in_common: Brain white-matter abnormalities may occur in affected individuals
symptoms_not_in_common: Mucolipidosis type II usually presents from birth or early infancy with severe skeletal disease and growth failure, which are not described
No joint contractures, hip dysplasia, bone deformities, gingival hypertrophy, or short stature is reported
A primarily progressive neurologic phenotype beginning at 30 months is more suggestive of another lysosomal disorder

data.description: A male neonate, born at 36+1 weeks gestation via cesarean section due to scarred uterus and fetal heart rate deceleration, weighing 2700g with Apgar scores of 2-8-9. The infant experienced severe asphyxia at birth requiring intubation and chest compressions. After resuscitation, he presented with respiratory distress and difficulty breathing. Following extubation from mechanical ventilation on day 6, the patient developed recurrent inspiratory dyspnea and stridor. The infant had no relevant family history and no history of laryngeal or thoracic surgery.

Impaired movement of both vocal folds, often leaving them near the midline and producing a critically narrowed glottic airway. In neonates it may be congenital or associated with hypoxic-ischemic injury.
symptoms_in_common: Severe airway obstruction with a very narrow glottic opening on laryngoscopy
History of severe perinatal asphyxia, which can be associated with neurologic injury affecting vocal-fold motion
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear symptoms are strongly atypical; the early respiratory distress may also have been partly related to the initial birth asphyxia

data.description: Loss of movement of one vocal fold due to recurrent laryngeal nerve or central neurologic dysfunction. It usually causes a weak cry, hoarseness, aspiration, or milder stridor than bilateral paralysis.
symptoms_in_common: Potential association with traumatic or hypoxic neurologic injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe recurrent airway obstruction is more typical of bilateral than unilateral paralysis
No weak cry or hoarseness is reported
No feeding difficulty, choking, or aspiration is reported

data.description: Scarring or fixation of the posterior glottis after endotracheal intubation, causing reduced vocal-fold abduction and a narrow airway that can mimic bilateral vocal fold paralysis.
symptoms_in_common: History of endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation
Narrow glottic airway on endoscopic examination
symptoms_not_in_common: The intubation duration of approximately 6 days is relatively short for significant mature scar-related stenosis
Symptoms occurring immediately after extubation may be more consistent with edema or pre-existing vocal-fold dysfunction than established scar stenosis
No history of repeated or prolonged intubations is reported

data.description: Swelling of the laryngeal mucosa caused by endotracheal tube irritation or traumatic intubation, producing temporary narrowing of the glottic or subglottic airway.
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent or persistent symptoms are less typical if edema does not improve over time
Markedly restricted vocal-fold opening on imaging is more suggestive of vocal-fold immobility or fixation
Severe perinatal asphyxia is not a typical cause of isolated laryngeal edema

data.description: The most common congenital cause of neonatal stridor, caused by dynamic collapse of supraglottic tissues during inspiration.
symptoms_not_in_common: Stridor beginning specifically after extubation is less typical
A fixed narrow glottic opening is not typical because laryngomalacia primarily affects supraglottic structures
Severe airway obstruction requiring prior intubation is less typical in uncomplicated laryngomalacia
No feeding-related worsening, regurgitation, or poor weight gain is reported

diagnoses.name: Bilateral vocal cord paralysis
diagnoses.title: Paralysis of vocal cords or larynx[Bilateral]

data.description: 24-year-old man presented with a 2-day history of swelling on the left side of neck and fever. Past medical history included two similar neck abscesses 2 years and 6 years ago, which were treated with antibiotics and drainage. Physical examination showed a 2 cm diameter swelling at the level of thyroid cartilage.

data.diagnosis: Pyriform sinus fistula (fourth branchial pouch anomaly)
data.description: A congenital tract arising from the apex of the pyriform sinus that commonly presents on the left side with recurrent neck infections or abscesses, often near the thyroid gland.
symptoms_in_common: Lesion near the level of the thyroid cartilage
Prior need for drainage and antibiotics

data.diagnosis: Third branchial cleft sinus or fistula
data.description: A rare congenital branchial anomaly that can form a sinus tract in the lower lateral neck and cause repeated infections or abscess formation.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported dysphagia
No reported odynophagia
No reported respiratory symptoms

data.description: A congenital cystic neck lesion that typically occurs along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle and may become infected, causing painful swelling and fever.
symptoms_in_common: History of recurrent infected neck mass
Improvement with antibiotics and drainage during prior episodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Swelling is at the thyroid cartilage/lower central neck rather than the typical upper lateral neck location
Multiple recurrent abscesses strongly suggest a persistent internal fistula rather than an isolated cyst

data.description: A bacterial infection of the thyroid gland, often associated with an underlying pyriform sinus fistula in younger patients and usually involving the left thyroid lobe.
symptoms_in_common: Acute neck swelling near the thyroid cartilage
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported thyroid pain
No reported painful swallowing
No reported thyroid function abnormalities

data.diagnosis: Recurrent cervical deep neck abscess or suppurative cervical lymphadenitis
data.description: A bacterial infection of cervical lymph nodes or deep neck spaces causing localized swelling, fever, and possible abscess formation; recurrent disease should prompt evaluation for an underlying congenital tract.
symptoms_in_common: Prior response requiring antibiotics and drainage
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeated infections in the same left lower-neck region are less typical without an underlying anatomical abnormality
No reported dental infection
No reported upper respiratory or throat infection preceding the episodes

data.description: 35-year-old female with a history of intermittent rhinitis presented with 5 days of urticaria, fever, severe headaches, myalgia, and arthralgia. She developed pruritic, painful wheals and erythematous macules >1 cm with burning sensation on the limbs; lesions lasted >24 hours and left skin pigmentation changes. Angioedema involved the hands, fingers, ankles, and feet without pitting. Fever reached 39.5°C, and headache and myalgia impaired daily activities. She had taken over-the-counter diet pills 18 days before symptom onset and had been seen 6 days earlier for dehydration and violaceous palmar hives, after which she stopped the pills. Examination showed large confluent wheals and macules on the limbs with pruritus rated 6/10 and muscle pain. Labs showed lymphopenia and mildly elevated CRP (7.5 mg/L); other routine tests, complement, thyroid studies, and ANA were normal/negative. Skin biopsy showed papillary dermal edema, superficial perivascular lymphocytic and eosinophilic infiltrate, focal fibrin in vessel walls, and erythrocyte extravasation.

A delayed immune-mediated reaction to a medication or supplement, characterized by urticarial eruptions, fever, joint symptoms, and sometimes angioedema; complement levels are often normal in serum sickness-like reactions.
symptoms_in_common: Onset after over-the-counter diet pill exposure
Angioedema of hands, fingers, ankles, and feet
Lymphocytic and eosinophilic perivascular infiltrate on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Individual lesions lasting longer than 24 hours with residual pigmentation are more suggestive of urticarial vasculitis
Focal fibrin in vessel walls suggests a vasculitic component
Severe headache is less characteristic

data.description: A small-vessel cutaneous vasculitis presenting with urticarial lesions that are painful or burning, persist for more than 24 hours, and may resolve with bruising or hyperpigmentation. Systemic symptoms such as fever, arthralgia, myalgia, and angioedema can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous macules and large confluent wheals
Focal fibrin in vessel walls on biopsy
Normal complement levels, consistent with normocomplementemic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent pruritus is more typical of ordinary urticaria than vasculitic lesions
Clear temporal association with diet pills suggests a drug-triggered reaction rather than idiopathic disease
Lymphopenia is not a typical defining feature

data.description: An acute hypersensitivity reaction causing transient itchy wheals and localized swelling, often triggered by medications, supplements, foods, or infections.
symptoms_in_common: Recent exposure to over-the-counter diet pills
Angioedema involving hands, fingers, ankles, and feet
History of intermittent rhinitis, indicating an atopic tendency
Dermal edema and eosinophilic infiltrate on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions persisted longer than 24 hours
Residual pigmentation after lesions
Pain and burning rather than predominantly itch
High fever
Severe headache
Marked myalgia and arthralgia
Fibrin in vessel walls and erythrocyte extravasation on biopsy

data.diagnosis: DRESS syndrome (drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms)
data.description: A severe delayed drug hypersensitivity syndrome, usually occurring 2 to 8 weeks after exposure, with fever, widespread rash, facial edema, hematologic abnormalities, and internal-organ involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Delayed onset after diet pill exposure
Eosinophils present in the skin biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported peripheral eosinophilia
Lymphopenia rather than the more typical atypical lymphocytosis
No liver, kidney, lung, or other internal-organ involvement
Lesions are urticarial wheals rather than the typical morbilliform eruption
No facial edema or lymphadenopathy reported
Onset 18 days after exposure is somewhat earlier than typical

data.description: A systemic immune-complex vasculitis with recurrent urticarial lesions lasting more than 24 hours, often accompanied by low complement levels, arthralgia, angioedema, and potential renal, pulmonary, or ocular disease.
symptoms_in_common: Urticarial lesions lasting more than 24 hours
Histologic vascular injury with fibrin and erythrocyte extravasation
symptoms_not_in_common: Complement levels were normal
No renal involvement reported
No pulmonary disease reported
No ocular inflammation reported
Negative ANA and no evidence of systemic autoimmune disease
Acute onset after diet pill use favors a drug-induced reaction

data.description:
16-year-old girl with 4 weeks of intermittent severe sharp abdominal pain, worst in the epigastrium and upper quadrants, increasing in frequency over 2 weeks from every few days to twice daily and later lasting up to 15 minutes. Two weeks before admission she developed nausea and vomiting, with worsening episodes that woke her from sleep and caused missed school. Pain was abrupt, followed by nausea, and vomiting relieved it somewhat; it was not related to menstruation, position, meals, or time of day. She also had decreased appetite, fatigue, dizziness, generalized weakness, and worsening constipation, with last bowel movement 3 days before admission. 

At initial evaluation she was tachycardic and had dry mucous membranes and diffuse abdominal tenderness with guarding, especially in the epigastrium and upper quadrants. Labs showed leukocytosis, anemia with microcytosis, thrombocytosis, and elevated ESR; urinalysis was normal and abdominal/pelvic ultrasound was unrevealing. Medical history included iron-deficiency anemia and anxiety disorder; medications were iron, oral contraception, and famotidine.

A large gastric trichobezoar (hair ball) with a tail extending beyond the stomach into the small intestine, potentially causing intermittent gastric outlet or intestinal obstruction. The imaging appearance is highly characteristic.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent severe epigastric and upper abdominal pain
Early obstructive symptoms worsening over several weeks
Palpable or radiologically visible intragastric mass
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported history of hair pulling or hair eating
No reported weight loss
No reported halitosis
No reported alopecia

data.description: An accumulation of swallowed hair in the stomach that forms a dense, matted mass. It can cause gastric outlet obstruction, mucosal injury, anemia, and abdominal pain; this may be confined to the stomach or represent the gastric component of Rapunzel syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Symptoms of partial gastric outlet obstruction
Endoscopic appearance of a large hair-containing gastric mass
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hair ingestion behavior
No reported hair loss or bald patches
Pain is not specifically meal-related
No reported weight loss

data.description: Mechanical obstruction of the small intestine caused by a bezoar or a tail of a gastric trichobezoar. Obstruction may be intermittent initially and progress to more frequent pain and vomiting.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt intermittent cramp-like severe abdominal pain
Vomiting with partial relief of pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain is predominantly epigastric rather than diffuse or periumbilical
No reported abdominal distension
No reported inability to pass flatus
Four-week intermittent course is longer than many acute complete obstructions

data.diagnosis: Peptic ulcer disease or erosive gastritis
data.description: Inflammation or ulceration of the stomach or duodenum can cause epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and iron-deficiency anemia from chronic occult blood loss.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain is not related to meals
Pain is abrupt and intermittent with vomiting relief, suggesting obstruction more than ulcer disease
Worsening constipation is not typical
Large hair-containing gastric mass on imaging is not explained by peptic ulcer disease
No reported gastrointestinal bleeding, melena, or hematemesis

data.description: Inflammation of the pancreas that typically produces severe persistent epigastric pain with nausea and vomiting, often radiating to the back.
symptoms_in_common: Severe epigastric and upper abdominal pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain is intermittent and brief rather than persistent
No radiation of pain to the back is reported
Vomiting partially relieves the pain, which is more suggestive of obstruction
Constipation is not a prominent typical feature
No elevated pancreatic enzyme results are provided
The gastric hair-containing mass on imaging is not explained by pancreatitis

data.description: A 45-year-old white man was found dead at home and underwent autopsy as the cause of death was not apparent. He had recently been under review by the respiratory team for poor respiratory function and patchy fibronodular lung changes. His medical history included osteomyelitis of the elbow, congenital kyphoscoliosis, and testicular seminoma, which had been treated with orchidectomy and chemotherapy. At postmortem examination, the abdominal cavity contained copious pus covering the serosal aspect of the small bowel. There was an obvious perforation at the level of the mid-ileum, as well as three ulcers on the mucosal aspect of the ileum, one of which had perforated. Widespread pale nodules measuring up to 5 mm each were noted throughout the parenchyma of both lungs and a small pale lesion was present in the left kidney. No abnormalities were seen in the cardiovascular, endocrine, or central nervous systems.

Hematogenous Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving the lungs, ileum, and kidney, with ulcerative ileal disease causing perforation and tuberculous peritonitis. Histology showing granulomatous inflammation and acid-fast bacilli strongly supports this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Numerous small pale nodules throughout both lungs
Acid-fast bacilli demonstrated on special stain
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, weight loss, night sweats, or chronic cough were reported
Previous testicular seminoma is not a typical feature of tuberculosis
Congenital kyphoscoliosis is not a typical feature of tuberculosis

data.description: A disseminated form of tuberculosis caused by hematogenous spread, classically producing innumerable tiny nodules in the lungs and potentially involving the gastrointestinal tract, kidneys, and other organs.
symptoms_not_in_common: No abnormalities were identified in the central nervous system, endocrine organs, or cardiovascular system despite widespread disease
No reported prolonged fever, severe constitutional symptoms, or hepatosplenomegaly
Purulent peritonitis is a complication of intestinal involvement rather than a usual primary presentation

data.description: Systemic infection with environmental mycobacteria, such as Mycobacterium avium complex, which can cause pulmonary disease and disseminated granulomatous infection, particularly in immunocompromised individuals.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary nodules and fibronodular lung disease
Possible extrapulmonary renal and intestinal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Ileal ulceration with perforation is less typical than in intestinal tuberculosis
No known severe immunodeficiency was reported
The combination of fibronodular lung disease and intestinal ulceration is more characteristic of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
No reported chronic fever, marked weight loss, or anemia

data.description: A systemic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum that may produce pulmonary nodules and granulomatous disease, with gastrointestinal ulceration in disseminated cases.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acid-fast bacilli are not typical of histoplasmosis
No fungal yeasts were described in the tissue
Ileal perforation with acid-fast organisms favors tuberculosis over histoplasmosis
No reported immunosuppression or exposure history supporting disseminated histoplasmosis

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that commonly affects the terminal ileum and can cause deep ulcers, transmural inflammation, strictures, fistulas, and bowel perforation; noncaseating granulomas may be present.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse pulmonary nodules and fibronodular lung changes are not typical
Acid-fast bacilli are not a feature of Crohn disease
Renal pale lesion suggesting disseminated infection is not typical
No reported chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, or weight loss before death

data.description: 33-year-old white man with chest pain սկսing 2 hours before admission: epigastric pain progressed to central chest pain, with one episode of vomiting, dizziness, dyspnea, diaphoresis, and distal paresthesias. Pain resolved on arrival. Later the same day he became nauseated, pale, diaphoretic, with blurred vision, muffled hearing, and tingling in both hands; systolic blood pressure fell to 89 mm Hg and cardiac monitoring showed a 3–4 second pause without P waves. History of syncope with phlebotomy. Had flu-like symptoms, and his daughter had gastroenteritis. Physical examination was normal before and after the hypotensive episode.

A reflex-mediated autonomic event causing hypotension and sometimes marked sinus bradycardia or transient sinus arrest, often triggered by pain, nausea, vomiting, emotional stress, or medical procedures.
symptoms_in_common: Hypotension with systolic blood pressure of 89 mm Hg
Transient 3–4 second pause without P waves
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial epigastric pain progressing to central chest pain
Dyspnea during the initial chest-pain episode
Flu-like prodrome

data.description: Inflammation of the myocardium and/or pericardium, commonly following a viral illness, which can cause chest pain, electrocardiographic ST-segment abnormalities, arrhythmias, and occasionally hemodynamic instability.
symptoms_in_common: Possible transient arrhythmia or sinus pause
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain resolved rapidly before evaluation
No reported fever
No persistent chest pain
No reported positional or pleuritic character of chest pain
History of syncope specifically triggered by phlebotomy

data.description: Acute coronary artery obstruction causing myocardial ischemia and injury, classically presenting with central chest pressure, autonomic symptoms, and ST-segment elevation in anterior precordial ECG leads.
symptoms_in_common: Epigastric pain that may represent an anginal equivalent
Anterior precordial ST-segment elevation on the ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 33 years with no stated cardiovascular risk factors
Pain resolved on arrival
Flu-like symptoms and household gastroenteritis exposure
Pronounced vagal prodrome with muffled hearing, blurred vision, and bilateral hand tingling
Prior syncope with phlebotomy

data.description: Transient spasm of a coronary artery causing episodic myocardial ischemia, often with transient ST-segment elevation and chest pain that can resolve spontaneously.
symptoms_not_in_common: Flu-like illness
History of phlebotomy-triggered syncope
Prominent presyncope with blurred vision, muffled hearing, and hand tingling
Documented sinus pause without P waves, which more strongly suggests a vagal cardioinhibitory event

data.diagnosis: Acute gastroenteritis with nausea-induced vagal reaction
data.description: An acute gastrointestinal viral illness can cause epigastric pain, vomiting, and nausea; gastrointestinal distress can trigger a strong vagal reflex with hypotension and transient bradycardia or sinus arrest.
symptoms_not_in_common: Central chest pain
Dyspnea
Electrocardiographic ST-segment abnormalities
No reported diarrhea
No reported abdominal tenderness or persistent gastrointestinal symptoms

data.description: A 21-year-old man presented to his general practitioner with intermittent left-sided pain in the anterior chest wall associated with neck discomfort. The pain was described as 'stabbing' in nature and had arisen suddenly while watching television, with no history of trauma before onset. The pain was not exacerbated by inspiration or effort. His medical history and physical examination were initially unremarkable. Several days later, he attended the emergency department with worsening chest pain and dyspnea. On examination, chest expansion was equal and breath sounds were normal, although there was crepitus on auscultation of the precordium. Palpation of the neck and supraclavicular fossae detected subcutaneous emphysema. His respiratory rate was 25 breaths per minute and oxygen saturations were 100%. His full blood count and inflammatory markers were within normal limits.
Free air within the mediastinum occurring without trauma or an invasive procedure, often caused by alveolar rupture with air tracking into the mediastinum and neck tissues.
symptoms_in_common: Subcutaneous emphysema in the neck and supraclavicular fossae

data.description: A full-thickness tear of the esophagus that can release air and gastrointestinal contents into the mediastinum, causing pneumomediastinum and potentially severe mediastinitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of severe vomiting or retching
No fever
Normal inflammatory markers
No signs of systemic toxicity
No dysphagia or odynophagia reported
Several-day course without rapid clinical deterioration

data.description: Accumulation of air in the pleural space without trauma, most often in young adults, producing sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath.
symptoms_in_common: Normal oxygen saturation can occur in a small pneumothorax
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain was not worsened by inspiration
Breath sounds were normal and equal
Chest expansion was equal
Subcutaneous neck emphysema is not typical in an uncomplicated small pneumothorax
Imaging primarily demonstrates mediastinal rather than pleural air

data.description: A tear in the trachea or major bronchi can allow air to enter the mediastinum and subcutaneous tissues, typically after major blunt trauma, intubation, or airway procedures.
symptoms_not_in_common: No trauma
No recent intubation or airway procedure
No respiratory distress or hypoxemia
Normal and equal breath sounds
No hemoptysis reported

data.description: Inflammation of the pericardial sac, commonly viral or idiopathic, causing sharp chest pain that often varies with position or breathing and may be associated with a pericardial friction rub.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain was not worsened by inspiration
No positional component reported
Subcutaneous emphysema is not typical
Precordial crepitus rather than a pericardial friction rub
Pneumomediastinum on imaging is not typical
No fever or inflammatory marker elevation

data.description: 34-year-old man in Scotland presented with an expanding itchy rash on the right flank that persisted for three months. He did not recall any insect bite or foreign travel history, but regularly visits the Scottish highlands. Initial Borrelia serology performed at 4 weeks after rash onset was negative.

Early localized infection with Borrelia bacteria transmitted by Ixodes ticks. Erythema migrans is an enlarging red patch or annular rash, often with central clearing, and may occur without a recalled tick bite.
symptoms_in_common: Expanding annular rash with central clearing
Regular exposure in the Scottish Highlands, where tick exposure is possible
No recalled insect bite does not exclude tick bite
Initial Borrelia serology can be negative early in infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked itch is less typical than a non-itchy or mildly symptomatic erythema migrans rash
Persistence for three months without other reported Lyme symptoms is less typical for untreated early localized disease

data.description: A superficial dermatophyte fungal infection of the skin that commonly causes an itchy, enlarging ring-shaped rash with a more active red edge and relative central clearing.
symptoms_in_common: Red, more prominent border with central clearing
Persistence over several months can occur if untreated
symptoms_not_in_common: No scaling or raised scaly border is described or clearly visible
Regular visits to the Scottish Highlands and concern for tick exposure are not specifically associated with fungal infection
The lesion appears relatively large and uniform compared with many typical tinea corporis lesions

data.description: A reactive inflammatory skin eruption characterized by slowly expanding annular red patches or plaques, sometimes triggered by infections, medications, fungal disease, or an unidentified cause.
symptoms_in_common: Can persist for weeks to months
symptoms_not_in_common: No characteristic trailing inner scale is described
The Scottish Highlands exposure history is not specifically relevant
The lesion's appearance is strongly suggestive of erythema migrans in the setting of possible tick exposure

data.description: Inflammation of the skin caused by contact with an allergen or irritant, such as clothing materials, topical products, plants, adhesives, or occupational exposures.
symptoms_in_common: Rash can remain present or recur for a prolonged period if exposure continues
symptoms_not_in_common: A progressively expanding annular lesion with central clearing is not the usual pattern
No exposure to a new topical product, chemical, adhesive, plant, or clothing-related trigger is reported
Three months of expansion despite no stated repeated contact is less typical

data.description: A benign inflammatory skin condition that produces ring-shaped papules or plaques, usually without scale. It may occur on the hands and feet but can also appear on the trunk.
symptoms_not_in_common: Granuloma annulare is usually not itchy
It typically consists of firm raised papules rather than a broad expanding red patch
Central clearing with a rapidly enlarging erythematous border is more characteristic of erythema migrans or tinea corporis
Potential tick exposure in the Scottish Highlands is not associated with granuloma annulare

data.description: A 39-year-old man with a history of current smoking and no other medical history presented with left-sided squeezing chest pain that was worse in the early morning after drinking alcohol and lasted 30 minutes. Initial vital signs showed blood pressure of 132/89 mmHg and pulse rate of 98 beats/minute. Initial laboratory findings revealed creatine kinase 118 U/L (normal 58-348), CK-MB 1.7 ug/L (normal 0-5.0), elevated highly sensitive troponin-T 0.027 ng/mL (normal 0-0.014), and microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL. Echocardiography showed normal-sized cardiac chambers with good left ventricular systolic function (ejection fraction of 61%) and no regional wall motion abnormality.

data.diagnosis: Vasospastic angina (Prinzmetal angina) with myocardial injury
data.description: Transient coronary artery spasm causing episodic myocardial ischemia, often occurring at rest in the early morning and strongly associated with smoking. Spasm can cause ECG ischemic changes and a small troponin rise despite nonobstructive coronary arteries between episodes.
symptoms_in_common: Squeezing left-sided chest pain at rest
Preserved left ventricular ejection fraction and no regional wall-motion abnormality
Coronary imaging without a clear fixed obstructive lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.description: Acute myocardial infarction caused by myocardial ischemia and necrosis, typically identified by elevated cardiac troponin with ischemic chest symptoms and/or ECG changes. It may result from plaque disruption, coronary spasm, embolism, or supply-demand imbalance.
symptoms_in_common: ECG ischemic repolarization abnormalities, including anterior T-wave changes
Smoking as a cardiovascular risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal CK-MB
Normal creatine kinase
No regional wall-motion abnormality on echocardiography
Young age with few conventional atherosclerotic risk factors
Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.diagnosis: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA)
data.description: A working diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction in which coronary angiography does not show an obstructive epicardial coronary lesion. Potential mechanisms include coronary vasospasm, plaque erosion or rupture, coronary embolism, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, and microvascular dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: No fixed obstructive coronary lesion apparent on angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic hypochromic anemia
Normal CK-MB and creatine kinase despite troponin elevation

data.diagnosis: Wellens syndrome (critical proximal left anterior descending coronary artery ischemia pattern)
data.description: An ECG syndrome characterized by biphasic or deeply inverted T waves in the anterior precordial leads, classically indicating critical proximal left anterior descending artery stenosis and high risk of anterior myocardial infarction. Similar ECG changes can also occur with coronary spasm as pseudo-Wellens syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Recent episode of anginal chest pain
Anterior precordial T-wave abnormalities on ECG
Preserved ventricular function can occur early in the condition
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of a clearly fixed critical proximal left anterior descending artery obstruction on coronary imaging
Early-morning and alcohol-associated episodes, which favor coronary spasm
Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.diagnosis: Type 2 myocardial infarction due to oxygen supply-demand mismatch from iron-deficiency anemia
data.description: Myocardial injury or infarction caused by inadequate myocardial oxygen supply relative to demand rather than acute coronary thrombosis. Significant anemia can contribute to ischemic chest pain and troponin elevation, particularly when another trigger such as coronary vasospasm is present.
symptoms_in_common: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin of 9.8 g/dL
Normal or nonobstructive coronary angiographic findings may be present
symptoms_not_in_common: Early-morning episodic chest pain after alcohol intake
Current smoking-associated vasospastic trigger
Anterior ischemic T-wave abnormalities suggesting focal coronary ischemia
Chest pain pattern occurring at rest rather than during increased oxygen demand

data.description: 12-year-old Saudi boy presented with severe spontaneous dental pain for 3 days. He was the fourth of five siblings. Parents were not related. His mother had 5 previous spontaneous abortions in first trimester. Mother took acetazolamide 1000mg/day for idiopathic intracranial hypertension before and throughout pregnancy. Patient was born at full term via spontaneous vaginal delivery, weighing 2,270g (below 5th percentile). He presented without major dysmorphic features, was intelligent with good behavior, and had normal skin, hair and nails. Intraoral exam showed mixed dentition with retained primary lower central incisors, hypocalcified permanent upper incisors, and multiple carious teeth. Tongue, floor of mouth, upper lip, hard and soft palate were normal.

A pattern of congenital malformations potentially associated with fetal exposure to acetazolamide, including limb-reduction defects, digital anomalies, and occasionally craniofacial or dental developmental abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Continuous high-dose maternal acetazolamide exposure before and throughout pregnancy
Bilateral congenital hand and foot digital malformations consistent with oligodactyly/ectrodactyly
Multiple missing or developmentally abnormal teeth
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe spontaneous dental pain for 3 days
Multiple dental caries
Maternal history of recurrent first-trimester spontaneous abortions

data.description: A genetic disorder characterized by split hand/foot malformations, missing teeth or abnormal tooth enamel, ectodermal abnormalities, and frequently cleft lip and/or palate.
symptoms_in_common: Dental agenesis or delayed eruption suggested by retained primary teeth and absent permanent teeth on panoramic imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal skin, hair and nails
Normal upper lip, hard palate and soft palate without clefting
No major dysmorphic facial features
Prenatal acetazolamide exposure
Low birth weight

data.description: A congenital limb-malformation phenotype involving central digital absence or clefting of the hands and feet, sometimes accompanied by hypodontia or oligodontia without the ectodermal and clefting features of EEC syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Panoramic radiograph suggesting multiple absent or delayed-developing permanent teeth
symptoms_not_in_common: Low birth weight
Severe dental pain
Multiple active dental caries
Maternal acetazolamide exposure
History of recurrent maternal spontaneous abortions

data.description: A heterogeneous group of genetic disorders causing digital malformations and dental abnormalities, often associated with oral frenula, tongue lobulation, cleft palate, facial changes, and sometimes intellectual or renal abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Digital malformations of the hands and feet
Possible tooth agenesis on panoramic imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal tongue and floor of mouth
Normal upper lip and hard and soft palate
No reported oral frenula, tongue clefting, or tongue lobulation
No major facial dysmorphism
Normal intelligence and behavior
Prenatal acetazolamide exposure

data.description: A teratogenic embryopathy characterized by congenital limb-reduction defects, including absent or malformed digits and limbs; dental developmental defects can occur in some fetal drug-exposure syndromes.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital bilateral hand and foot limb/digital reduction abnormalities
Possible tooth agenesis or delayed tooth eruption
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported thalidomide exposure
Maternal exposure was to acetazolamide rather than thalidomide
No reported ear, eye, cardiac, renal, or gastrointestinal malformations
Severe dental pain from caries is not a defining feature
Normal skin, hair and nails

data.description: 62-year-old man with hypertension on amlodipine presented with palpitations occurring four times in the past week, associated with rapid heartbeat and shortness of breath; two episodes followed alcohol intake. He denied chest pain and syncope. Exam showed blood pressure 160/90 mm Hg, regular pulse 82/min, and normal cardiac and respiratory examinations. Holter monitoring recorded two episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, with frequent supraventricular ectopy.
An intermittent supraventricular arrhythmia characterized by uncoordinated atrial electrical activity and an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm; episodes terminate spontaneously.
symptoms_in_common: Holter-documented two episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain
No syncope
Normal regular pulse between episodes

data.diagnosis: Alcohol-triggered paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (holiday heart syndrome)
data.description: Atrial fibrillation precipitated by acute alcohol intake, often occurring in people without severe structural heart disease but more likely in those with cardiovascular risk factors such as hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Episodes that are intermittent rather than persistent
symptoms_not_in_common: No information about binge or heavy alcohol consumption
Hypertension may indicate an additional underlying predisposition rather than alcohol as the sole cause
No chest pain
No syncope

data.description: Early atrial beats arising outside the sinus node that can cause skipped beats, fluttering, or palpitations and may trigger atrial fibrillation.
symptoms_in_common: Frequent supraventricular ectopic beats on Holter monitoring
Supraventricular couplets and runs on Holter monitoring
Association with alcohol intake, which can increase atrial ectopy
Normal pulse and cardiac examination between symptomatic episodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is more significant than isolated premature atrial contractions alone
Shortness of breath is less typical with isolated premature atrial contractions
Sustained rapid-heartbeat episodes are less typical for isolated ectopic beats

data.description: A sudden-onset, sudden-termination fast rhythm originating above the ventricles, commonly causing episodic palpitations and dyspnea.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt recurrent episodes of rapid heartbeat
Normal heart rate and regular pulse between episodes
Supraventricular ectopy and short supraventricular runs on Holter monitoring
symptoms_not_in_common: Holter monitoring specifically documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation rather than a re-entrant supraventricular tachycardia
No syncope
No chest pain
Alcohol-related episodes are more classically associated with atrial fibrillation

data.description: A macroreentrant atrial tachyarrhythmia that can produce palpitations, dyspnea, and rapid ventricular rates; it may coexist with or alternate with atrial fibrillation.
symptoms_in_common: Hypertension as a predisposing cardiovascular condition
Frequent atrial ectopy, which may reflect atrial electrical instability
symptoms_not_in_common: Holter report identifies paroxysmal atrial fibrillation rather than atrial flutter
No documented characteristic flutter-wave rhythm
No chest pain
No syncope

data.description: A 58-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. He also experienced urinary symptoms including frequency, urgency, and dysuria. Initial colonoscopy revealed prominent congestion and edema, loss of vascular pattern, and multiple moth-eaten ulcers with purulent exudates involving the entire colon. A repeat colonoscopy showed scattered irregular ulcers with with granular background mucosa and 'fuzzy' vasculature. The ileum appeared normal.

data.diagnosis: Primary colorectal extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
data.description: An aggressive Epstein-Barr virus-associated cytotoxic lymphoid malignancy that can rarely arise in the colon and produce destructive ulcerative colitis-like lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Normal-appearing ileum despite extensive colonic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria

data.description: A rare aggressive intestinal T-cell lymphoma, often composed of monomorphic cytotoxic lymphocytes, which may cause multifocal ulceration, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss.
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria
Disease limited to the colon with a normal ileum is less typical

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by continuous mucosal inflammation of the colon, causing congestion, edema, loss of vascular pattern, friability, and ulceration.
symptoms_not_in_common: Moth-eaten scattered irregular ulcers with purulent exudate
Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria

data.description: A chronic transmural inflammatory bowel disease that can cause discontinuous colonic inflammation, deep irregular ulcers, diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, and fistulizing complications.

symptoms_not_in_common: Normal ileum

symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria

data.description: A previously healthy 9-year-old boy presented to the emergency department with a 6-hour history of left chest pain and increasing respiratory distress. His vital signs showed a respiratory rate of 40/min and heart rate of 105/min. Physical examination revealed unremarkable cardiac auscultation, while auscultation of lung fields showed diminished breath sounds over the left side.

data.diagnosis: Ruptured pulmonary hydatid cyst (echinococcal cyst) with hydropneumothorax
data.description: A parasitic Echinococcus cyst in the lung that ruptures into a bronchus or pleural space, producing an air-fluid level and detached internal membranes on chest radiography.

symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No cough or expectoration of cyst material reported
No history of exposure to dogs or livestock provided

data.description: The simultaneous presence of air and fluid in the pleural space, which can compress the lung and cause acute respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Diminished breath sounds on the left
Left pleural air-fluid level on chest radiography
symptoms_not_in_common: No preceding trauma reported
No known recent thoracic procedure reported
No fever or systemic infectious symptoms reported

data.description: Air enters the pleural space without trauma, causing partial or complete lung collapse and acute pleuritic chest pain with dyspnea.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced breath sounds over the affected left lung
symptoms_not_in_common: A prominent pleural fluid level is not typical of an uncomplicated pneumothorax
Internal floating membrane-like radiographic findings are not typical
No clear pleural line or purely air-filled pleural collection is described

data.description: Infected pleural fluid (empyema) may communicate with the bronchial tree, creating a hydropneumothorax and respiratory compromise.
symptoms_in_common: Diminished breath sounds on the left
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No preceding pneumonia or prolonged cough reported
Abrupt onset over 6 hours is less typical
Internal detached membranes on imaging are not typical

data.diagnosis: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation or other cystic lung lesion complicated by infection or rupture
data.description: A congenital cystic lesion of the lung can become infected, communicate with an airway, or rupture, potentially producing an air-fluid level and acute respiratory symptoms.

symptoms_not_in_common: No prior recurrent respiratory infections reported
No known congenital lung abnormality reported
Acute chest pain is less characteristic as the initial presentation
Membrane-like structures within the lesion are more suggestive of a ruptured hydatid cyst

data.description: 63-year-old man with well-controlled hypertension and diabetes was referred from primary clinic due to hepatic mass found on ultrasonography. Physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory findings showed normal hematological indexes, liver function tests, and renal functions. Patient was negative for viral markers with normal α-fetoprotein levels. Bone marrow biopsy showed 30% marrow cellularity but was otherwise normal. Serum calcium, β-2 microglobulin, and serum/urine protein immunoelectrophoresis were normal. Skeletal radiography revealed no abnormalities.

data.diagnosis: Solitary extramedullary plasmacytoma of the liver
data.description: A localized monoclonal plasma-cell tumor arising outside bone marrow; primary hepatic involvement is very rare and may occur without systemic multiple myeloma.
symptoms_in_common: Normal bone marrow examination without plasma-cell proliferation
Normal serum and urine protein immunoelectrophoresis
Histology showing sheets of plasmacytoid cells
Immunohistochemical staining consistent with plasma-cell differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as weight loss, fever, or night sweats
Normal liver function tests despite a hepatic mass

data.description: A systemic malignant plasma-cell disorder that usually involves bone marrow and may rarely produce focal or diffuse liver involvement.

Normal renal function

Possible absence of abnormalities on physical examination

No fever, weight loss, night sweats, or lymphadenopathy

data.description: A primary malignant tumor of hepatocytes, most commonly associated with chronic hepatitis B or C infection, cirrhosis, or other chronic liver disease.

Negative viral markers
Normal liver function tests

Plasma-cell immunophenotype is not typical of hepatocellular carcinoma

symptoms_in_common: Normal liver function tests can occur
No major abnormalities on physical examination
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology suggests a dense, relatively uniform plasma-cell neoplasm rather than mixed inflammation and fibrosis

No fever, abdominal pain, or inflammatory laboratory abnormalities

data.description: Young female European traveler presented to a clinic in central Australia with vaginal discharge after having sex with a new partner, also a European traveler, 1 week earlier in Sydney.
A common sexually transmitted bacterial infection that may cause cervicitis, vaginal discharge, bleeding, pelvic discomfort, or no symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sex with a new partner
Symptoms occurring about 1 week after sexual exposure

data.description: A sexually transmitted bacterial infection that can infect the cervix and cause increased or purulent vaginal discharge, urinary symptoms, pelvic pain, or no symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Recent unprotected or new-partner sexual exposure
Onset within approximately 1 week can be consistent with gonorrhea

data.description: A sexually transmitted infection caused by the protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis, often producing vaginal discharge, irritation, odor, and discomfort with urination or sex.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sexual contact with a new partner
symptoms_not_in_common: Very rapid onset at 1 week is less typical, as symptoms may take longer to develop

data.description: A disruption of normal vaginal bacteria that commonly causes thin vaginal discharge and a fishy odor; it is associated with sexual activity but is not usually classified as a conventional STI.
symptoms_in_common: New sexual partner can be associated with bacterial vaginosis
symptoms_not_in_common: The discharge beginning specifically after a new sexual exposure may suggest an STI more strongly than bacterial vaginosis

data.description: An overgrowth of Candida yeast in the vagina that usually causes thick discharge, itching, burning, and vulvar irritation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent sex with a new partner is not a typical cause of yeast infection
No itching, vulvar irritation, or burning was reported

data.description: A 44-year-old man with a 17-year history of tobacco and cannabis use presented with acute dyspnoea and left-sided pleuritic chest pain. He had no other medical conditions and took no regular medications. On examination, he was thin and hypoxic, with a silent, hyper-resonant left hemithorax. Laboratory results showed normal α-1 antitrypsin concentration (1.4 g/L), normal immunoglobulins, and specific IgE for Aspergillus. Spirometry revealed severe obstruction with FVC of 2.95 L (57% predicted), FEV1 of 1.37 L (34% predicted), and FEV1/FVC ratio of 59% predicted.

A severe form of bullous emphysema characterized by giant air-filled bullae, usually in the upper lungs, that compress adjacent normal lung tissue. It is strongly associated with cigarette smoking and cannabis use.
symptoms_in_common: Long history of tobacco and cannabis smoking
Imaging showing a very large left-sided bulla with compression of residual lung
symptoms_not_in_common: No chronic cough or sputum production was reported
The acute onset of pain may indicate a complication such as pneumothorax rather than uncomplicated giant bullous emphysema

data.diagnosis: Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax due to ruptured emphysematous bullae
data.description: Air entering the pleural space because of rupture of a subpleural bleb or bulla, commonly occurring in people with smoking-related emphysema or giant bullous disease.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly reduced or absent breath sounds on the left
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging appears dominated by a giant intrapulmonary bulla rather than a clear pleural line with a collapsed lung
No haemodynamic instability, hypotension, or tracheal deviation was reported

data.diagnosis: Smoking-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with bullous emphysema
data.description: Progressive airflow obstruction caused by smoking-related emphysematous destruction of alveoli, sometimes producing large bullae and markedly reduced lung function.
symptoms_in_common: Severe airflow obstruction with low FEV1 and reduced FEV1/FVC ratio
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute pleuritic chest pain is not typical of stable COPD
A silent unilateral hemithorax is more suggestive of a giant bulla or pneumothorax than diffuse COPD alone
No chronic productive cough or recurrent infective exacerbations were reported

data.description: An inherited cause of early-onset emphysema, often with lower-lobe-predominant panacinar emphysema and severe airflow obstruction, particularly in smokers.
symptoms_in_common: Emphysematous/bullous lung disease at a relatively young age
symptoms_not_in_common: Alpha-1 antitrypsin concentration was normal
The extensive smoking and cannabis exposure provides a more likely acquired cause
Giant predominantly unilateral bullae are less typical than diffuse lower-lobe-predominant emphysema
Acute pleuritic pain is not a usual presenting symptom unless complicated by pneumothorax

data.diagnosis: Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome with cystic lung disease and spontaneous pneumothorax
data.description: A hereditary disorder causing multiple pulmonary cysts and recurrent spontaneous pneumothoraces; it may also be associated with skin fibrofolliculomas and renal tumors.
symptoms_not_in_common: The marked smoking-related obstructive ventilatory defect is less typical
A single massive giant bulla is less characteristic than multiple bilateral lung cysts
No family history of pneumothorax, characteristic skin lesions, or renal tumors was reported
Long-term tobacco and cannabis exposure more strongly supports smoking-related giant bullous emphysema

data.description: 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presented with 3 months of progressive fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, and vague upper abdominal pain. He had a prior 40-pack-year smoking history. Examination and labs showed renal insufficiency (creatinine 3.2 mg/dL), severe anemia (hemoglobin 7 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (77,000/μL), hypercalcemia (12.7 mg/dL), elevated total protein (>10 g/dL), biochemical evidence of tumor lysis syndrome (LDH 1,157 U/L, uric acid 20.8 mg/dL), and coagulopathy with findings consistent with disseminated intravascular coagulation.
An aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma with a very high proliferation rate, often presenting as an abdominal mass and causing spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, and abdominal pain
Severe hyperuricemia and biochemical tumor lysis syndrome
Anemia and thrombocytopenia from marrow involvement
Histology compatible with a high-grade B-cell lymphoma with a starry-sky appearance
Disseminated intravascular coagulation can occur in advanced aggressive lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcemia is less typical than in plasma-cell disorders or some other lymphomas
Elevated total protein greater than 10 g/dL is not a classic feature

data.description: The most common aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults; it may involve abdominal lymph nodes, bone marrow, kidneys, and other extranodal organs and can produce high LDH and tumor lysis.
symptoms_in_common: Older adult with constitutional symptoms including fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
Vague upper abdominal pain and abdominal lymphadenopathy/mass
Anemia and thrombocytopenia suggesting marrow involvement
Spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome can occur with bulky, rapidly proliferating disease
Coagulopathy/DIC can occur in advanced disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Very marked hyperuricemia and spontaneous tumor lysis are more characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma
Hypercalcemia is not a dominant usual feature
Markedly elevated total protein is not typical

data.diagnosis: Plasma cell myeloma (multiple myeloma), possibly aggressive/anaplastic with extramedullary disease
data.description: A malignant plasma-cell disorder producing a monoclonal immunoglobulin, classically causing hypercalcemia, renal dysfunction, anemia, and increased serum protein; aggressive variants may form masses and rarely cause tumor lysis.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal or retroperitoneal mass could represent extramedullary plasmacytoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome with very high uric acid and LDH is unusual in typical multiple myeloma
Disseminated intravascular coagulation is uncommon
Prominent bulky abdominal lymphadenopathy is less typical than for lymphoma

data.diagnosis: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements (double-hit/triple-hit lymphoma)
data.description: A highly aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma, often occurring in older adults and presenting with bulky nodal or extranodal disease, marrow involvement, high LDH, and a substantial risk of spontaneous tumor lysis.
symptoms_in_common: Weight loss, fatigue, anorexia, and abdominal pain
Possible DIC in advanced rapidly progressive disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcemia is not a common defining feature

Definitive diagnosis requires cytogenetic demonstration of MYC with BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement

data.diagnosis: Lymphoblastic lymphoma/acute lymphoblastic leukemia of B-cell lineage
data.description: A precursor lymphoid malignancy that can involve bone marrow, lymph nodes, and abdominal organs; high tumor burden may cause cytopenias, elevated LDH, renal dysfunction, and tumor lysis syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia and thrombocytopenia from bone-marrow involvement
Abdominal lymphadenopathy or mass can occur
DIC may occur in severe advanced hematologic malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: This disease is more common in children and younger adults than in a 62-year-old patient
Hypercalcemia is uncommon
Marked hyperproteinemia is not typical
The described mature high-grade B-cell morphology would favor Burkitt lymphoma or another mature B-cell lymphoma instead

data.description: A 26-year-old woman presented with a one-year history of rash on her lower legs, abdomen, and arms, accompanied by a six-month history of paraesthesia in her right hand and left foot. She had no history of fatigue, weight loss, fever, or arthralgia. Neurological examination showed reduced sensation to light touch in the right ring and little fingers, the lateral palmar and dorsal hand, the left lateral calf, and the dorsum of the left foot. She experienced clumsiness in her right hand causing difficulty with writing, but no weakness was noted. Blood tests, including a full autoimmune screen, were normal. Electromyography demonstrated sensory damage in the right ulnar nerve and asymmetrical superficial sensory damage in the peroneal nerve, with greater involvement on the left side.

data.diagnosis: Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (cutaneous PAN) with mononeuritis multiplex
data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of small- to medium-sized muscular arteries in the skin, which can cause livedo-like rash, nodules or purpura and peripheral nerve ischemia. The biopsy appearance of inflamed, damaged vessel walls supports this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic mottled purpuric/livedoid rash on the legs, abdomen and arms
Asymmetric sensory neuropathy affecting multiple named nerves
Hand clumsiness from sensory nerve dysfunction
Normal autoimmune blood tests can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No painful skin nodules or ulceration were reported
No arthralgia was reported

data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that may involve skin, peripheral nerves, kidneys, gastrointestinal tract and other organs. Mononeuritis multiplex and livedo reticularis are characteristic features.
symptoms_in_common: Mononeuritis multiplex pattern with ulnar and peroneal nerve involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, weight loss or fatigue
No arthralgia
No reported hypertension, renal symptoms or abdominal pain
No reported motor weakness

symptoms_in_common: Ulnar and peroneal nerve involvement consistent with mononeuritis multiplex
Vasculitic inflammatory changes on biopsy can overlap
symptoms_not_in_common: Autoimmune screening was normal
No constitutional symptoms
No renal, pulmonary, sinus or upper-airway symptoms
No arthralgia
The biopsy appearance of medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis is more typical of polyarteritis nodosa

data.diagnosis: Leprosy (Hansen disease), multibacillary or borderline form
data.description: A chronic infection with Mycobacterium leprae that can cause skin lesions and peripheral nerve involvement, especially affecting cooler superficial nerves such as the ulnar and common peroneal nerves.

Reduced sensation in the peroneal nerve distribution of the lower leg and foot
Hand clumsiness related to nerve involvement

No weakness or muscle wasting was noted

data.description: 17-year-old male with high myopia and craniofacial/skeletal abnormalities. Full-term vaginal birth, birth weight 4.3 kg. Height tracked around the 80th percentile until age 15, then plateaued. At age 12, had dental crowding and a class III dentofacial growth pattern with retroclined lower teeth. At age 13, developed a grade 3/6 systolic heart murmur. Pectus excavatum was present at birth. Current exam shows loss of normal upper spinal curvature and scoliosis; measurements: weight 66.3 kg, height 177.5 cm, head circumference 58.5 cm. Laboratory testing showed marked hyperhomocysteinemia and elevated methionine.

data.diagnosis: Classical homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) deficiency
data.description: An autosomal-recessive disorder of methionine metabolism causing markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine. It produces a marfanoid skeletal phenotype, ectopia lentis, osteoporosis, and thromboembolic risk.
symptoms_in_common: High myopia with lens displacement/ectopia lentis
Scoliosis and loss of normal thoracic spinal curvature
Vertebral osteopenia or osteoporosis on imaging
Dental crowding and class III dentofacial pattern
Tall or relatively long-limbed habitus during childhood

Large birth weight is not a typical characteristic

data.description: An autosomal-dominant connective-tissue disorder, usually caused by FBN1 variants, characterized by skeletal overgrowth, chest wall deformity, scoliosis, lens dislocation, and aortic-root disease.

Elevated methionine

data.diagnosis: Homocystinuria due to methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) deficiency
data.description: An inherited remethylation disorder that elevates homocysteine because conversion of homocysteine to methionine is impaired; it commonly causes neurologic and thrombotic disease.

Elevated methionine

Severe osteoporosis with vertebral changes is not a usual primary feature

data.description: 29-year-old right-hand dominant male with hypothyroidism on thyroxine presented after 4 days of progressive dull left-sided neck pain radiating to the head, diplopia, right-sided numbness, dropping objects, and unsteady gait. He denied alcohol or illicit drug use, seizure, head injury, or loss of consciousness. Examination showed mild hypertension (141/94 mmHg), right-sided weakness mainly in the upper limb with pronator drift, decreased pinprick/light touch/proprioception on the right, resting and intention tremor with dysdiadochokinesia worse on the right, broad-based cerebellar ataxic gait, right upgoing plantar response, and diplopia on extremes of gaze without ocular palsy or papilloedema.

data.diagnosis: Pontine cavernous malformation with acute hemorrhage
data.description: A cavernous malformation is a cluster of fragile, abnormal small blood vessels that can bleed repeatedly. In the pons, an acute hemorrhage can cause crossed motor, sensory, cerebellar, and ocular symptoms and may obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow.

Right-sided loss of pinprick, light touch, and proprioception
Pontine hyperdense lesion on CT consistent with acute blood
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild hypertension

data.description: Bleeding within the pons, often related to hypertension or an underlying vascular lesion, produces acute or subacute brainstem dysfunction with weakness, sensory deficits, ataxia, and ocular movement symptoms.

Extensor plantar response on the right

data.diagnosis: Vertebral artery dissection with posterior-circulation ischemic stroke

Very rapid symptom evolution over only 4 days

data.diagnosis: Multiple sclerosis with a brainstem demyelinating lesion

Possible obstructive hydrocephalus
No described prior relapsing neurological episodes

data.description: 18-year-old male with 4 days of fatigue, subjective fever, chills, headache, non-bilious nonbloody vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, low back pain, dysuria, and pain in the lower abdomen, groin, and scrotum. Past history includes exercise-induced asthma and childhood hospitalization for diarrhea. He was born in Central America and moved to the US at age 15. On examination, he was tired-appearing with fever (39.4°C), tachycardia, tachypnea, and low back paraspinal muscle tenderness. Recent infectious testing was negative for tuberculosis, HIV, syphilis, gonorrhea, and chlamydia.

Systemic infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, often acquired by inhaling fungal spores. Disseminated disease can involve the reticuloendothelial system, bone marrow, gastrointestinal tract, lymph nodes, and occasionally the genitourinary tract. The marrow images are compatible with intracellular small yeasts within macrophages.
symptoms_in_common: Possible bone marrow involvement on pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: Dysuria
Scrotal pain
Groin pain
Very acute 4-day presentation

data.description: A systemic protozoal infection caused by Leishmania species and transmitted by sandflies. It may cause fever, constitutional symptoms, gastrointestinal complaints, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and macrophages containing intracellular amastigotes in bone marrow.
symptoms_in_common: Possible intracellular organisms in bone marrow macrophages
Birth in Central America, where Leishmania exposure is possible
symptoms_not_in_common: Dysuria
Scrotal pain
Groin pain
Focal lower abdominal or pelvic pain
Acute onset over only 4 days

data.description: Acute infection and inflammation of the prostate, usually due to enteric gram-negative bacteria such as Escherichia coli. It can cause fever, systemic illness, dysuria, pelvic or perineal pain, low back pain, and referred pain to the groin or scrotum.

data.diagnosis: Acute pyelonephritis or complicated urinary tract infection

Scrotal pain
Groin pain
Bone marrow findings of intracellular organisms

data.description: Systemic infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis that can involve lymph nodes, bone marrow, abdomen, spine, and genitourinary organs. Genitourinary tuberculosis may cause dysuria, pelvic pain, and scrotal involvement, although disseminated disease is usually more subacute or chronic.
symptoms_in_common: Origin from a region with higher tuberculosis prevalence
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative recent tuberculosis testing
Abrupt 4-day onset
Acute vomiting and diarrhea as dominant features
Bone marrow morphology more suggestive of intracellular yeast or protozoal organisms than acid-fast bacilli

data.description: This is a 56-year-old woman who underwent radical nephrectomy and lymph-node resection for clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma in February 2012. During subsequent follow-up, a single metastasis to the body of the left mandible was detected. She was referred in October 2012 for resection of the mandibular metastasis and fibular free-flap reconstruction. Two months later, bone scintigraphy revealed good vascularization of the flap, though additional bone metastases to the right humerus and pelvis were detected. In January 2014, the patient presented with visible bone exposure in the area of the graft with inflammation of surrounding tissues. Over days, there was an increase in bone exposure and necrosis without evidence of acute secondary infection.

data.diagnosis: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), likely bisphosphonate- or denosumab-associated
data.description: Progressive necrosis of jaw bone with persistent exposed bone, often occurring in patients receiving antiresorptive therapy for metastatic bone disease. It can affect reconstructed vascularized bone flaps as well as native jawbone.
symptoms_in_common: Visible exposed bone in the mandibular graft area
Progressive enlargement of bone exposure over days
History of metastatic cancer with additional skeletal metastases, a common indication for antiresorptive treatment
No evidence of acute secondary infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No specific medication history documenting bisphosphonate or denosumab use is provided
The affected bone is a fibular free-flap graft rather than only native mandible

data.diagnosis: Chronic osteomyelitis of the reconstructed mandible
data.description: Chronic infection and inflammation of bone that may cause bone destruction, sequestration, mucosal inflammation, and exposed necrotic bone, particularly after major mandibular surgery and reconstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammation of tissues surrounding the exposed graft
History of extensive mandibular surgery and reconstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No evidence of acute secondary infection
No reported fever, purulent drainage, severe pain, or systemic inflammatory symptoms
The rapid progression without clear infection is less typical for purely infectious osteomyelitis

data.diagnosis: Recurrent or progressive metastatic clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma involving the mandibular reconstruction
data.description: Clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma can metastasize to bone and may cause destructive osteolytic lesions in the mandible. Local tumor recurrence or tumor involvement of a graft can result in bony destruction and mucosal breakdown.
symptoms_in_common: Known history of clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma
Additional bone metastases in the humerus and pelvis
Progressive bone loss/necrosis in the reconstructed mandibular region
symptoms_not_in_common: Visible exposed devitalized bone is more characteristic of osteonecrosis than metastatic tumor alone
No reported soft-tissue mass, bleeding lesion, facial swelling, or radiographic evidence of a new focal tumor mass
No evidence of acute infection does not specifically support metastasis

data.description: Osteoradionecrosis is radiation-induced hypovascular, hypocellular bone injury that may lead to persistent exposed necrotic jawbone and chronic mucosal inflammation after head and neck radiotherapy.
symptoms_in_common: Lack of an acute infectious process
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of radiotherapy to the mandible or head and neck is provided
The lesion involves a vascularized fibular free flap, whereas osteoradionecrosis generally occurs in previously irradiated bone
The clinical history more strongly suggests medication-related or postoperative causes

data.diagnosis: Vascular compromise and delayed necrosis of the fibular free-flap reconstruction
data.description: Partial flap ischemia, venous congestion, or delayed failure of a vascularized bone graft can result in loss of flap viability, exposed bone, and necrosis. Late compromise may occur due to thrombosis, mechanical factors, wound breakdown, or impaired local healing.
symptoms_in_common: Necrosis and exposure of bone in the fibular graft region
Progressive breakdown of surrounding soft tissues
History of fibular free-flap mandibular reconstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Bone scintigraphy two months after reconstruction showed good flap vascularization
The presentation occurred more than one year after reconstruction, making immediate flap failure less typical
Inflammation and progressive exposed bone may be better explained by osteonecrosis or chronic local disease

data.description: 67-year-old man with 10 days of nausea, nonbloody vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain treated as reflux without relief, followed on the day of presentation by exertional substernal nonradiating chest heaviness progressing to rest pain with diaphoresis and dyspnea (8/10). Past history includes mild asthma, hemicolectomy for dysplastic polyps, and ventral abdominal hernia; remote 20 pack-year smoking history. On exam: tachycardia (125 bpm), hypotension (84/62 mmHg), tachypnea (22/min), oxygen saturation 94% on 6 L oxygen, pallor, diaphoresis, accessory muscle use, elevated JVP (18 cm H2O), holosystolic apical murmur, left basilar rales, palpable liver edge 4 cm below the costal margin, and cool, clammy extremities with thready pulses.

A rare, rapidly progressive autoimmune myocarditis characterized by myocardial inflammation, myocyte necrosis, and multinucleated giant cells on biopsy; it can cause fulminant heart failure, cardiogenic shock, arrhythmias, and chest-pain syndromes mimicking acute coronary syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Cool clammy extremities and thready pulses consistent with cardiogenic shock
Cardiac biopsy showing inflammatory myocardial injury with giant-cell-type features
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten days of prominent nausea, nonbloody vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain are not classic presenting features
No documented sustained ventricular tachyarrhythmia or high-grade heart block

data.description: A severe form of eosinophilic myocarditis in which eosinophil-rich inflammation causes myocardial necrosis and rapidly progressive heart failure or cardiogenic shock. It may occur with drug hypersensitivity, allergic disease, infection, or without an identifiable trigger.
symptoms_in_common: Signs of acute biventricular heart failure including elevated JVP, rales, and hepatomegaly
Cardiogenic shock with cool clammy extremities
History of mild asthma, which is an atopic condition
Myocardial biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrates and necrotic myocardial injury
symptoms_not_in_common: No rash, fever, or other systemic hypersensitivity manifestations are reported
No peripheral eosinophilia is reported
Prolonged nausea, vomiting, and abdominal bloating are not typical primary manifestations

data.description: Acute inflammation of the heart muscle, commonly following a viral illness, which can produce chest pain, ventricular dysfunction, acute heart failure, arrhythmias, and cardiogenic shock.
symptoms_in_common: Chest heaviness that can mimic myocardial infarction
Elevated JVP and hepatomegaly from heart failure
New mitral regurgitation-type murmur due to ventricular dysfunction
Cool extremities and hypoperfusion consistent with cardiogenic shock
Subacute gastrointestinal prodrome may occur with a viral illness
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, myalgias, sore throat, or other clear viral prodrome is described
