The biopsy appearance suggesting giant-cell or eosinophilic involvement would be less typical than predominantly lymphocytic myocarditis
Exertional chest heaviness progressing to rest pain is more classically ischemic

data.diagnosis: Acute anterior myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock and acute ischemic mitral regurgitation
data.description: Acute coronary occlusion can cause myocardial infarction, severe left-ventricular pump failure, pulmonary congestion, cardiogenic shock, and acute mitral regurgitation from papillary-muscle ischemia or ventricular remodeling.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional substernal chest heaviness progressing to pain at rest
Nausea and vomiting, which may be anginal equivalents
New holosystolic apical murmur compatible with mitral regurgitation
Cool clammy extremities and weak pulses consistent with cardiogenic shock
Remote smoking history as a coronary artery disease risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten days of bloating and persistent epigastric symptoms before the acute chest syndrome are less typical for a single acute infarction
Myocardial biopsy demonstrating prominent inflammatory or giant-cell/eosinophilic features would not be expected in uncomplicated infarction
Markedly elevated JVP and hepatomegaly may be disproportionate early in isolated left-sided infarction

data.diagnosis: Massive pulmonary embolism with obstructive shock
data.description: A large pulmonary arterial thromboembolism can abruptly increase right-sided cardiac pressure, causing dyspnea, tachycardia, elevated JVP, hypoxemia, hypotension, and obstructive shock.
symptoms_not_in_common: Chest discomfort is described as exertional substernal heaviness rather than sudden pleuritic pain
A new holosystolic apical murmur is not typical of pulmonary embolism
Left basilar rales are less typical than clear lungs in isolated pulmonary embolism
Ten days of nausea, vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain are not typical
Myocardial biopsy evidence of myocarditis would not be explained by pulmonary embolism

data.description: A 30-month-old boy presented with sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction with sevoflurane and nitric oxide before plastic surgery on June 7, 2004. The patient had never undergone ECG before the operation. Physical examination revealed distinctive facial features including a round face, small upper jaw and teeth, and nearly bald head. He had normal toes, with no history of seizure or syncope, and normal neurodevelopment. The patient was born via vaginal delivery without complications. Echocardiogram showed no intracardiac anomaly with normal ventricular function. Preoperative biochemical analysis and electrolyte levels were normal. Family history was notable for his older sister showing paradoxical QT interval prolongation on epinephrine stress test (QTc baseline 0.4 → peak 0.53 sec), though she was asymptomatic. The QT intervals of parents and sister were not significantly prolonged on ECG, and there was no family history of syncope, seizure, or sudden death.

data.diagnosis: Timothy syndrome (CACNA1C-related long QT syndrome type 8)
data.description: A rare multisystem genetic disorder caused by pathogenic CACNA1C variants, classically associated with marked QT prolongation, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, syndactyly, distinctive facial features, and variable developmental abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction
Long QT interval findings on ECG
Paradoxical QT prolongation with epinephrine stress in an affected sibling
Distinctive facial appearance with round face, small upper jaw, and small teeth
Hand syndactyly suggested by the clinical and radiographic images
Normal echocardiogram despite severe arrhythmic event
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal toes without toe syndactyly
Normal neurodevelopment
No prior syncope or seizures

data.diagnosis: Congenital long QT syndrome type 1 (KCNQ1-related LQTS)
data.description: An inherited cardiac ion-channel disorder causing delayed ventricular repolarization and risk of torsades de pointes, syncope, and sudden cardiac arrest, often triggered by adrenergic stress.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal QT response during epinephrine stress testing in a family member
symptoms_not_in_common: CACNA1C p.G406R variant rather than a KCNQ1 variant
Distinctive craniofacial features
Sparse hair/nearly bald head
Hand syndactyly
Cardiac arrest during anesthetic induction rather than a typical exercise or swimming trigger

data.diagnosis: CACNA1C-related isolated long QT syndrome (non-syndromic LQT8)
data.description: A CACNA1C-associated channelopathy that can produce QT prolongation and life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias without the full extracardiac manifestations of classic Timothy syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Normal cardiac structure and ventricular function
Possible familial inheritance with abnormal epinephrine QT response in the sister
symptoms_not_in_common: Hand syndactyly
Distinctive facial features
Small upper jaw and teeth
Sparse hair/nearly bald head

data.diagnosis: Andersen-Tawil syndrome (KCNJ2-related long QT syndrome type 7)
data.description: A genetic potassium-channel disorder characterized by ventricular arrhythmias, periodic paralysis, and characteristic craniofacial or skeletal abnormalities; QT-U prolongation may be present.
symptoms_in_common: Potential ventricular arrhythmia causing cardiac arrest
symptoms_not_in_common: CACNA1C p.G406R variant rather than a KCNJ2 variant
No periodic paralysis or episodic muscle weakness
No reported prominent ventricular ectopy or bidirectional ventricular tachycardia
Hand syndactyly is not typical
Sparse hair is not typical

data.description: An inherited arrhythmia syndrome, usually caused by RYR2 or CASQ2 variants, in which adrenergic stress can trigger bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia despite a structurally normal heart and often normal resting ECG.
symptoms_in_common: Family member with an abnormal response during epinephrine stress testing
symptoms_not_in_common: QT prolongation is not a defining feature of CPVT
CACNA1C p.G406R variant
Distinctive facial abnormalities
Hand syndactyly
Sparse hair/nearly bald head
No history of exertional or emotion-triggered syncope

data.description: 27-year-old man with a history of ulcerative colitis presented with 2 weeks of fatigue and several days of bloating and persistent nonbloody loose diarrhea after recent travel from Indonesia, including a rural area in India. He also reported decreased exercise tolerance and ~4.5 kg weight loss over recent weeks. He had no fever, chills, vomiting, cramping, or abdominal pain. Medications included mesalamine and acetaminophen. On examination, vital signs were normal, the spleen tip was palpable, and an erythematous papular rash was present on the anterior thorax. Laboratory testing showed marked leukocytosis with severe eosinophilia.

A soil-transmitted intestinal nematode infection acquired through skin contact with contaminated soil in tropical and subtropical regions. It can cause diarrhea, rash, marked eosinophilia, and chronic or intermittent gastrointestinal symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel to Indonesia and rural India
symptoms_not_in_common: Palpable splenic tip/splenomegaly is not a common isolated feature of uncomplicated strongyloidiasis
No abdominal pain or cramping, which are common gastrointestinal complaints in symptomatic infection

data.description: A disorder characterized by persistent marked eosinophilia that can infiltrate and damage multiple organs, including the gastrointestinal tract, skin, spleen, heart, lungs, and bone marrow. It may be idiopathic, clonal, or secondary to another condition.
symptoms_in_common: Diarrhea and bloating from possible gastrointestinal eosinophilic infiltration
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset after travel to endemic tropical areas suggests a parasitic cause more strongly
Persistent loose diarrhea as the dominant initial symptom is less typical than systemic or end-organ manifestations

data.description: An eosinophil-predominant inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract that may cause diarrhea, abdominal bloating, weight loss, and peripheral eosinophilia. It can occur independently or alongside other inflammatory bowel disorders.
symptoms_in_common: History of ulcerative colitis, which can complicate interpretation of gastrointestinal inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent travel to areas with risk for helminth infection is not typical of a primary eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorder
Palpable splenic tip/splenomegaly is not a usual feature
Erythematous papular rash is not a typical primary manifestation

data.description: A soil-transmitted helminth infection acquired by skin penetration of larvae in contaminated soil. It may produce a pruritic skin eruption, eosinophilia during larval migration, gastrointestinal symptoms, and chronic weight loss or anemia.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous papular rash compatible with larval skin exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain or cramping, which may occur with intestinal hookworm infection
Palpable splenic tip/splenomegaly is not typical
No reported iron-deficiency anemia or overt gastrointestinal blood loss

data.diagnosis: Acute schistosomiasis (Katayama syndrome) or intestinal schistosomiasis
data.description: A trematode infection acquired through freshwater exposure in endemic areas. Acute infection can cause eosinophilia, rash, systemic symptoms, and gastrointestinal complaints; chronic intestinal disease can cause diarrhea and colitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or chills, which are common in acute schistosomiasis
No abdominal pain or cramping
Nonbloody diarrhea is less typical of clinically significant intestinal schistosomiasis than diarrhea with blood or mucus

data.description: 28-year-old male who suddenly went into coma for 9 hours preceded by tonic-clonic seizures lasting 10 minutes. No fever, vomiting or micturition. No focal neurological signs. Past medical history was unremarkable. Neurological examination revealed normal cranial nerves, normal power and reflexes. Routine laboratory tests were normal.

An aggressive diffuse astrocytic glioma that can present as a necrotic, ring-enhancing cerebral mass with substantial surrounding edema and occasional intratumoral hemorrhage. The reported GFAP and OLIG2 positivity with IDH1 negativity, retained ATRX, p53 expression, and elevated proliferative activity favor a high-grade IDH-wildtype astrocytic tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged postictal coma or impaired consciousness
Frontal cerebral mass with ring enhancement
Young adult age can occur, although less commonly than in older adults
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt presentation without preceding headache, cognitive decline, or focal symptoms
Normal neurological examination without focal deficit
No vomiting or symptoms of raised intracranial pressure

data.diagnosis: High-grade astrocytoma (anaplastic astrocytoma or diffuse astrocytic glioma)
data.description: A malignant primary glial tumor arising from astrocytes. High-grade lesions may enhance, cause edema, provoke seizures, and sometimes bleed; definitive classification depends on histologic and molecular features.
symptoms_in_common: Transient coma or altered consciousness after prolonged seizure
symptoms_not_in_common: Very sudden presentation dominated by intracranial hemorrhage
No preceding progressive headache, personality change, or focal neurological deficit
No persistent neurological abnormalities on examination

data.description: A focal intracranial infection consisting of a pus-filled cavity surrounded by a capsule. On MRI it often appears as a ring-enhancing lesion with extensive edema and can cause seizures and reduced consciousness.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Normal routine laboratory tests
No reported infectious source, sinus disease, ear infection, cardiac infection, or immunosuppression
Hemorrhagic appearance is less typical
Tumor-marker pathology findings such as GFAP and OLIG2 positivity are not typical of an abscess

data.description: Metastatic cancer to the brain can form a sharply circumscribed enhancing mass with edema and intratumoral bleeding. Some metastases, especially melanoma, renal-cell carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, and lung carcinoma, bleed readily.
symptoms_in_common: Acute loss of consciousness related to hemorrhage and edema
symptoms_not_in_common: No known systemic malignancy
Young age makes common metastatic cancers less likely
Solitary lesion without reported additional brain lesions
Glial immunohistochemical profile with GFAP and OLIG2 positivity favors a primary glial tumor rather than metastasis

data.diagnosis: Cerebral arteriovenous malformation or cavernous malformation with hemorrhage
data.description: Vascular malformations may cause spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage and seizures in young adults. Cavernous malformations can have repeated small hemorrhages, whereas arteriovenous malformations may cause acute larger hemorrhage.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent ring-enhancing mass with extensive vasogenic edema is less typical of a simple vascular malformation
CTA/angiographic imaging does not show a clear vascular nidus or arteriovenous shunt
Histology and immunohistochemistry support a glial neoplasm rather than a vascular lesion
No recurrent prior seizures or prior hemorrhagic events reported

data.description: 82-year-old man with 6 months of worsening back and left hip pain, worse with activity and sometimes waking him from sleep, without leg radiation, morning stiffness, fever, chills, night sweats, or bowel/bladder incontinence. He reported 9 kg weight loss over the past few months. Pain began after resolution of pneumonia symptoms treated with levofloxacin. Past history includes sick sinus syndrome with pacemaker, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary fibrosis, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, gout, herpes zoster with postherpetic neuralgia, and basal-cell carcinoma. Exam showed no acute distress, no spinal or sacroiliac tenderness, normal hip exam, no neurologic deficits, mildly diminished patellar reflexes bilaterally, intact sensation, normal rectal tone, and negative straight-leg raise.

A fungal infection caused by Cryptococcus species that can disseminate from the lungs to bone, producing destructive vertebral lesions and paraspinal soft-tissue masses. Histology may show round encapsulated budding yeasts with a surrounding clear halo.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive back and left hip pain for 6 months
Pain occurring at night and waking him from sleep
Preceding pulmonary illness diagnosed as pneumonia
Destructive lumbar vertebral lesion with adjacent soft-tissue involvement on imaging
Absence of radicular leg pain or major neurologic deficits despite vertebral involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or chills
No headache, altered mental status, or meningismus suggesting cryptococcal meningitis
Pain is worse with activity, which can resemble mechanical back pain

data.description: Blastomycosis is a systemic fungal infection caused by Blastomyces species, usually acquired through inhalation. Pulmonary infection may disseminate to bone, causing lytic vertebral lesions and chronic painful osteomyelitis.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic progressive back and hip pain
Lytic/destructive vertebral abnormality with soft-tissue extension
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, or night sweats
No current respiratory symptoms
No reported skin lesions, which are common in disseminated blastomycosis
No neurologic deficits

data.description: Disseminated coccidioidomycosis is infection with Coccidioides fungi that begins in the lungs and can later involve bone, including the spine. Vertebral disease may cause lytic lesions, pain, and paraspinal inflammatory masses.
symptoms_in_common: Respiratory illness preceding the onset of skeletal symptoms
Pain that sometimes wakes him from sleep
Destructive vertebral lesion with possible paraspinal soft-tissue involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, night sweats, or chills
No cough or persistent pulmonary complaints
No rash, erythema nodosum, or arthralgia reported
No neurologic deficits or bowel/bladder dysfunction

data.description: Tuberculosis of the spine is a chronic granulomatous infection of vertebral bodies that can cause vertebral destruction, disc-space involvement, paraspinal abscesses, pain, constitutional symptoms, and possible neurologic compromise.
symptoms_in_common: Vertebral destruction and adjacent paraspinal soft-tissue abnormality
History of a preceding pulmonary illness
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, or night sweats
No spinal tenderness on examination
No neurologic deficits, bowel/bladder dysfunction, or leg radiation
No reported persistent cough or other active pulmonary tuberculosis symptoms

data.diagnosis: Metastatic malignancy involving the lumbar spine
data.description: Cancer metastatic to the spine, such as lung, prostate, renal, thyroid, or hematologic malignancy, may produce destructive vertebral lesions, persistent night pain, weight loss, and eventual neurologic compression.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive persistent back and hip pain
Destructive vertebral lesion with an associated soft-tissue mass
History of prior basal-cell carcinoma and pulmonary disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No known active internal malignancy
No neurologic deficits, bowel/bladder incontinence, or spinal cord compression symptoms
No focal spinal tenderness
Pain began after a pneumonia-like illness, which may favor an infectious cause

data.description: A 47-year-old woman presented with intermittent cough, shortness of breath, fever (body temperature up to 38.5°C), accompanied by right eyelid swelling around June 17, 2017, which worsened day by day. Weight loss was about 9 kg. Physical examination included high body temperature of 39°C, right eyelid swelling, and a painless enlarged lymph node about 2 cm × 2 cm in size in the left axilla. Auscultation of lungs revealed coarse respiratory sounds with moist rale. No hepatosplenomegaly and edema in lower limbs.

A systemic dimorphic fungal infection that can involve the lungs, lymph nodes, skin, subcutaneous tissue, bone marrow, and other organs; it is especially associated with immunosuppression but can occur in apparently immunocompetent individuals.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral pulmonary nodular/infiltrative abnormalities on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly
No lower-limb edema

data.description: A systemic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma species, usually acquired by inhalation; disseminated disease can produce fever, weight loss, pulmonary infiltrates, lymphadenopathy, and skin or soft-tissue lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse bilateral lung nodules or infiltrates
Possible eyelid or periorbital soft-tissue involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Isolated prominent right eyelid swelling is less typical
No hepatosplenomegaly
No reported mucosal ulcers or generalized skin lesions

data.description: An invasive infection caused by Cryptococcus species that can involve the lungs and spread to lymph nodes, skin, bone, eyes, or the central nervous system, particularly in immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_in_common: Eyelid or orbital soft-tissue swelling can occur with cutaneous or disseminated disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache, neck stiffness, altered mental status, or other meningitis symptoms
No reported umbilicated papules or other classic cryptococcal skin lesions
Prominent axillary lymphadenopathy is less typical

data.description: A systemic fungal disease caused by Blastomyces species, producing pulmonary infection with possible spread to skin, soft tissue, bone, genitourinary sites, and occasionally the orbit.
symptoms_not_in_common: Painless axillary lymph node enlargement is less characteristic
No verrucous or ulcerative skin lesions described
No bone or joint symptoms reported

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection may cause chronic pulmonary disease and constitutional symptoms, with extrapulmonary involvement of lymph nodes, soft tissue, and rarely the orbit or eyelid.
symptoms_in_common: Possible extrapulmonary soft-tissue or eyelid involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapidly progressive eyelid swelling over days is less typical
Moist rales are not a classic tuberculosis finding
No night sweats, hemoptysis, or chronic sputum production reported

data.description: A 19-year-old previously healthy gravida 3 para 2002 female presented at 28 weeks' gestation after emigrating to the U.S. at 25 weeks of gestation. During the 20th week of gestation, she experienced a maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache. She and her spouse had unprotected intercourse through the first and second trimester. The patient's initial fetal ultrasound with neurosonography revealed cerebral ventriculomegaly (20-25 mm) with dangling choroid, prominent 3rd ventricle, and a widened cavum septum pellucidum. Amniocentesis showed negative NAT for ZIKV with no evidence of chromosomal variations by CMA; TORCH panel was negative.

Fetal infection with Zika virus acquired during pregnancy, which can cause severe brain abnormalities including ventriculomegaly, cortical malformations, intracranial calcifications, and microcephaly. Maternal infection often causes a mild febrile rash illness with conjunctivitis.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in or emigration from a Zika-endemic area
Unprotected sexual intercourse during pregnancy, allowing possible sexual transmission
Abnormal cavum septum pellucidum and prominent third ventricle suggesting fetal CNS involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of fetal microcephaly
Negative Zika virus nucleic acid test in amniotic fluid

data.description: CMV is a common congenital viral infection that can cause fetal ventriculomegaly, periventricular calcifications, abnormal brain development, growth restriction, hearing loss, and neurodevelopmental impairment.
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash and conjunctivitis are less typical of CMV infection
No reported fetal growth restriction
No reported intracranial calcifications
Negative TORCH panel

data.description: Congenital infection with Toxoplasma gondii can produce hydrocephalus or ventriculomegaly, diffuse intracranial calcifications, chorioretinitis, and neurologic impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal fever and headache can occur with acute maternal infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal conjunctivitis is not typical
Maculopapular rash is not typical
No reported intracranial calcifications
No reported chorioretinitis or ocular abnormalities
Negative TORCH panel

data.diagnosis: Fetal aqueductal stenosis causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: Obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid flow at the cerebral aqueduct causes enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles, often with relative sparing of the fourth ventricle. It may be isolated or associated with genetic or structural CNS disorders.
symptoms_in_common: Dangling choroid plexus, consistent with significant ventriculomegaly
No chromosomal abnormality detected by chromosomal microarray
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal rash, fever, conjunctivitis, and headache are not explained by aqueductal stenosis
Epidemiologic risk for Zika exposure is not related to aqueductal stenosis
Abnormal or widened cavum septum pellucidum may suggest a more diffuse brain developmental abnormality rather than isolated obstruction

data.diagnosis: Genetic fetal brain malformation, such as L1 syndrome or a tubulinopathy
data.description: Genetic neurodevelopmental disorders affecting neuronal migration, axon formation, or cerebrospinal fluid pathways can cause severe ventriculomegaly, hydrocephalus, abnormal commissural structures, and cortical malformations. L1 syndrome is a classic cause of X-linked hydrocephalus, while tubulinopathies can cause complex cortical and ventricular abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Normal chromosomal microarray does not exclude single-gene disorders
Negative TORCH testing supports consideration of a noninfectious etiology
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal rash, fever, headache, and conjunctivitis are not features of fetal genetic brain malformations
Exposure in a Zika-endemic setting and possible sexual transmission do not support a purely genetic cause
No reported family history of hydrocephalus or neurodevelopmental disorder

data.description: 26-year-old Chinese female with a 2-year history of progressive lower-limb weakness and scissor gait beginning at age 24, followed by dysphagia and severe cognitive impairment (MMSE 16/30). Exam showed severe lower-extremity spasticity, mild upper-extremity spasticity, and left patellar clonus. Birth history and developmental milestones were normal. Initially classified as sporadic HSP; later genetic testing showed compound heterozygous mutations consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

data.diagnosis: SPG11-related hereditary spastic paraplegia (Spastic paraplegia type 11, Kjellin syndrome spectrum)
data.description: An autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by biallelic SPG11 mutations. It commonly causes progressive spastic paraparesis, cognitive decline, dysphagia, peripheral neurologic features, and thinning of the corpus callosum on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive lower-limb weakness beginning in young adulthood
MRI appearance consistent with thinning of the corpus callosum and white-matter abnormalities
Compound heterozygous mutations with autosomal recessive inheritance
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal birth history and normal early developmental milestones are possible but do not specifically support the disorder

data.diagnosis: SPG15-related hereditary spastic paraplegia (ZFYVE26-associated spastic paraplegia)
data.description: A complicated autosomal recessive hereditary spastic paraplegia that closely resembles SPG11. It can cause progressive spastic paraparesis, intellectual or cognitive decline, dysphagia, and a thin corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive spastic weakness of the lower limbs
symptoms_not_in_common: The reported compound heterozygous mutations are in SPG11 rather than ZFYVE26
No retinal degeneration or macular abnormalities were reported, which can occur in some SPG15 cases

data.diagnosis: FA2H-associated neurodegeneration / SPG35 (fatty acid hydroxylase-associated neurodegeneration)
data.description: An autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by FA2H mutations. It may present with complicated spastic paraplegia, cognitive decline, dysphagia, white-matter disease, and sometimes brain iron accumulation.
symptoms_in_common: Upper motor neuron signs including clonus
symptoms_not_in_common: No brain iron accumulation in the globus pallidus or substantia nigra was described
No dystonia, parkinsonism, seizures, optic atrophy, or peripheral neuropathy was reported
The identified genetic finding is consistent with SPG11 rather than FA2H

data.description: A hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by KIF1A variants, with either dominant or recessive inheritance. Complicated forms can include cognitive impairment, optic neuropathy, peripheral neuropathy, and progressive spastic gait.
symptoms_in_common: Possible early-adult onset in some affected individuals
symptoms_not_in_common: Thin corpus callosum is less characteristic than in SPG11
No optic atrophy, visual impairment, sensory neuropathy, or cerebellar ataxia was reported
The genetic result indicates biallelic SPG11 mutations rather than KIF1A variants

data.description: A peroxisomal disorder caused by ABCD1 mutations. Adult forms can produce progressive spastic paraparesis, gait impairment, bladder dysfunction, neuropathy, and, in cerebral disease, cognitive decline and white-matter lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive spastic weakness of the lower limbs
Upper motor neuron signs including clonus
Cognitive impairment can occur in cerebral involvement
White-matter abnormalities may be seen on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: The patient is female; severe early cerebral presentations are much more typical in males
No adrenal insufficiency, hyperpigmentation, bladder dysfunction, sensory neuropathy, or sexual dysfunction was reported
Corpus callosum thinning with the described phenotype is more characteristic of SPG11
The genetic findings indicate autosomal recessive SPG11-related disease rather than ABCD1-related disease

diagnoses.name: Complex hereditary spastic paraplegia
diagnoses.title: Autosomal recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia

data.description: A 25-year-old female in her third trimester of pregnancy presented with paroxysmal headache, palpitations, sweating, and hypertension up to 230/130 for three weeks. Her medical history was negative for previous hypertension, and physical examination was unremarkable. Initial work-up excluded pre-eclampsia. Her urine catecholamines were markedly elevated: Dopamine 607 μg/24 hours (range 65-400), Norepinephrine 978 μg/24 hours (range 15-80), Metanephrine 108 μg/24 hours (range 24-96), Normetanephrine 4067 μg/24 hours (range 75-375), and Vanillyl mandelic acid 13.6 mg/24 hours (range 2-7). Epinephrine level was normal at 0.8 μg/24 hours (range 0.0-20.0). Initial abdominal MRI showed a 28×19 mm left juxta-adrenal mass that was later found to be brown fat.

A rare extra-adrenal neuroendocrine tumor arising from sympathetic paraganglia in the mediastinum, often near the heart or great vessels. It can secrete norepinephrine and cause episodic catecholamine crises; the imaging appearance is consistent with a hypervascular mediastinal mass.
symptoms_in_common: Normal epinephrine level, which is compatible with an extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma
symptoms_not_in_common: Left juxta-adrenal mass on initial abdominal MRI, later identified as brown fat

data.description: A catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor arising from adrenal medullary chromaffin cells. It classically causes episodic headache, diaphoresis, palpitations, and severe hypertension, including during pregnancy.
symptoms_not_in_common: No confirmed adrenal mass
The presumed juxta-adrenal lesion was brown fat rather than a tumor
Normal epinephrine level is less typical for many adrenal pheochromocytomas
Imaging localizes a mass in the mediastinal/cardiac region rather than the adrenal gland

data.description: A pregnancy-specific hypertensive disorder occurring after 20 weeks of gestation, typically associated with proteinuria or maternal end-organ dysfunction. Severe hypertension and headache are common warning features.
symptoms_in_common: Sweating and palpitations may occur nonspecifically during severe hypertensive episodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Paroxysmal episodic pattern of symptoms
Marked elevation of urinary norepinephrine and normetanephrine
Elevated urinary vanillylmandelic acid
Hypermetabolic mediastinal/cardiac-region mass
Preeclampsia was excluded during the initial evaluation

data.diagnosis: Neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma with catecholamine secretion
data.description: Neuroblastic tumors derived from sympathetic neural crest tissue that can produce catecholamine metabolites, especially vanillylmandelic acid and homovanillic acid. They are predominantly pediatric tumors but rarely occur in adults.
symptoms_in_common: Hypertension can occur with catecholamine secretion
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 25 years, whereas neuroblastoma is primarily a childhood malignancy
Classic paroxysmal triad of headache, palpitations, and sweating is more characteristic of pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma
Marked normetanephrine elevation is more typical of a functional paraganglioma
No reported systemic malignancy features such as weight loss, bone pain, or metastatic disease

data.description: A usually benign tumor of sympathetic ganglia that may arise in the posterior mediastinum or retroperitoneum. Most are nonfunctional, but a minority secrete catecholamines and can cause hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated norepinephrine and dopamine can occur in functional cases
symptoms_not_in_common: Very marked normetanephrine elevation is more typical of paraganglioma
Severe paroxysmal hypertension up to 230/130 is less common
Strongly hypermetabolic imaging appearance is less typical of a benign ganglioneuroma
Ganglioneuromas are often asymptomatic and discovered incidentally

data.description: A 71-year-old woman presented with a 3-day history of headache and fatigue, followed by sudden onset of confusion and language production difficulties while typing at work. The confusion resolved briefly but recurred later that evening. She had a history of myasthenia gravis (diagnosed 18 years prior, treated with mycophenolate mofetil for 7 years), vitamin B12 deficiency, and hypertension. Past surgical history included supracervical hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (31 years prior), transsternal thymectomy and wedge resection of right upper lobe for cortical thymoma (22 years prior), and sigmoid colectomy for recurrent diverticulitis (7 years prior). On examination at the current hospital, she had severe expressive aphasia, followed commands intermittently, disconjugate gaze at rest, motor strength 5/5 in left extremities and 4/5 in right extremities. Blood phosphorus was 2.2 mg/dL (reference range 2.6-4.5); other routine labs were normal.

An opportunistic infection caused by Nocardia species that can produce a focal, often ring-enhancing brain abscess, particularly in patients receiving chronic immunosuppressive therapy. Histology may show suppurative inflammation with branching filamentous bacteria.
symptoms_in_common: Focal enhancing cerebral lesion with surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No pulmonary symptoms reported
Disconjugate gaze is not a typical primary feature

data.description: Reactivation of Toxoplasma infection in immunocompromised patients, causing focal necrotizing brain lesions, commonly with ring enhancement and edema.
symptoms_in_common: Focal contrast-enhancing brain lesion with edema
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No seizures reported
A solitary superficial frontal lesion is less typical than multiple basal-ganglia or corticomedullary lesions

data.description: A lymphoma confined to the brain, spinal cord, meninges, or eyes. It is more common in older adults and in immunosuppressed patients and can cause focal neurologic deficits and enhancing brain masses.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing cerebral mass with surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset and fluctuation of symptoms are less typical
Only a 3-day prodrome is less typical for lymphoma
Suppurative inflammatory histology would not be typical

data.description: A localized collection of pus in the brain caused by bacterial infection, often producing a ring-enhancing lesion with vasogenic edema and focal neurologic deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing focal brain lesion with edema
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
Routine laboratory studies were otherwise normal
No identified contiguous ear, sinus, dental, cardiac, or traumatic source

data.description: An invasive fungal infection caused by Aspergillus species that can involve the central nervous system in immunocompromised patients, producing infarcts, hemorrhagic lesions, or abscess-like enhancing masses.
symptoms_in_common: Mass-like enhancing brain lesion with edema
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No respiratory or sinus symptoms reported
No reported neutropenia or other major routine laboratory abnormality

data.description: 36-year-old obese woman with a 5-year history of type 2 diabetes, positive Mantoux test, smoking one pack per day, and social alcohol use, presented with 5 days of fever, chills, productive cough with yellow sputum, and sharp right lower chest pain worsened by deep breathing, starting about a week after a stay at a lakeside cottage. On return 5 days later, she was febrile (39°C) with mild tachycardia; blood pressure, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation were normal. Exam showed decreased air entry and bronchial breath sounds in the right lower chest.
A severe atypical bacterial pneumonia caused by Legionella species, often acquired from aerosolized freshwater sources and capable of progressing from focal to bilateral patchy consolidation.
symptoms_in_common: Recent stay near a freshwater lake
Right lower-lobe infiltrate progressing to bilateral lower-lung infiltrates on imaging
Diabetes and smoking as risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: Yellow sputum is less characteristic than a dry or minimally productive cough
No reported diarrhea, nausea, confusion, headache, or hyponatremia

data.description: An acute bacterial pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, commonly producing abrupt fever, productive sputum, pleuritic pain, and lobar or segmental air-space consolidation.
symptoms_in_common: Sharp pleuritic chest pain worsened by deep breathing
Bronchial breath sounds and reduced air entry at the right base
Right lower-lobe consolidation on chest radiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent lakeside freshwater exposure is not specifically associated with pneumococcal infection
Rapid progression to multifocal bilateral lower-lobe infiltrates is less typical than a single lobar consolidation

data.description: Pulmonary infection or inflammation caused by inhalation of oropharyngeal or gastric contents, often affecting dependent lower-lobe lung segments and sometimes causing polymicrobial infection.
symptoms_in_common: Bibasal and dependent distribution of infiltrates on imaging
Social alcohol use may increase aspiration risk
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported vomiting, impaired consciousness, dysphagia, seizure, or witnessed aspiration event
Abrupt chills after freshwater exposure is not characteristic
Young age and only social alcohol use make aspiration less likely

data.description: A chronic pulmonary infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that can cause cough, fever, and radiographic infiltrates or cavitation; diabetes is a risk factor for active disease.
symptoms_in_common: Diabetes as a risk factor for active tuberculosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute 5-day presentation is atypical
Chills and abrupt high fever are less typical
Pleuritic lower-chest pain is less typical
No chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats, hemoptysis, or upper-lobe cavitary disease reported
Predominantly lower-lobe acute consolidation is less typical

data.description: A common atypical community-acquired pneumonia that usually causes a gradual respiratory illness with fever, cough, and diffuse or patchy interstitial-to-air-space infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: Patchy bilateral pulmonary infiltrates later in the course
symptoms_not_in_common: Productive yellow sputum is less typical because cough is often dry
Marked chills and high fever are less typical
Focal bronchial breath sounds and dense right lower-lobe consolidation favor typical bacterial pneumonia
Pleuritic chest pain is less common
Freshwater exposure does not specifically support Mycoplasma infection

data.description: 19-year-old female with neonatal hypotonia and weak breathing/crying at birth. In the first month of life she developed respiratory failure requiring tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation. She had a patent ductus arteriosus repaired at age 2, recurrent respiratory infections, and scoliosis surgery at age 12. At age 4, nerve stimulation showed a 36% decrement in compound muscle action potential area with no repetitive CMAPs; AChR and MuSK antibodies were negative. Recent examination showed normal cognition, bilateral ptosis, mild limitation of upward gaze, and facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness with intact deep tendon reflexes.

data.diagnosis: CHRNE-related congenital myasthenic syndrome (primary acetylcholine receptor deficiency)
data.description: A postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by reduced function or number of acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, often presenting from birth with severe generalized weakness and respiratory involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Weak cry and weak breathing at birth
Early respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
Significant decrement on repetitive nerve stimulation
Mild ophthalmoparesis with limited upward gaze
Facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not a typical feature
Scoliosis can occur secondarily to chronic weakness but is not a defining feature

data.description: A postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by rapsyn deficiency, impairing clustering of acetylcholine receptors at the motor endplate. It commonly causes neonatal or infantile weakness, ptosis, bulbar dysfunction, and respiratory crises.
symptoms_in_common: Weak respiratory effort and weak cry at birth
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not typically associated
Persistent need for long-term mechanical ventilation is possible but more severe than many RAPSN-related cases
Scoliosis is not a primary characteristic

data.description: A congenital disorder of neuromuscular-junction development caused by biallelic MUSK variants. It can produce severe neonatal respiratory and bulbar weakness, facial weakness, ptosis, and impaired eye movements despite negative MuSK antibodies.
symptoms_in_common: Early respiratory failure requiring tracheostomy and ventilation
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not a usual manifestation
Scoliosis is not a specific hallmark, although it may develop because of chronic muscle weakness

data.description: A postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by impaired agrin-MuSK signaling and abnormal neuromuscular-junction formation. It often produces limb-girdle, neck, and respiratory weakness with normal sensation and reflexes; ocular symptoms may be mild or absent.
symptoms_in_common: Scoliosis associated with chronic axial weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe neonatal respiratory failure from the first month of life is less typical than in some other congenital myasthenic syndromes
Prominent bilateral ptosis and ophthalmoparesis are less typical
Patent ductus arteriosus is not characteristic

data.description: A synaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by deficiency of acetylcholinesterase anchored at the motor endplate, resulting in prolonged acetylcholine action, fatigable weakness, respiratory involvement, and progressive skeletal deformity.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital or early-infantile onset of weakness
Respiratory failure and recurrent respiratory infections
Facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of repetitive compound muscle action potentials is not typical, because repetitive CMAPs are a classic electrophysiologic feature of acetylcholinesterase deficiency
Patent ductus arteriosus is not a characteristic feature

data.description: A 52-year-old man was brought to the emergency department with acute onset shortness of breath and confusion. On physical examination, he was agitated and taking deep breaths at a rate of 28/min. Initial venous blood gas on ambient air showed pH 7.02, partial pressure of carbon dioxide 3.4 kPa, and partial pressure of oxygen 4.1 kPa. Laboratory studies revealed blood glucose 7.1 mmol/L (reference range 4.4-6.1), lactic acid 6.6 mmol/L (0.5-2.2), serum anion gap 19 mmol/L (8-16), serum osmolality 318 mmol/kg (275-295), serum osmolal gap 20 mmol/kg (<10), and acute kidney injury with creatinine 141 μmol/L (70-120). Blood ethanol was undetectable and urine drug screen was negative. Urinalysis showed haematuria and no ketones.
Toxic alcohol ingestion causing high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, elevated osmolal gap, calcium oxalate crystal deposition, acute kidney injury, and neurologic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Deep rapid breathing consistent with respiratory compensation for severe metabolic acidosis
Urine sediment suggestive of calcium oxalate crystals
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported history of antifreeze or other toxic alcohol ingestion
Shortness of breath is not usually the primary presenting complaint, although compensatory hyperventilation is common

data.description: Toxic methanol ingestion produces an elevated osmolal gap initially and later severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis due to formic acid accumulation; it can cause central nervous system toxicity and visual impairment.
symptoms_not_in_common: Haematuria is not typical
Acute kidney injury is less prominent than in ethylene glycol poisoning
Urinary calcium oxalate-type crystals are not expected
No visual symptoms such as blurred vision, photophobia, or vision loss are reported

data.description: Diabetic ketoacidosis is a metabolic emergency caused by insulin deficiency, resulting in hyperglycemia, ketone production, dehydration, and high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Deep rapid breathing compatible with Kussmaul respirations
Acute kidney injury can occur from dehydration
symptoms_not_in_common: Blood glucose is only mildly elevated at 7.1 mmol/L
Urinalysis shows no ketones
Elevated osmolal gap is not typical
Haematuria and calcium oxalate-type urinary crystals are not typical

data.description: Salicylate toxicity causes respiratory stimulation, metabolic acidosis, neurologic symptoms, and often a mixed respiratory alkalosis with high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Acute kidney injury may occur in severe toxicity
symptoms_not_in_common: The osmolal gap is not typically elevated
The low carbon dioxide level could occur, but a primary respiratory alkalosis is not clearly demonstrated
Haematuria and urinary calcium oxalate-type crystals are not typical
No tinnitus, nausea, vomiting, fever, or diaphoresis is reported

data.description: Propylene glycol toxicity, often associated with large intravenous exposures to medications containing this solvent, can cause elevated osmolal gap, lactic acidosis, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, central nervous system depression, and kidney dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Deep rapid breathing due to acidemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Haematuria is not a characteristic feature
Urinary calcium oxalate-type crystals are not expected
No history of prolonged intravenous sedative or medication exposure is provided
Propylene glycol more often causes sedation or depressed consciousness than marked agitation

data.description: 36-year-old man with 18 days of fevers to 39.5°C, preceded by throat swelling sensation. Three days after onset he developed fever, and despite amoxicillin-clavulanic acid for presumed streptococcal pharyngitis, fevers persisted with headaches and fatigue. He also reported lower neck swelling and discomfort with neck movement, without dysphagia, odynophagia, rhinorrhea, or rash. Past history: seasonal allergies. Recent travel to the southwestern United States with his wife 2 weeks before onset; wife had self-limited fever and sore throat. On exam, he was afebrile but tachycardic, with normal oropharynx, no lymphadenopathy, and firm, nontender palpable thyroid tissue in the anterior neck.
A self-limited inflammatory thyroid disorder, usually triggered by a viral upper respiratory infection, causing thyroid enlargement, neck discomfort, fever, and transient release of thyroid hormone.
symptoms_in_common: Possible exposure to a viral illness through his wife
symptoms_not_in_common: Lack of clear thyroid tenderness on examination
No reported palpitations, tremor, weight loss, or heat intolerance despite tachycardia
Very high fever persisting for 18 days is somewhat more severe than usual

data.description: A rare bacterial infection of the thyroid gland that can produce fever, thyroid swelling, neck pain, and sometimes thyroid abscess formation.
symptoms_in_common: Failure to improve with initial outpatient antibiotic treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Thyroid tissue was firm and nontender rather than markedly painful or tender
No dysphagia or odynophagia
Normal oropharyngeal examination
No cervical lymphadenopathy
No described abscess, fluctuance, or overlying skin erythema

data.diagnosis: Viral thyroiditis associated with acute viral infection
data.description: Inflammation of the thyroid occurring during or shortly after a viral syndrome; it may overlap clinically with subacute granulomatous thyroiditis and can cause fever and diffuse thyroid enlargement.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel with exposure to an ill household contact
Wife had a self-limited fever and sore throat
No convincing bacterial pharyngitis on examination
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent fever for 18 days is longer than many uncomplicated viral syndromes
No rhinorrhea, cough, rash, or other typical viral upper-respiratory symptoms
Firm thyroid enlargement is more specific for thyroid inflammation than for a nonspecific viral illness

data.description: An autoimmune disorder in which thyroid-stimulating antibodies cause diffuse thyroid enlargement and excess thyroid hormone production, often resulting in tachycardia and heat intolerance.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute onset after a throat illness
High persistent fevers to 39.5°C
Neck swelling and discomfort with movement
No tremor, weight loss, sweating, heat intolerance, diarrhea, or anxiety reported
No ophthalmopathy or pretibial skin findings reported

data.diagnosis: Thyroid lymphoma or other infiltrative thyroid malignancy
data.description: An infiltrative tumor of the thyroid can cause firm thyroid enlargement and compressive neck symptoms; lymphoma may occasionally produce systemic fever.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent fever can occur as a constitutional symptom
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset over only 18 days following an apparent infectious illness
Young age for typical thyroid lymphoma
No progressive dysphagia, odynophagia, hoarseness, or dyspnea
No lymphadenopathy
High fever and headache are more suggestive of inflammatory or infectious thyroid disease

data.description: 42-year-old man with coronary artery disease and dyslipidemia presented with 2 days of sudden left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back in a bandlike pattern, worsened by movement, associated with nausea and early satiety. He also had substernal chest pressure similar to his usual angina but unrelieved by one sublingual nitroglycerin tablet. He denied trauma, vomiting, or GI bleeding. History notable for chronic diarrhea since coronary bypass surgery, worsening after a cholesterol medication dose increase 6 months earlier, 16 kg unintentional weight loss over 6 months, intermittent early satiety, daily headaches, nocturia, and a warm feeling at night without fever or night sweats. Exam showed mild left upper quadrant tenderness without peritoneal signs. Vitals were stable. Labs showed mild elevation of amylase, lipase, AST, and ALT; CBC, electrolytes, renal function, bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and triglycerides were normal. ECG and chest radiograph were normal.

An immune-mediated small-intestinal disorder triggered by gluten that causes malabsorption, chronic diarrhea, weight loss, and characteristic duodenal mucosal inflammation with increased intraepithelial lymphocytes and villous injury.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings compatible with small-bowel/mesenteric inflammatory changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden severe left upper quadrant pain radiating to the back
Mild amylase and lipase elevation
Substernal chest pressure resembling angina
Nocturia
Daily headaches

data.diagnosis: Drug-induced enteropathy or microscopic colitis related to lipid-lowering therapy
data.description: Medication-related intestinal injury can cause chronic watery diarrhea, weight loss, abdominal discomfort, and biopsy findings of lymphocytic inflammation or epithelial injury. Symptoms may worsen after an increased medication dose.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic diarrhea that worsened after a cholesterol medication dose increase
Possible lymphocytic inflammatory changes on intestinal biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute bandlike pain radiating to the back
Mild pancreatic enzyme elevation
Substernal chest pressure unrelieved by nitroglycerin
Warm sensation at night
Nocturia

data.description: A chronic systemic infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei, usually involving the small bowel and producing diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, malabsorption, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy. It can also cause neurologic, cardiac, and joint manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Mesenteric lymph node or small-bowel abnormalities on CT
Daily headaches, which could represent a neurologic manifestation
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No arthralgias or migratory joint symptoms
Sudden acute left upper quadrant pain radiating to the back
Chest pressure similar to established angina
Normal CBC

data.diagnosis: Chronic mesenteric ischemia with acute exacerbation
data.description: Reduced intestinal blood flow from atherosclerotic mesenteric arterial disease can cause abdominal pain, food avoidance, diarrhea, early satiety, and weight loss. Acute worsening may cause severe abdominal pain and mild laboratory abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Known coronary artery disease and dyslipidemia, indicating significant atherosclerotic risk
Mild elevation of AST and ALT
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain was not clearly described as postprandial
No food fear was reported
No metabolic acidosis or elevated lactate was reported
No GI bleeding
Histologic mucosal lymphocytic changes would not be the classic primary finding

data.description: Inflammation of the pancreas typically causes acute upper abdominal pain radiating to the back with nausea and elevated amylase and lipase. Some medications can precipitate pancreatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back in a bandlike pattern
Possible temporal association with medication exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Only mild pancreatic enzyme elevation
Chronic diarrhea for years is not explained by isolated acute pancreatitis
Marked 16 kg weight loss over 6 months is not typical of a single acute episode
No vomiting
CT findings appear centered on small bowel or mesenteric structures rather than classic pancreatic inflammation

data.description: A 59-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with a 9-day history of stiffness, swelling, and severe pain beginning in the metacarpophalangeal joint of the right thumb, followed by bilateral ankle involvement 3 days later. She had a history of stroke, glaucoma, and total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy 7 years prior. The patient lived in New England, worked in health care, and reported unprotected vaginal intercourse 2 weeks before presentation. Physical examination showed the right thumb metacarpophalangeal joint was erythematous, warm, and painful with movement. Both ankles showed effusion and warmth without erythema, with pain on all range of motion. No fever, chills, night sweats, or systemic symptoms were reported. Joint stiffness was not worse in the morning and did not improve throughout the day. Symptoms had not improved despite 4 days of methylprednisolone therapy.

Acute bacterial infection of one or more joints, commonly caused by S. aureus. It produces painful, warm, swollen joints and can occur without fever, particularly in older adults or after corticosteroid exposure. The image is consistent with gram-positive cocci in clusters growing on blood and chocolate agar.
symptoms_in_common: Warmth, swelling, and effusion of involved joints
Erythematous and painful right thumb metacarpophalangeal joint
Bilateral ankle effusions with pain on range of motion
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, or other systemic symptoms
Recent unprotected vaginal intercourse

data.diagnosis: Disseminated gonococcal infection with gonococcal arthritis
data.description: Hematogenous dissemination of Neisseria gonorrhoeae can cause migratory polyarthralgia or septic arthritis, often affecting wrists, knees, ankles, and small joints. It may occur after unprotected sexual exposure and may have little or no genital symptomatology.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of prominent systemic symptoms can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked erythema and swelling initially centered in a thumb metacarpophalangeal joint
No rash or tenosynovitis reported
Gram-positive cocci in clusters on the provided microbiologic image are not typical of Neisseria gonorrhoeae

data.description: A sterile inflammatory arthritis that develops after genitourinary or gastrointestinal infection, including Chlamydia trachomatis. It commonly causes asymmetric lower-extremity arthritis and enthesitis.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sexual exposure that could precede a genitourinary infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent purulent-appearing inflammatory involvement of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint
Severe pain with warmth and effusions suggesting direct joint infection
No urethritis, cervicitis, conjunctivitis, uveitis, rash, or enthesitis reported
No improvement with corticosteroid therapy

data.description: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis that typically causes symmetric small-joint synovitis, prolonged morning stiffness, and gradual progression over weeks to months.
symptoms_in_common: Joint swelling, warmth, pain, and stiffness
More than one joint is affected
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset over days
Severe focal erythema of one thumb joint
Stiffness is not worse in the morning and does not improve during the day
Initial asymmetric pattern with sudden ankle involvement
No improvement after methylprednisolone therapy

data.description: A late manifestation of Borrelia burgdorferi infection that causes intermittent or persistent swelling of large joints, especially the knee, in individuals exposed to ticks in endemic regions such as New England.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of fever or systemic symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute onset over 9 days
Severe pain and marked warmth are more typical of septic arthritis than Lyme arthritis
Thumb metacarpophalangeal joint involvement is uncommon
No reported tick exposure, erythema migrans rash, or preceding flu-like illness
Multiple acutely inflamed joints with prominent erythema are atypical

data.description: A 29-year-old man presented to the hospital after several weeks of lumbar pain and fever up to 38°C. He had no significant past medical history. Physical examination revealed vital signs of blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 121/min, and body temperature 38.2°C. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly detected on examination. Laboratory tests showed anemia with hematocrit 31.8% and hemoglobin 11.8 g/dL, white blood cell count 3.92 × 10³/μL, elevated liver enzymes with AST 78 IU/L and ALT 71 IU/L, and markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase 1,591 IU/L. Serum cortisol level was 17.47 μg/dL at 8 AM and ACTH level was 12.1 pg/mL (normal range: 10-90). Ten days after admission, the patient developed pancytopenia with WBC 2.88 × 10³/μL, Hb 10.7 g/dL, and platelets 129 × 10³/μL. Bone marrow biopsy was negative for specific hematologic or malignant disorder.

data.diagnosis: Primary adrenal lymphoma (bilateral diffuse large B-cell lymphoma)
data.description: A rare extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma that often presents as bilateral adrenal masses, constitutional symptoms, high LDH, and may later cause adrenal insufficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral adrenal enlargement or masses on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age of 29 years, as primary adrenal lymphoma more often affects older adults
Normal morning cortisol and ACTH without clear adrenal insufficiency

data.description: An aggressive lymphoma in which malignant B cells proliferate within small blood vessels, often causing fever, cytopenias, very high LDH, liver abnormalities, and extranodal organ involvement without enlarged lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Possible bilateral adrenal, pulmonary, and hepatic involvement on imaging
Negative bone marrow biopsy can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Lumbar pain is not a classic dominant manifestation
Discrete bilateral adrenal masses are less typical than diffuse extranodal organ involvement

data.description: A systemic fungal infection that can involve the reticuloendothelial system and adrenal glands, producing fever, cytopenias, liver enzyme elevation, bilateral adrenal enlargement, and possible adrenal insufficiency.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported immunosuppression or exposure history
No hepatosplenomegaly, which is common in disseminated disease
Normal cortisol and ACTH without evident adrenal insufficiency
Bone marrow biopsy did not identify an infectious process

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with bilateral adrenal tuberculosis
data.description: Hematogenous tuberculosis may involve both adrenal glands and lungs, causing prolonged fever, constitutional illness, bilateral adrenal masses or enlargement, and eventual adrenal destruction.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary infiltrative abnormalities on chest imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase is less characteristic
No reported cough, weight loss, night sweats, or tuberculosis exposure
No clear adrenal insufficiency despite bilateral adrenal involvement
No hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy

data.description: A severe hyperinflammatory syndrome, frequently triggered by lymphoma or infection, characterized by persistent fever, cytopenias, liver dysfunction, high LDH, and often hepatosplenomegaly.
symptoms_in_common: Possible association with an occult lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly
No reported hyperferritinemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, or hemophagocytosis
Bilateral adrenal masses are not a typical primary feature
Bone marrow biopsy was negative for a specific hematologic disorder

diagnoses.name: Non-Hodgkin T-cell lymphoma, natural killer (NK)/T-cell, nasal type
diagnoses.title: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type

data.description: A 23-year-old female presented with a complaint of intermittent dyspnea (New York Heart Association NYHA grade, II), which aggravates on exertion and mild chest pain. No past significant medical and surgical history was given by the patient. On clinical examination, bruit was heard on auscultation in the left mid-zone.
A congenital persistent connection between the descending aorta and pulmonary artery, producing a left-to-right shunt and increased pulmonary blood flow.
symptoms_in_common: Thoracic bruit or continuous murmur over the left chest
Imaging appearance of an abnormal systemic-to-pulmonary vascular connection
symptoms_not_in_common: No typical symptoms are clearly inconsistent; many adults with a small or moderate PDA may have only mild symptoms

data.diagnosis: Patent ductus arteriosus with ductal aneurysm
data.description: An aneurysmal dilatation of a persistent ductus arteriosus, which may appear as a large vascular structure between the aortic arch/descending aorta and left pulmonary artery.
symptoms_in_common: Bruit on auscultation in the left chest
Young age with no prior medical history
Prominent abnormal mediastinal vascular structure on CT angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: No hoarseness
No dysphagia
No cough
No hemoptysis
No evidence provided of aneurysm rupture or compression symptoms

data.description: A rare congenital communication between the ascending aorta and pulmonary artery that causes a left-to-right shunt, pulmonary overcirculation, and potentially pulmonary hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal communication between systemic and pulmonary arterial structures on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation in adulthood is less typical because large aortopulmonary windows usually cause symptoms during infancy or childhood
No history of recurrent respiratory infections
No overt signs of heart failure
No cyanosis

data.diagnosis: Anomalous origin of the left pulmonary artery from the aorta (hemitruncus arteriosus)
data.description: A congenital anomaly in which one pulmonary artery, often the right but occasionally the left, originates from the aorta rather than the main pulmonary artery, causing excessive flow and pressure in the affected lung.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal enlarged left hilar/pulmonary arterial vascular structure on imaging
Young patient without acquired cardiopulmonary disease history
symptoms_not_in_common: Survival to age 23 without earlier severe symptoms is uncommon for an unrepaired major anomalous pulmonary artery origin
No recurrent childhood respiratory infections reported
No cyanosis reported
No clinical evidence of severe pulmonary hypertension provided

data.description: An abnormal direct communication between a pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein that creates a right-to-left shunt; lesions can produce a bruit and appear as enlarged tortuous pulmonary vessels on contrast imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Bruit over the left mid-lung zone
Abnormal prominent vascular structures in the left lung/hilum on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No hypoxemia or cyanosis reported
No hemoptysis reported
No migraine, stroke, or brain abscess history reported
No epistaxis or family history suggestive of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia reported

data.description: A 65-year-old man presented with bilateral leg swelling that had worsened over six weeks. He reported vague abdominal discomfort and tiredness. Physical examination revealed bilateral pitting edema up to the groin, without erythema, tenderness, or warmth. The patient was systemically well with normal heart sounds and clear chest examination. No palpable masses or lymphadenopathy were found in the abdomen. Laboratory testing showed normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 95 g/L; normal range 130-180), elevated C-reactive protein of 33.0 mg/L (normal range 0-5.0), and raised IgG4 level (3.55 g/L; normal range 0.08-1.4). Doppler ultrasound showed no deep vein thrombosis.

An IgG4-related fibroinflammatory disorder causing plaque-like soft-tissue thickening around the abdominal aorta, iliac vessels, ureters, and/or inferior vena cava. Venous or lymphatic compression can cause severe bilateral leg edema.
symptoms_in_common: Retroperitoneal periaortic soft-tissue abnormality on CT imaging
No deep vein thrombosis on Doppler ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: No other typical IgG4-related organ manifestations were reported, such as pancreatitis, salivary gland enlargement, or orbital disease

data.description: A chronic inflammatory fibrosing condition characterized by retroperitoneal tissue surrounding the aorta and iliac vessels, often causing obstruction of ureters, veins, or lymphatics. Some cases are now recognized as part of IgG4-related disease.
symptoms_in_common: Six-week progression of bilateral leg edema
Pitting edema extending to the groin
Periaortic retroperitoneal soft-tissue process on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly raised serum IgG4, which favors an IgG4-related subtype rather than truly idiopathic disease
No reported flank pain, renal impairment, hydronephrosis, or urinary symptoms

data.description: Lymphoma can produce retroperitoneal soft-tissue masses or nodal conglomerates that compress the inferior vena cava, iliac veins, or lymphatic channels, resulting in bilateral lower-extremity edema.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral leg edema due to possible venous or lymphatic obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable lymphadenopathy
No reported fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss
Raised IgG4 is not a typical primary finding of lymphoma
Systemically well appearance

data.diagnosis: Malignancy-associated retroperitoneal fibrosis or metastatic retroperitoneal malignancy
data.description: Solid tumors, including prostate, colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, renal, or urothelial cancers, can cause retroperitoneal infiltration or secondary fibrosis that obstructs major pelvic veins and lymphatics.
symptoms_in_common: Retroperitoneal soft-tissue abnormality that could cause venous obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable abdominal mass
No lymphadenopathy on examination
No reported weight loss, anorexia, bowel symptoms, urinary symptoms, or bleeding
Raised IgG4 is not typical of most metastatic solid malignancies

data.description: A rare non-Langerhans histiocytic disorder that may cause retroperitoneal infiltration, periaortic sheathing ('coated aorta'), renal or ureteric involvement, and vascular compression. It most often affects middle-aged or older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Age in the typical affected range
Leg edema potentially related to retroperitoneal vascular or lymphatic compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Raised IgG4 is not a characteristic finding
No reported bone pain or symmetric long-bone abnormalities
No reported diabetes insipidus, orbital involvement, cardiac involvement, or renal/perirenal infiltration

data.description: A 19-year-old man with no previous medical problems presented with a six-day history of breathlessness and left-sided chest pain that had started acutely. On examination, his respiratory rate was 22 breaths per minute with oxygen saturations of 95% on room air. The patient had no significant past medical history and no other baseline characteristics were reported.

Air in the pleural space causing partial or near-complete collapse of the left lung. This is common in otherwise healthy young men and the radiograph shows a hyperlucent left hemithorax with absent peripheral lung markings and a collapsed lung medially.
symptoms_in_common: Tachypnea with respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute
Young man with no previous medical problems
Oxygen saturation can remain relatively preserved in an uncomplicated pneumothorax
symptoms_not_in_common: Six-day duration is somewhat longer than the usual immediate presentation, although it can occur

data.description: A large pneumothorax involves substantial pleural air and marked reduction in visible aerated lung on the affected side. The chest radiograph appearance is consistent with a large left-sided pneumothorax.
symptoms_in_common: Marked left-sided hyperlucency with absent peripheral vascular markings on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Oxygen saturation of 95% on room air is relatively preserved despite the apparently large radiographic pneumothorax
No severe respiratory distress was reported

data.description: A life-threatening form of pneumothorax in which rising pleural pressure compresses the lung and may impair venous return and circulation. It is diagnosed clinically, often with radiographic mediastinal shift when imaging is obtained.
symptoms_in_common: Large unilateral pneumothorax appearance on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Oxygen saturation is relatively normal at 95% on room air
No hypotension, tachycardia, altered mental status, or hemodynamic instability was reported
No clear mediastinal shift away from the left side was reported or is obvious on the image

data.description: A pneumothorax caused by an underlying lung disorder, such as emphysematous bullae, asthma, cystic fibrosis, infection, or interstitial lung disease. It may resemble a primary pneumothorax radiographically.
symptoms_in_common: Chest radiograph findings compatible with a left pneumothorax
symptoms_not_in_common: No known prior lung disease or medical history
Age 19 years is less typical for many causes of secondary spontaneous pneumothorax
No chronic respiratory symptoms were reported

data.description: A large air-filled space within the lung can create unilateral hyperlucency and may mimic a pneumothorax on chest radiography. Differentiation may require CT imaging, especially if a pleural line is uncertain.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset of symptoms is more typical of pneumothorax than a stable giant bulla
No history of smoking, emphysema, connective-tissue disease, or chronic lung disease was reported
The radiographic absence of peripheral lung markings and apparent collapsed lung favor pneumothorax rather than a bulla

data.description: 28-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented with fatigue and migratory joint pain. She had several days of right foot and ankle pain and swelling that resolved, followed by pain in the knees and hips and swelling/pain in the right elbow, with intermittent low-grade fevers. On initial exam, she was febrile (38.3°C), tachycardic, and had diffuse joint tenderness without swelling, erythema, or limited range of motion. Five days later, she returned with progressive shortness of breath worse when supine and persistent right knee pain/stiffness. Repeat exam showed mild fever, tachycardia, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral crackles, a holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla, and a warm left knee with limited range of motion and severe pain on flexion.

data.diagnosis: Acute rheumatic fever with rheumatic carditis and mitral regurgitation
data.description: A post-streptococcal autoimmune inflammatory illness characterized by migratory polyarthritis and carditis. Carditis can cause valvulitis, most often involving the mitral valve, resulting in mitral regurgitation and heart failure.
symptoms_in_common: Migratory joint pain involving ankles, knees, hips, and elbow
Transient swelling and pain of the right foot and ankle
New holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla, consistent with mitral regurgitation
Shortness of breath worse when supine
Bilateral crackles suggesting congestive heart failure
Warm painful knee with restricted movement
Echocardiographic appearance consistent with significant mitral regurgitation
symptoms_not_in_common: No preceding sore throat or documented group A streptococcal infection is reported
No rash, subcutaneous nodules, chorea, or erythema marginatum is described

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis with mitral valve regurgitation
data.description: An infection of the endocardial surface, usually involving a cardiac valve. Valve destruction can produce acute mitral regurgitation and pulmonary congestion; immune phenomena can cause arthralgias or arthritis.
symptoms_in_common: New holosystolic murmur consistent with mitral regurgitation
Echocardiographic evidence of significant mitral regurgitation
symptoms_not_in_common: Migratory large-joint arthritis is more characteristic of acute rheumatic fever than infective endocarditis
No reported intravenous drug use, prosthetic valve, congenital heart disease, or other clear endocarditis risk factor
No embolic skin lesions, petechiae, splinter hemorrhages, or neurologic deficits are described
No persistent high fever or positive blood cultures are reported

data.description: Hematogenous spread of Neisseria gonorrhoeae that commonly causes migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, and later septic monoarthritis, usually in sexually active young adults.
symptoms_in_common: Initial ankle and foot pain/swelling followed by involvement of other joints
Painful warm knee with limited range of motion, compatible with gonococcal septic arthritis
symptoms_not_in_common: New mitral regurgitation murmur is not typical
Orthopnea, elevated jugular venous pressure, and bilateral crackles are not typical
Heart failure findings are not typical
No rash or tenosynovitis is described
No genital, urinary, or pelvic symptoms are reported

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with inflammatory arthritis and cardiac involvement
data.description: A systemic autoimmune disease that can cause constitutional symptoms, migratory or symmetric inflammatory arthralgias/arthritis, serositis, myocarditis, and Libman-Sacks valvular disease.
symptoms_in_common: Migratory polyarthralgia involving multiple large joints
Possible cardiac involvement causing dyspnea and tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute severe mitral regurgitation with a classic holosystolic murmur is less typical than rheumatic valvulitis
No malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, Raynaud phenomenon, renal symptoms, or cytopenia findings are reported
Marked pulmonary congestion and elevated jugular venous pressure are not typical initial manifestations of lupus arthritis
The episodic migratory large-joint pattern is more characteristic of acute rheumatic fever

data.diagnosis: Viral myocarditis or myopericarditis with viral polyarthritis
data.description: Viral infection can cause fever, fatigue, arthralgias, and myocardial inflammation leading to impaired cardiac function, dyspnea, and signs of heart failure. Some viruses, such as parvovirus B19, can cause prominent arthralgias.
symptoms_in_common: Shortness of breath worse when supine
symptoms_not_in_common: A new holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla indicates mitral regurgitation and is not a typical primary feature of uncomplicated viral myocarditis
Migratory arthritis with transient joint swelling is less typical
A severely warm knee with major limitation of flexion is more suggestive of inflammatory or septic arthritis
No preceding viral respiratory or gastrointestinal syndrome is reported

data.description: A 56-year-old female patient presented with low-back and hip pain radiating down to her left leg for 12 months. She did not respond to initial management with conservative therapy of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications.

data.diagnosis: Tuberculous spondylodiscitis (Pott disease) with epidural/paraspinal extension
data.description: Spinal tuberculosis is a chronic infection of vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs that can cause vertebral destruction, paraspinal or psoas collections, epidural extension, and nerve-root compression.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating into the left leg, consistent with nerve-root compression
Failure to improve with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medication
Imaging appearance of destructive lumbar vertebral/disc disease with adjacent soft-tissue and epidural involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as fever, night sweats, weight loss, or fatigue were reported

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic lumbar spondylodiscitis with epidural abscess
data.description: Pyogenic spondylodiscitis is a bacterial infection of an intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral endplates. It may extend into the epidural space or paraspinal tissues and produce radicular pain or neurologic deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Poor response to conservative anti-inflammatory treatment
Imaging findings suggestive of disc-space/endplate destruction with epidural and paraspinal inflammatory extension
symptoms_not_in_common: The very prolonged 12-month course is less typical of acute pyogenic infection
No fever, systemic illness, or acute severe deterioration was reported

data.description: Brucellar spondylodiscitis is a subacute or chronic spinal infection caused by Brucella species, often involving the lumbar spine and causing back pain, endplate abnormalities, disc involvement, and occasionally epidural or paraspinal collections.
symptoms_in_common: Radiation of pain into the left leg
Lack of improvement with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medication
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported exposure to livestock, unpasteurized dairy products, or an endemic setting
No reported fever, sweats, malaise, or generalized arthralgia

data.diagnosis: Lumbar spinal metastasis with epidural tumor extension
data.description: Metastatic cancer involving the lumbar vertebrae can cause destructive bone lesions, epidural soft-tissue extension, neural compression, and persistent back pain with radiculopathy.
