symptoms_in_common: Unilateral radiating leg pain suggesting nerve-root involvement
Destructive-appearing vertebral abnormality with possible epidural soft-tissue component on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No known history of cancer was provided
No reported weight loss, night pain predominance, or other systemic cancer symptoms
Disc-space involvement and adjacent inflammatory/collection-like changes are less typical for metastasis than for infection

data.diagnosis: Degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis or disc disease with radiculopathy
data.description: Degenerative disc disease, facet arthropathy, and spinal canal or foraminal stenosis can compress lumbar nerve roots, producing chronic low-back pain and pain radiating into one leg.
symptoms_in_common: Left-leg radiating pain consistent with lumbar radiculopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Failure to respond to anti-inflammatory therapy
Imaging appearance of vertebral endplate destruction and prominent epidural/paraspinal soft-tissue abnormality is not typical of uncomplicated degenerative disease

data.description: A 57-year-old male patient presented with a three-month history of fatigue, recurrent sore throats, and a persistent 'cold sore.' The patient had no relevant medical history, drank little alcohol, and was a non-smoker.

data.diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lip with regional lymph-node metastasis
data.description: A malignant tumor of squamous cells, commonly affecting the lower lip or oral commissure. It may present as a persistent crusted ulcer and can spread to submental or submandibular lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent nonhealing 'cold sore' at the lip corner
Possible enlarged submandibular or cervical lymph node shown by the neck swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent sore throats are not a classic presenting feature
No smoking history, although lip squamous cell carcinoma can occur in nonsmokers
Little alcohol intake, which reduces but does not exclude risk

data.diagnosis: Chronic herpes simplex virus type 1 infection
data.description: HSV-1 commonly causes painful recurrent vesicles and crusted erosions around the lips. Persistent, extensive, or nonhealing lesions can occur in people with impaired immunity.
symptoms_in_common: Lesion described as a persistent 'cold sore'
Crusted lesion at the lip margin
Recurrent sore throats may accompany viral illness
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistence for three months is atypical in an immunocompetent person
A prominent submandibular or cervical neck mass is not typical of uncomplicated herpes labialis
The lesion appears ulcerative and indurated rather than a typical cluster of short-lived vesicles

data.diagnosis: Human immunodeficiency virus infection with opportunistic oral herpes infection
data.description: HIV causes progressive immune dysfunction and may present with fatigue, recurrent infections, persistent mucocutaneous herpes lesions, and enlarged lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent sore throats or recurrent infections
Persistent or atypical cold-sore-like oral lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: No other opportunistic infections are described
No fever, weight loss, night sweats, diarrhea, or generalized lymphadenopathy are reported
A solitary ulcerated lip lesion may instead represent a local malignancy

data.diagnosis: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: Non-Hodgkin lymphomas are cancers of lymphocytes that can cause persistent lymph-node enlargement, fatigue, recurrent infections, and occasionally extranodal lesions involving the oral cavity.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent sore throats or recurrent infections
Possible enlarged cervical or submandibular lymph node
Persistent oral or lip lesion can occur with extranodal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: A crusted lesion clinically resembling a cold sore is not a typical initial presentation
No reported fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss
Only one apparent neck node is described rather than widespread lymphadenopathy

data.diagnosis: Basal cell carcinoma of the perioral skin
data.description: Basal cell carcinoma is a slow-growing skin cancer associated with ultraviolet exposure. It can produce a persistent ulcerated or crusted lesion near the lip, although spread to lymph nodes is uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent nonhealing crusted ulcer near the lip
Location on a sun-exposed facial area
symptoms_not_in_common: Cervical or submandibular lymph-node enlargement is unusual because basal cell carcinoma rarely metastasizes
Fatigue is not usually caused by localized basal cell carcinoma
Recurrent sore throats are not typical
The lesion at the lip margin is more suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma or chronic infection

diagnoses.name: Perioral lesion with plasma cell rich infiltrate
diagnoses.title: Plasma cell neoplasms

data.description: 28-year-old male patient admitted on November 27, 2013, complaining of diarrhea (loose stool, three to five times per day) for over 10 years and hematochezia for about 1 month. Had been diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia 5 months after birth, with hemoglobin level remaining 70-80 g/L (normal range 110-150 g/L) for most of the time. On admission, albumin level was 26 g/L (normal range 35-52 g/L). Liver and renal function were otherwise normal. Patient reported recurrent arthralgia in the knee and ankle joints.

A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can involve any part of the gastrointestinal tract, often causing patchy transmural inflammation, ulceration, bowel-wall thickening, strictures, malabsorption, and extraintestinal joint manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic diarrhea for more than 10 years
Hypoalbuminemia consistent with intestinal protein loss or malnutrition
Imaging suggesting bowel-wall thickening and possible segmental intestinal involvement
Endoscopic inflammatory mucosal lesions and possible narrowing/ulceration
symptoms_not_in_common: Iron deficiency anemia beginning at 5 months of age is unusually early for typical Crohn disease
Hemoglobin persistently 70-80 g/L since infancy is more severe and longstanding than usual without earlier recognized inflammatory bowel disease

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease limited to the colon and rectum, characterized by continuous superficial colonic inflammation, bloody diarrhea, anemia, hypoalbuminemia in severe disease, and possible peripheral arthritis.
symptoms_in_common: Iron deficiency anemia from chronic intestinal blood loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Possible small-bowel involvement or segmental disease on imaging is not typical
Intestinal stricturing or deep ulceration would be less typical than in Crohn disease
Severe anemia present since infancy is unusual
A history of diarrhea for more than 10 years without earlier prominent rectal bleeding is less typical

data.description: A congenital or early-onset disorder of intestinal lymphatic drainage causing protein-losing enteropathy, diarrhea, malabsorption, edema, hypoalbuminemia, and sometimes iron deficiency. Endoscopy may show whitish villi, mucosal edema, or nodular changes.
symptoms_in_common: Very early onset illness suggested by anemia beginning in infancy
Possible bowel-wall edema or thickening on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematochezia is not a typical feature
Recurrent knee and ankle arthralgia is not typical
Inflammatory ulceration or bowel stenosis would be atypical unless another inflammatory bowel disorder is also present

data.diagnosis: Common variable immunodeficiency with nodular lymphoid hyperplasia/enteropathy
data.description: An immune-deficiency syndrome that can cause chronic infectious or inflammatory diarrhea, malabsorption, nodular lymphoid hyperplasia of the intestine, protein loss, anemia, and inflammatory arthritis-like symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Possible intestinal nodular lesions on endoscopy
Arthralgia can occur with immune dysregulation
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of recurrent respiratory, sinus, or other infections is reported
Hematochezia is less typical unless there is associated colitis or another gastrointestinal complication
Anemia from 5 months of age would be unusual without severe early-onset immune deficiency

data.description: A systemic inflammatory vasculitis that may produce deep intestinal ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, diarrhea, anemia, hypoalbuminemia, and recurrent arthritis; it most commonly affects the ileocecal region.
symptoms_in_common: Possible ileocecal or segmental bowel involvement on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent oral ulcers are reported
No genital ulcers are reported
No eye inflammation, skin lesions, or vascular manifestations are reported
Anemia beginning in infancy is highly atypical for Behçet disease

data.description: A 65-year-old male retired farmer presented with an inability to fully straighten the ring finger and little finger of his right hand, which had progressed over the past two years. He had recently noticed a 'rope like' swelling in his palm with no history of trauma. His medical history was unremarkable except for smoking cessation 10 years earlier with a 90 pack-year history. His father had a similar deformity. On examination, he had palpable cords to his middle, ring, and little fingers with palpable nodules on the volar aspect of all proximal phalanges, causing flexion contractures of the proximal interphalangeal joints. The cord and nodules in the ring finger were adherent to the overlying skin.
A benign fibroproliferative disorder of the palmar fascia that forms nodules and cords, progressively causing flexion contractures, most often affecting the ring and little fingers.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive inability to fully straighten the ring and little fingers
Palpable palmar cords extending toward the middle, ring, and little fingers
Palpable volar nodules over the proximal phalanges
Adherence of the ring-finger cord and nodules to the overlying skin
Positive family history in his father
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms are substantially atypical; the presentation is classic for Dupuytren disease

data.description: Inflammation and thickening around the flexor tendon pulley, usually at the A1 pulley, causing painful catching, clicking, or locking of a finger during flexion and extension.
symptoms_in_common: Palmar thickening or nodular swelling may be felt near the base of a finger
symptoms_not_in_common: No pain, clicking, catching, or episodic locking was reported
Palpable cords extending along the palm and digits are not typical
Multiple volar proximal-phalanx nodules are not typical
Fixed progressive proximal interphalangeal flexion contractures are less typical
Skin adherence over the cord is not typical
Family history of a similar deformity is more characteristic of Dupuytren disease

data.diagnosis: Flexor tendon adhesion or post-traumatic flexion contracture
data.description: Scarring of the flexor tendons or surrounding soft tissues after injury, surgery, infection, or immobilization, which can restrict finger extension and produce contractures.
symptoms_in_common: Limited ability to actively extend the ring and little fingers
Possible palpable thickening along the flexor tendon pathway
symptoms_not_in_common: There is no history of hand trauma, surgery, infection, or immobilization
The course is associated with characteristic palmar cords and nodules rather than scar tissue
Skin adherence and multiple fascial nodules are more typical of palmar fibromatosis
Positive family history is not typical
Simultaneous involvement of several digits in a stereotyped ulnar distribution is less typical

data.description: A congenital or developmental condition characterized by a persistent flexion deformity, usually of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the little finger and sometimes other fingers.
symptoms_in_common: Potential involvement of more than one finger
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation began later in life rather than in childhood or adolescence
Progressive rope-like palmar cord is not typical
Palpable palmar and volar digital nodules are not typical
Ring-finger skin adherence is not typical
The strong familial pattern with palmar fascial cords is more consistent with Dupuytren disease
Middle, ring, and little finger palmar fascial involvement is not typical

data.description: A complication of long-standing diabetes characterized by waxy thickened skin and painless limitation of finger extension due to periarticular connective-tissue glycation and fibrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Palmar and digital skin thickening may be present
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of diabetes mellitus was reported
Discrete rope-like palmar cords are not typical
Palpable focal nodules over the proximal phalanges are not typical
Involvement is usually more diffuse and often bilateral rather than focused on ring and little fingers
Skin adherence to a specific cord is more suggestive of Dupuytren disease
Family history of an identical palmar contracture is not typical

data.description: 57-year-old man with 8-year HIV infection and a 10-year history of bilateral inguinal hernias, presenting with 3 weeks of worsening left inguinal pain and enlarging hernia. Over the prior 3 months, pain with the bulging had increased. In the 3 weeks before presentation, he developed intermittent subjective fevers, night sweats, and hard, tender lumps adjacent to the hernia; the night before presentation, his temperature reached 38.1°C. HIV was well controlled on antiretroviral therapy (CD4 250/mm³, undetectable viral load). Past history included Kaposi sarcoma, molluscum contagiosum, anal dysplasia, pulmonary Mycobacterium avium complex infection, pneumocystis pneumonia, thrush, preseptal cellulitis, and cryptosporidium-related diarrhea. On examination, he was afebrile with stable vital signs and had easily reducible bilateral inguinal hernias with bulky, slightly tender left inguinal lymphadenopathy, including three large nodes up to 3 cm.

data.diagnosis: Syphilitic lymphadenitis due to secondary syphilis
data.description: Lymph-node involvement by Treponema pallidum during secondary syphilis, which can cause prominent regional or generalized lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms; spirochetes may be demonstrated in the node by immunohistochemistry.
symptoms_in_common: Enlarging hard lumps adjacent to the hernia
HIV infection, which increases risk of sexually transmitted infections and atypical presentations
symptoms_not_in_common: Long-standing bilateral reducible inguinal hernias
Pain specifically associated with hernia bulging
No reported rash, mucous patches, genital ulcer, or other classic secondary-syphilis skin findings

data.description: A human herpesvirus 8-associated lymphoproliferative disorder in people with HIV, characterized by inflammatory flares, constitutional symptoms, and enlarged lymph nodes at multiple sites.
symptoms_in_common: History of Kaposi sarcoma, suggesting prior HHV-8-associated disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Lymphadenopathy appears predominantly localized to the left inguinal region rather than clearly multicentric
No reported weight loss, edema, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, or generalized inflammatory syndrome
Long-standing bilateral reducible inguinal hernias are not typical manifestations

data.description: Aggressive B-cell lymphomas occur more often in people with HIV and may present with rapidly enlarging lymph nodes, fever, night sweats, and extranodal disease.
symptoms_in_common: New bulky inguinal lymphadenopathy with nodes up to 3 cm
Subacute progression over weeks to months
symptoms_not_in_common: The lymph nodes are tender, whereas lymphoma nodes are often painless
No reported weight loss, generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or extranodal mass
Reducible bilateral inguinal hernias are unrelated to lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Mycobacterial lymphadenitis, including recurrent Mycobacterium avium complex infection
data.description: Mycobacterial infection can cause chronic lymph-node enlargement and constitutional symptoms in immunocompromised patients; disseminated MAC is particularly associated with advanced HIV immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Previous pulmonary Mycobacterium avium complex infection
symptoms_not_in_common: CD4 count of 250/mm³ and undetectable HIV viral load make disseminated MAC less typical than in severe immunosuppression
No reported chronic weight loss, diarrhea, abdominal pain, anemia, or diffuse adenopathy
Long-standing reducible inguinal hernias are not typical of mycobacterial infection

data.diagnosis: Inguinal lymphadenitis from a local genital, perianal, or lower-extremity infection
data.description: Reactive or bacterial lymphadenitis develops when lymph nodes draining the lower abdomen, genital region, perianal area, or legs respond to infection or inflammation in those areas.
symptoms_in_common: Hard painful lumps in the groin
History of anal dysplasia and prior skin infections, which may indicate potential local inflammatory or infectious sources
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported genital lesion, perianal abscess, leg wound, cellulitis, urethral symptoms, or skin infection
Night sweats may suggest a systemic infection or malignancy rather than uncomplicated local bacterial lymphadenitis
Bilateral long-standing reducible inguinal hernias do not explain infectious lymphadenitis

diagnoses.name: Necrotizing lymphadenitis
diagnoses.title: Histiocytic necrotising lymphadenitis of Kikuchi and Fujimoto

data.description: A 16-year-old girl presented with acute left shoulder pain, left-sided chest pain, and shortness of breath. She had a 4-month history of intermittent left shoulder and left-sided chest pain following a dance recital, which had been treated with analgesia and physiotherapy. She denied fever, cough, orthopnea, weight loss, and appetite change. Physical examination revealed tenderness at the location of the left fifth rib and reduced left chest expansion.

data.diagnosis: Ewing sarcoma of the rib (chest-wall Ewing sarcoma)
data.description: A malignant small round-cell bone tumor that commonly affects adolescents and can arise from a rib, causing a chest-wall soft-tissue mass, pleural involvement, pain, and respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain beginning after a dance recital and initially resembling a musculoskeletal injury
Absence of fever, weight loss, and appetite change

data.description: An aggressive peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor within the Ewing sarcoma family that typically arises in the chest wall of children and adolescents and may involve ribs, pleura, and soft tissues.
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as weight loss or reduced appetite
Initial association with physical activity during a dance recital

data.description: A primary malignant bone-forming tumor that rarely arises in the ribs and may present as focal chest-wall pain, swelling, cortical destruction, and an adjacent soft-tissue mass.
symptoms_in_common: Pain that may initially be attributed to trauma or activity
Shortness of breath due to an intrathoracic mass or pleural reaction
symptoms_not_in_common: Left shoulder pain without a reported chest-wall swelling
No reported palpable mass

data.diagnosis: Primary bone lymphoma of the rib
data.description: A malignant lymphoid tumor involving bone that can cause persistent localized bone pain and may produce a chest-wall soft-tissue component; it is less common in adolescents than Ewing sarcoma.
symptoms_in_common: Possible shortness of breath if there is pleural or chest-wall involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age of 16 years
Acute worsening after a four-month history
Absence of fever, weight loss, appetite change, or other constitutional symptoms

data.diagnosis: Rib osteomyelitis with chest-wall inflammatory mass or empyema
data.description: Infection of a rib can cause focal pain and tenderness and may extend into adjacent soft tissues or pleural space, producing reduced chest expansion and breathlessness.
symptoms_in_common: Possible progression over weeks to months
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No cough
No reported infectious prodrome
Four months of intermittent pain without systemic illness
Initial onset after a dance recital

diagnoses.name: Rib osteosarcoma
diagnoses.title: Osteosarcoma of bone or articular cartilage of ribs, sternum or clavicle

data.description: A 66-year-old man presented with a 4 to 5-month history of fever, chills, drenching night sweats, and unintentional 35-kg weight loss. He had previously undergone work-up for fever of unknown origin including evaluation for infectious causes such as tuberculosis, typhoid, and brucellosis, but these were not revealing. On physical examination, his spleen was palpable but no adenopathy was detected. Blood tests revealed anemia with hemoglobin of 9.0 g/dL (normal 13.0-18.0 g/dL), microcytosis with mean corpuscular volume of 75 fl (normal 80.0-94.0 fl), normal platelet count of 354,000/μL, and elevated international normalized ratio of 1.30 (normal 0.85-1.20). His serum ferritin level was significantly elevated at 1,796.0 ng/mL (normal 25-310 ng/mL).

A rare form of classical Hodgkin lymphoma confined predominantly to the spleen, characterized by malignant Reed-Sternberg cells that are often CD30-positive and associated with constitutional symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy can occur in primary splenic disease
Cytology/immunostaining appearance suggestive of large atypical Reed-Sternberg-like cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytosis is not a classic specific feature of Hodgkin lymphoma
Mildly elevated INR is not a typical defining finding

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving the spleen
data.description: An aggressive non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma that can present as a splenic mass, constitutional symptoms, anemia, and elevated inflammatory markers.
symptoms_in_common: No palpable lymphadenopathy may occur with primary splenic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: The illustrated large cells with a Reed-Sternberg-like appearance and likely CD30 staining are more suggestive of classical Hodgkin lymphoma
Microcytic anemia is not specifically typical of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Mild INR elevation is not a usual presenting feature

data.description: A CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma composed of large pleomorphic malignant cells that may mimic Hodgkin lymphoma and can cause systemic B symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical cells with possible CD30 positivity on immunostaining
symptoms_not_in_common: An isolated dominant splenic mass without lymphadenopathy is less typical
Splenomegaly as the main clinical site is less common
Microcytic anemia is not characteristic
Mild INR elevation is not characteristic

data.description: An indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that commonly presents with splenomegaly, cytopenias, and little or no peripheral lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_not_in_common: High-grade fever and drenching night sweats are less typical
Extreme 35-kg weight loss is less typical of this indolent lymphoma
A discrete splenic mass is less typical than diffuse splenic enlargement
Large atypical Reed-Sternberg-like cells and CD30-positive staining would not be expected
Marked ferritin elevation is not a classic feature

data.description: A severe hyperinflammatory syndrome, often triggered by lymphoma or infection, causing persistent fever, splenomegaly, cytopenias, and markedly elevated ferritin.
symptoms_in_common: Constitutional symptoms including weight loss and night sweats
Possible mild coagulation abnormality reflected by elevated INR
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal platelet count is less typical because hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis commonly causes bicytopenia or pancytopenia
A focal splenic mass is not typical of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis itself
The presence of large malignant-appearing cells suggests an underlying lymphoma rather than isolated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis

diagnoses.name: Splenic involvement
diagnoses.title: Fibrosis of spleen[Schistosomiasis involving the skin]

data.description: 52-year-old man with hypertension, benign prostatic hypertrophy, chronic renal insufficiency requiring dialysis until a living-related renal transplant 1 year prior, and hyperparathyroidism s/p bilateral cataract surgery presented with acute palpitations and chest pressure. Two days earlier he developed epigastric burning, fatigue, weakness, and vomiting, partially relieved by antacids; he denied fever or chills. On arrival, heart rate was 200 bpm with atrial fibrillation and rapid ventricular response; after cardioversion, pulse was 53 bpm and blood pressure 128/90 mmHg. Exam showed a diffuse, laterally displaced apical impulse, prominent S2, and an S4, without murmurs or jugular venous distention. Labs showed creatinine 1.5 mg/dL, troponin T 1.04 ng/mL, 2+ proteinuria, and markedly reduced leukocyte α-galactosidase activity.

An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-galactosidase A deficiency, leading to globotriaosylceramide accumulation in the kidneys, heart, nervous system, and other organs. Cardiac involvement commonly causes concentric left-ventricular hypertrophy, conduction abnormalities, atrial arrhythmias, and myocardial injury.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic renal failure requiring dialysis before renal transplantation
Left-ventricular hypertrophy suggested by laterally displaced apical impulse, S4, and ECG changes
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
symptoms_not_in_common: Vomiting
Epigastric burning partially relieved by antacids
Hypertension

data.description: A genetic myocardial disorder characterized by abnormal myocardial thickening, often involving the left ventricle, which can cause diastolic dysfunction, ischemic chest pain, atrial fibrillation, and sudden arrhythmias. The imaging findings are compatible with substantial ventricular hypertrophy.
symptoms_in_common: S4 gallop indicating impaired ventricular relaxation
ECG evidence of left-ventricular hypertrophy with repolarization abnormalities
Elevated troponin, which can occur from demand ischemia or microvascular ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity
Long-standing renal failure requiring dialysis
Proteinuria
History of renal transplantation
Early cataracts
Vomiting and epigastric burning

data.diagnosis: Hypertensive heart disease with left-ventricular hypertrophy
data.description: Chronic hypertension can produce concentric left-ventricular hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction, resulting in an S4, repolarization changes on ECG, atrial enlargement, and atrial fibrillation.
symptoms_in_common: Electrocardiographic left-ventricular hypertrophy and strain-type repolarization changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity
Renal failure severe enough to require dialysis at a relatively young age
Proteinuria despite renal transplantation
History of early cataracts
Vomiting and epigastric burning

data.diagnosis: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction or acute coronary syndrome
data.description: Acute myocardial ischemia caused by coronary plaque rupture, thrombosis, or supply-demand mismatch. It may present with chest pressure, gastrointestinal symptoms, arrhythmias, and elevated cardiac troponin without classic ST-segment elevation.
symptoms_in_common: Epigastric burning, which can be an anginal equivalent
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, which may accompany or provoke myocardial ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity
Chronic proteinuria and prior dialysis-dependent renal failure as a unifying feature
Marked ventricular hypertrophy suggestive of infiltrative or storage cardiomyopathy
History of early cataracts

data.description: An infiltrative cardiomyopathy caused by extracellular amyloid deposition in the myocardium. It commonly produces increased ventricular wall thickness, diastolic dysfunction, atrial arrhythmias, conduction disease, proteinuria, and renal impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Ventricular hypertrophy or increased wall thickness on cardiac imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity
Early cataracts
Relatively preserved blood pressure without signs of restrictive heart failure
No jugular venous distention
Vomiting and antacid-responsive epigastric burning

data.description: Male infant, 22 hours old, admitted for repeated right-sided limb clonic seizures for 16 hours. Born at 40+6 weeks by cesarean section after fetal heart monitoring showed frequent variable decelerations 1 hour before delivery; amniotic fluid was decreased and mildly turbid, with no premature rupture of membranes. Apgar scores were 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes; birth weight 3380 g. Seizures began 6 hours after birth, involved the right limbs, were not associated with consciousness disturbance or cyanosis, resolved spontaneously, and occurred 4 times. On admission: T 36.7°C, P 125/min, R 46/min, BP 74/47 mmHg; weight 3290 g, head circumference 36 cm. Physical examination showed alertness with good response, normal skin color, flat anterior fontanelle, equal reactive pupils, coarse breath sounds without rales, normal cardiac exam, soft abdomen without masses, normal bowel sounds, and normal limb movement, muscle tone, and primitive reflexes.

data.diagnosis: Neonatal arterial ischemic stroke (left middle cerebral artery territory)
data.description: An acute focal cerebral infarction caused by arterial occlusion, most often involving the middle cerebral artery in term neonates. Diffusion-restricted left hemispheric cortical injury and focal contralateral seizures strongly support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Seizures beginning within the first 24 hours of life
Repeated focal clonic seizures involving the right limbs
Term infant with otherwise relatively normal neurologic examination
MRI appearance of focal left cerebral diffusion restriction consistent with acute infarction
Possible perinatal fetal distress with variable decelerations before delivery
symptoms_not_in_common: No persistent weakness or asymmetry was detected on the initial examination
No altered consciousness was reported
No cyanosis or major systemic instability was reported

data.description: Brain injury caused by impaired oxygen delivery and/or cerebral perfusion around birth. It may cause neonatal seizures, although injury is more often diffuse or bilateral than a single arterial-territory lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Neonatal seizures in the first day after birth
Fetal heart-rate variable decelerations before delivery
MRI diffusion abnormality can occur after hypoxic-ischemic injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Apgar scores were normal at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
No need for resuscitation was described
The seizures were focal and unilateral rather than multifocal or generalized
The infant was alert with normal tone, reflexes, and limb movement
Imaging appears focal and unilateral, rather than the more typical bilateral basal-ganglia, thalamic, or watershed injury pattern

data.diagnosis: Neonatal intracranial hemorrhage (including focal intraparenchymal hemorrhage)
data.description: Bleeding within the brain, ventricles, or extra-axial spaces can provoke seizures in newborns. Hemorrhagic lesions may occur after birth trauma, coagulation abnormalities, or vascular injury.
symptoms_in_common: Focal right-sided clonic movements could result from a left hemispheric lesion
Cesarean delivery after evidence of fetal distress
symptoms_not_in_common: No bulging fontanelle was present
No anemia, shock, pallor, or hemodynamic instability was reported
No depressed consciousness or irritability was reported
No vomiting or rapidly increasing head circumference was reported
The described MRI diffusion pattern is more suggestive of ischemic infarction than primary hemorrhage

data.diagnosis: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) with venous infarction
data.description: Thrombosis of intracranial venous sinuses or cortical veins may cause neonatal seizures and can produce venous infarction, sometimes with hemorrhage. Dehydration, perinatal stress, and prothrombotic conditions may contribute.
symptoms_in_common: Focal seizures involving one side of the body
A focal brain lesion on MRI can occur with venous infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: No lethargy, poor feeding, apnea, or vomiting was reported
No bulging fontanelle or signs of raised intracranial pressure were present
No systemic dehydration or severe illness was described
The lesion appears more compatible with an arterial territorial infarct than the often non-territorial pattern of venous infarction
No venous sinus or cortical vein thrombosis was described on the provided vascular imaging

data.description: Central nervous system infection can present with seizures in newborns, including bacterial meningitis or viral encephalitis. Illness may initially be subtle but usually develops systemic or neurologic signs.
symptoms_in_common: Seizures in the first days of life
Mildly turbid amniotic fluid could raise concern for an infectious perinatal environment
Coarse breath sounds may indicate nonspecific associated respiratory findings
symptoms_not_in_common: Temperature was normal
The infant was alert and responsive
No poor feeding, lethargy, irritability, apnea, or respiratory failure was reported
No skin rash, cyanosis, or signs of sepsis were reported
No meningeal signs or abnormal fontanelle findings were reported
The focal arterial-territory MRI lesion is more typical of ischemic stroke than diffuse infectious encephalitis

data.description: 19-year-old woman with 3 weeks of right shoulder and right flank pain, followed 2 weeks later by exertional dyspnea and nonproductive cough that progressively worsened over 8 days, leading to severe shortness of breath with walking and wheelchair use by presentation. In the emergency department she appeared ill with increased work of breathing, tachycardia (132 bpm), tachypnea (>40/min), and hypoxemia (O2 saturation 88% on room air); a cardiac murmur was noted. She also had intermittent back pain for 6 months, asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection 2 months earlier, dental cleaning 5 weeks earlier, two episodes of diarrhea during a cruise, visible chest pulsations for 2 weeks, and labored breathing during sleep. Past history included anxiety and anemia. Labs showed microcytic anemia, leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, low albumin, and elevated inflammatory markers.

A granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis affecting the aorta and its major branches, most often in young women. It can cause aortic wall thickening, stenosis or aneurysmal change, aortic-root dilation with severe aortic regurgitation, and pulmonary hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings involving the aorta and major arterial branches
Findings compatible with significant aortic regurgitation and cardiac decompensation
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent dental cleaning
Two isolated episodes of diarrhea during a cruise
Nonproductive cough as a dominant symptom
Asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection shortly before presentation

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis with severe aortic regurgitation
data.description: Infection of the endocardial surface, usually involving a heart valve, which may produce vegetations, valve destruction, severe regurgitation, heart failure, and inflammatory laboratory abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Nonproductive cough due to pulmonary congestion
Recent dental procedure that could transiently cause bacteremia
Possible severe aortic-valve dysfunction on echocardiography
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever or chills
No reported embolic skin findings or neurologic deficits
Shoulder and flank pain preceding respiratory symptoms is nonspecific
Extensive aortic and branch-vessel wall abnormalities are not typical of isolated infective endocarditis

data.diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure from severe aortic regurgitation
data.description: Severe leakage of the aortic valve causes volume overload of the left ventricle and elevated pulmonary venous pressure, resulting in pulmonary edema, hypoxemic respiratory distress, and reduced exercise tolerance.
symptoms_in_common: Severe shortness of breath with minimal walking
Echocardiographic evidence compatible with severe aortic regurgitation
symptoms_not_in_common: Shoulder and flank pain
Six months of intermittent back pain
Leukocytosis and markedly elevated inflammatory markers unless there is an underlying inflammatory or infectious cause
Recent diarrhea

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arteries by thrombus, often causing acute or subacute dyspnea, tachycardia, hypoxemia, pleuritic pain, and right-heart strain.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel on a cruise, which may increase thrombotic risk
Prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, which can transiently increase thrombotic risk
symptoms_not_in_common: Cardiac murmur suggestive of structural valve disease
Visible chest pulsations
Findings of severe aortic regurgitation on echocardiography
Aortic and branch-vessel inflammatory imaging abnormalities
Prolonged inflammatory back, shoulder, and flank pain

data.diagnosis: Post-COVID inflammatory cardiac disease (myocarditis or aortitis)
data.description: Inflammatory cardiovascular disease temporally associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection can cause myocardial dysfunction, vascular inflammation, tachycardia, dyspnea, chest symptoms, and elevated inflammatory markers.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac symptoms with a new murmur or evidence of cardiac dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: SARS-CoV-2 illness was asymptomatic
Symptoms began with focal shoulder and flank pain
Six months of intermittent back pain predates COVID-19 infection
Severe aortic regurgitation and extensive large-vessel abnormalities are more suggestive of primary vasculitis or structural valve disease than isolated myocarditis

data.description: 56-year-old man with 7 days of worsening epigastric pain associated with nausea and belching. Past history includes traumatic splenectomy, hyperlipidaemia, obesity, and Bell’s palsy; prior CT showed multiple abdominal nodules consistent with splenunculi. He had started orlistat about 10 days before symptom onset. On examination he was haemodynamically stable, mildly febrile (37.5°C), with epigastric and left iliac fossa tenderness. Blood tests showed mild neutrophilia and elevated CRP, with normal liver, renal, amylase, and lipase results. Pain persisted despite analgesia and high-dose proton pump inhibitor therapy, and inflammatory markers worsened while awaiting endoscopy.

data.diagnosis: Torsion with infarction of an accessory spleen (splenunculus)
data.description: An accessory spleen can twist on its vascular pedicle, causing impaired blood supply, infarction, and focal intra-abdominal inflammation. This is particularly relevant in a patient with previous splenectomy and known splenunculi.
symptoms_in_common: Epigastric and left iliac fossa tenderness
History of traumatic splenectomy with known abdominal splenunculi
Persistent pain despite proton pump inhibitor therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: Belching
Recent commencement of orlistat

data.description: Mesenteric panniculitis is an inflammatory disorder of mesenteric fat that may cause a painful inflammatory mass or 'misty mesentery' on CT, sometimes associated with prior abdominal trauma or surgery.
symptoms_in_common: CT appearance of inflammatory change in the mesentery
History of prior abdominal trauma and surgery
symptoms_not_in_common: Left iliac fossa tenderness is less characteristic
Belching is not a typical feature
Abrupt severe deterioration over only several days is less typical
Recent orlistat exposure is not a recognized usual cause

data.diagnosis: Superior mesenteric venous thrombosis with mesenteric inflammation or early bowel ischemia
data.description: Thrombosis of the superior mesenteric vein can cause impaired venous drainage of bowel and mesentery, producing abdominal pain, mesenteric edema, inflammatory marker elevation, and potentially bowel ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Mesenteric inflammatory or vascular abnormality on CT
Obesity as a thrombotic risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal laboratory tests without reported lactate elevation or metabolic acidosis
No reported vomiting, diarrhea, gastrointestinal bleeding, or marked bowel distension
Pain is not described as disproportionate to examination

data.diagnosis: Epiploic appendagitis or focal omental infarction
data.description: Infarction or torsion of an epiploic appendage, or infarction of focal omentum, produces localized sterile inflammation and acute abdominal pain with fat stranding on CT. Omental infarction is more common in people with obesity.
symptoms_in_common: CT evidence of focal inflammatory fat change
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly epigastric pain is less typical for epiploic appendagitis
Nausea and belching are less common
Progressively worsening inflammatory markers may be more marked than usual

data.diagnosis: Acute gastritis or peptic ulcer disease, potentially medication-associated
data.description: Gastritis or peptic ulcer disease causes epigastric pain and dyspeptic symptoms. Although orlistat more often causes lower gastrointestinal adverse effects, a temporal medication association may initially raise concern for drug-related gastrointestinal symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Temporal relationship to starting a new medication
symptoms_not_in_common: Left iliac fossa tenderness
Low-grade fever
Neutrophilia
Worsening CRP
Persistence despite high-dose proton pump inhibitor treatment
Mesenteric inflammatory findings on CT
No reported gastrointestinal bleeding or anemia

data.description: A 12-year-old female presented to the Emergency Department with a 48-hour history of abdominal pain localised in the hypogastrium, which had progressively worsened in the last few hours. The patient mentioned previous episodes of less intense abdominal pain. Considering the clinical suspicion of acute appendicitis, an abdominal ultrasound was requested.

Accumulation of menstrual blood within the vagina and uterus caused by congenital obstruction at the hymen. Ultrasound commonly shows a large midline pelvic cystic mass with homogeneous low-level internal echoes.
symptoms_in_common: 12-year-old female at the typical age for presentation after menarche
Previous recurrent episodes of less intense abdominal pain
Large fluid-filled pelvic structure with internal echoes on ultrasound, compatible with retained blood
symptoms_not_in_common: No menstrual history, primary amenorrhea, cyclic pain pattern, urinary retention, or external genital examination findings were provided

data.diagnosis: Hematocolpos due to a transverse vaginal septum
data.description: A congenital transverse partition within the vagina can obstruct menstrual outflow, causing retained blood in the vagina, sometimes with extension into the uterus (hematometrocolpos).
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain that have worsened
Pelvic ultrasound appearance of a distended fluid-containing structure with internal echoes
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of absent menses, cyclic monthly symptoms, vaginal bulge, or difficulty voiding was reported

data.diagnosis: Obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal anomaly (OHVIRA syndrome)
data.description: A Müllerian duct anomaly, usually involving uterus didelphys with an obstructed hemivagina, that leads to hematocolpos or hematometra after menarche and may be associated with absence of a kidney on the same side.
symptoms_in_common: Young adolescent female with recurrent pelvic pain
Acute worsening of lower abdominal pain from retained menstrual blood
Pelvic cystic lesion with low-level internal echoes that may represent hematocolpos
symptoms_not_in_common: No duplicated uterus, unilateral pelvic collection, renal anomaly, menstrual history, or cyclic vaginal bleeding pattern was described

data.description: A functional ovarian cyst with internal bleeding that can produce acute or subacute pelvic pain and a complex cystic adnexal mass with internal echoes on ultrasound.
symptoms_in_common: History of prior less intense abdominal pain
Cystic pelvic lesion with internal echoes on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain is described as midline hypogastric rather than clearly unilateral
The ultrasound appearance appears more consistent with a large midline distended genital-tract structure than a typical adnexal cyst
No menstrual-cycle association, vaginal bleeding, or adnexal origin was provided

data.description: Inflammation of the appendix, classically causing progressively worsening abdominal pain that often migrates to the right lower quadrant and may be associated with fever, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening abdominal pain over 48 hours
Emergency presentation with clinical concern for appendicitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain is localized to the hypogastrium rather than the right lower quadrant
Previous recurrent episodes of similar pain are less typical of uncomplicated acute appendicitis
No fever, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, or right lower quadrant tenderness was reported
Ultrasound demonstrates a large pelvic fluid-containing structure rather than a described enlarged noncompressible appendix

data.description: 8-year-old Korean boy with severe global developmental delay and multiple exostoses. Developmental delay was noted at 3 months due to poor eye contact and head control. He had hypotonia, ptosis, nystagmus, and microcephaly. At age 6 years, he had marked growth retardation (height 96 cm, weight 15.7 kg, head circumference 45 cm, all <3rd percentile), sparse eyebrows, prominent nasal bridge, hypoplastic nare, down-turned mouth, and high-arched palate; he could not sit or walk independently. At age 5 years, testing showed severe intellectual disability. Multiple exostoses first appeared at age 6 years as protrusions of the right wrist and knee.

A contiguous-gene deletion syndrome involving 11p11.2, commonly including EXT2, ALX4, and PHF21A. It causes multiple osteochondromas/exostoses, enlarged parietal foramina, developmental delay/intellectual disability, hypotonia, craniofacial differences, and growth impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Severe global developmental delay and severe intellectual disability
Inability to sit or walk independently
Characteristic facial features including sparse eyebrows, prominent nasal bridge, hypoplastic nares, down-turned mouth, and high-arched palate
Parietal skull defects/enlarged parietal foramina on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are clearly atypical; nystagmus is less consistently reported than developmental delay, exostoses, and parietal foramina

data.description: An autosomal dominant skeletal disorder, usually caused by EXT1 or EXT2 variants, characterized by multiple cartilage-capped bony outgrowths near growth plates that develop during childhood.
symptoms_in_common: Childhood onset of bony protrusions around the wrist and knee
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe global developmental delay
Severe intellectual disability
Early hypotonia
Microcephaly
Ptosis and nystagmus
Characteristic craniofacial appearance
Enlarged parietal foramina/skull defects
Failure to sit or walk independently due to neurodevelopmental impairment

data.description: A contiguous-gene deletion disorder involving 8q24, typically including TRPS1 and EXT1. It is associated with craniofacial differences, sparse hair, short stature, cone-shaped epiphyses, and multiple exostoses.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent nasal bridge and distinctive facial appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound global developmental delay with inability to sit or walk independently
Severe intellectual disability is less typical
Microcephaly
Hypotonia from early infancy
Ptosis and nystagmus
Enlarged parietal foramina/skull defects
Typical cone-shaped phalangeal epiphyses were not described

data.description: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variants in chromatin-remodeling complex genes, characterized by developmental delay, hypotonia, feeding/growth problems, microcephaly or postnatal growth failure, and coarse or distinctive facial features.
symptoms_in_common: Severe developmental delay and intellectual disability
Inability to achieve independent sitting or walking
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple exostoses/osteochondromas
Parietal skull defects/enlarged parietal foramina
Bony protrusions at the wrist and knee
Hypoplastic fifth fingernails or distal phalanges, a common Coffin-Siris feature, were not reported

data.description: A RUNX2-related skeletal dysplasia characterized by delayed closure of cranial sutures, persistent or enlarged fontanelles, clavicular hypoplasia, dental abnormalities, short stature, and other skeletal differences.
symptoms_in_common: Skull ossification defects that can resemble enlarged parietal foramina
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple exostoses/osteochondromas
Severe global developmental delay
Severe intellectual disability
Early hypotonia
Microcephaly
Ptosis and nystagmus
Characteristic neurodevelopmental impairment causing inability to sit or walk independently
Typical clavicular hypoplasia and delayed tooth eruption were not described

data.description: 15-year-old boy with congenital neutropenia due to an ELA2 mutation and refractory anemia with excess blasts 2, referred for bone marrow transplantation. He had chronic severe neutropenia since infancy, recurrent bacterial skin and lung infections, and frequent treatment with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor and antimicrobials. He presented with multiple nonpruritic skin ulcerations on the right abdomen, scalp, and left ankle, present for several weeks. On examination, he was receiving granulocyte colony-stimulating factor with normal absolute neutrophil, lymphocyte, and eosinophil counts; immunoglobulin G was markedly elevated, and immunoglobulin E was normal.

A severe, highly contagious form of scabies with a high mite burden, often occurring in immunocompromised patients. Mites and eggs are present in the stratum corneum and can cause crusted, erosive, or ulcerated lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Histology demonstrating a mite within the stratum corneum
Normal eosinophil count does not exclude scabies
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of itching, since ordinary scabies is usually intensely pruritic
No described classic burrows on the hands, wrists, genital region, or finger webs
Localized abdominal, scalp, and ankle ulcers rather than diffuse hyperkeratotic crusting

data.description: Ecthyma is a deeper form of impetigo, usually due to Streptococcus pyogenes or Staphylococcus aureus, producing punched-out crusted ulcers. It is more common in patients with poor host defenses.
symptoms_in_common: History of severe neutropenia and recurrent bacterial skin infections
symptoms_not_in_common: Mite identified in the stratum corneum on histology
No reported purulent drainage, honey-colored crust, fever, or systemic bacterial illness
Multiple lesions involving the scalp and trunk are less typical than lower-extremity-predominant ecthyma

data.description: Pyoderma gangrenosum is an inflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis that causes painful, rapidly progressive ulcerations with undermined violaceous borders and may be associated with hematologic disorders.
symptoms_in_common: Underlying hematologic disease with refractory anemia and excess blasts
Possible occurrence in the setting of immune dysregulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Mites in the stratum corneum strongly indicate an infectious infestation instead
Lesions were described as nonpruritic but not as painful or rapidly expanding
No described undermined violaceous borders or pathergy
Histology does not describe the dense sterile neutrophilic infiltrate typical of pyoderma gangrenosum

data.description: Invasive fungal infections, including fusariosis or disseminated candidiasis, can cause papules, nodules, necrotic ulcers, or eschar-like lesions in patients with prolonged severe neutropenia.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent infections and substantial immunologic vulnerability
Potential for involvement of multiple noncontiguous skin sites
symptoms_not_in_common: Neutrophil count was normal at presentation while receiving granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
No fever, systemic illness, pulmonary deterioration, or fungemia is described
No fungal organisms, hyphae, or yeast forms are described on histology
A mite is visualized in the stratum corneum

data.diagnosis: Cutaneous involvement by myelodysplastic syndrome or leukemia cutis
data.description: Leukemia cutis refers to infiltration of the skin by malignant hematopoietic cells and may occur with myelodysplastic syndromes transforming toward acute myeloid leukemia. Lesions are typically papules, nodules, or plaques and only rarely ulcerate.
symptoms_in_common: Referral for bone marrow transplantation because of high-risk hematologic disease
Multiple skin lesions at separate sites
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are ulcerative and crusted rather than typical firm papules, nodules, or plaques
Histology shows epidermal ulceration, inflammation, and a mite rather than dermal infiltration by blasts
No reported progression to acute leukemia or peripheral blast-related findings

data.description: 16-year-old male with 4 weeks of weakness, malaise, anorexia, nausea, fever, and vomiting. No rash, joint pain, oral ulcers, or native/herbal medication use. Exam showed pallor, bilateral pitting pedal edema, and hypertension (160/90 mmHg); otherwise unremarkable. Labs: anemia (Hb 90 g/L), normal leukocytes and platelets, hematuria with RBC casts, proteinuria (3+ dipstick; 2.4 g/24 h), and rapidly worsening renal function (urea 130 mg/dL, creatinine 3 mg/dL rising to 10 mg/dL in 7 days). ANA and ANCA were negative; HBsAg, anti-HCV, and HIV were negative; complements were normal. Ultrasound showed normal-sized kidneys, and chest/abdomen CT and fundus exam were normal.
A severe glomerular inflammatory syndrome characterized by extensive crescent formation on kidney biopsy and rapid loss of renal function over days to weeks.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly rising creatinine from 3 mg/dL to 10 mg/dL within 7 days
Hematuria with red blood cell casts
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not always present in primary RPGN
No pulmonary hemorrhage or respiratory symptoms

data.description: A necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis with little or no immune-complex deposition; it is often associated with ANCA but can occur despite negative ANCA testing.
symptoms_in_common: Active urinary sediment with hematuria and red blood cell casts
Constitutional symptoms including fever, malaise, anorexia, and weakness
Negative ANA and normal complement levels
Negative ANCA does not exclude ANCA-negative pauci-immune disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No upper-airway, lung, skin, nerve, or joint manifestations of systemic vasculitis
No pulmonary hemorrhage
No ANCA positivity

data.description: An autoimmune disease in which antibodies target the glomerular basement membrane, causing severe crescentic glomerulonephritis; some patients also develop pulmonary hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: Hematuria with red blood cell casts
symptoms_not_in_common: No cough, hemoptysis, dyspnea, or pulmonary infiltrates
No reported anti-GBM antibody result
Fever and systemic constitutional symptoms are less characteristic

data.description: An immune-complex glomerulonephritis caused by mesangial IgA deposition; severe cases may develop crescents and rapidly progressive renal failure.
symptoms_in_common: Possible crescentic glomerulonephritis with rapid renal decline
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported preceding upper respiratory or gastrointestinal infection
Very rapid severe renal failure is uncommon in typical IgA nephropathy
Fever, prominent malaise, nausea, and vomiting are not typical initial IgA nephropathy features

data.description: An immune-complex glomerulonephritis that usually follows an infection, commonly streptococcal skin or throat infection, and can rarely progress to crescentic renal failure.
symptoms_in_common: Hematuria with red blood cell casts
Can rarely show crescents in severe disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented recent throat, skin, or other infection
Normal complement levels, whereas low C3 is typical
Rapid progression to severe renal failure is less typical
No reported evidence of streptococcal infection

data.description: A 44-year-old man was hospitalized because of jaundice. Physical examination revealed normal findings except jaundice, and his past medical history was unremarkable. Complete blood count showed hemoglobin of 15 g/dL, white blood cell count of 8,200/μL with differential of 79% segmented neutrophils, 15% lymphocytes, 5% monocytes, and 1% eosinophils, and platelet count of 248,000/μL. Liver function test showed elevation of total bilirubin (15.3 mg/dL), direct bilirubin (9.4 mg/dL), and alkaline phosphatase (298 IU/L). Immunohistochemical stains showed tumor cells positive for leukocyte common antigen (CD 45) and negative for CD 3,4,5,8,10,21,23,56 and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase. Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy showed neither significant abnormalities nor evidence of myelodysplasia or leukemic infiltration.

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal B-cell lymphoma of the extrahepatic bile duct
data.description: A rare non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising in or infiltrating the bile duct, producing obstructive jaundice. Lymphoma cells are typically CD45-positive and lack T-cell markers.
symptoms_in_common: Marked elevation of total and direct bilirubin
Elevated alkaline phosphatase indicating cholestatic obstruction
Imaging evidence of biliary obstruction or hilar bile-duct involvement
Tumor cells positive for leukocyte common antigen (CD45)
Absence of bone marrow infiltration can occur in localized primary biliary lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No peripheral lymphadenopathy was reported
No fever, night sweats, weight loss, or other B symptoms were reported
No hepatosplenomegaly was described

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving the biliary tract
data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that may rarely involve the hepatic hilum or extrahepatic bile ducts and mimic cholangiocarcinoma with obstructive jaundice.
symptoms_in_common: High direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
Negative T-cell markers including CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD8
Normal blood counts and uninvolved bone marrow may be present in localized extranodal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats
No reported bulky lymph-node enlargement
No cytopenias or marrow involvement

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the bile ducts, especially at the hepatic hilum, that commonly causes progressive obstructive jaundice and biliary dilatation.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings suggestive of obstruction near the hepatic hilum or bile ducts
Otherwise relatively normal physical examination can occur early
symptoms_not_in_common: Tumor cells positive for CD45 are not typical of cholangiocarcinoma
Negative epithelial-marker information and hematolymphoid immunophenotype favor lymphoma rather than carcinoma
Histology showing dense lymphoid-cell infiltration is not typical of a primary epithelial bile-duct cancer
Age 44 is younger than the usual age at presentation

data.diagnosis: Myeloid sarcoma involving the biliary tract
data.description: Myeloid sarcoma is an extramedullary mass of immature myeloid cells that can rarely involve the liver, gallbladder, or bile duct and may occur without detectable acute myeloid leukemia in bone marrow.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
Normal peripheral blood counts can occur in isolated myeloid sarcoma
Bone marrow can be negative in isolated extramedullary disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No myeloblasts or leukemic infiltration were found in bone marrow
No anemia, thrombocytopenia, or leukocytosis
No reported myeloid-marker positivity such as myeloperoxidase, CD33, CD34, CD117, or lysozyme
The reported immunophenotype does not specifically support myeloid lineage

data.description: An immune-mediated fibroinflammatory disorder causing bile-duct wall thickening and strictures, often associated with autoimmune pancreatitis and elevated serum IgG4.
symptoms_in_common: Biliary narrowing or hilar obstruction on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: A CD45-positive tumor-cell population is not typical
No elevated serum IgG4 was reported
No autoimmune pancreatitis or pancreatic enlargement was described
Histology described as malignant-appearing hematolymphoid cells would not be typical
No eosinophilia or other allergic/inflammatory features were present
